summary: The fixed full-academic-year charge in dollars for full-time undergraduate students who reside in the institution’s locality, covering tuition, required fees, room, and board and sometimes books and supplies.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living in institution-controlled on-campus housing who received any Title IV grant, work-study, or loan aid during the full aid year. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report a fall cohort, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour/occupational calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Aggregate dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state/local, and institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving Title IV aid whose financial-aid income is $30,001–$48,000; it is not an average or percentage. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students with aid awarded throughout the full aid year, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or clock-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Counts awards or degrees conferred during the reporting period to women identified as Asian, Native Hawaiian, or Other Pacific Islander, using a derived combination of the newer Asian and Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander categories and the former Asian/Pacific Islander category.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, receiving Title IV federal student aid during the full aid year, and reporting family income of $110,001 or more; applicable to public institutions with standard term-based calendar systems that report aid data for a fall cohort.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $0–$30,000 income group who received any Title IV federal student aid and any grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or the institution; private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard term calendars report fall-enrolled students receiving aid during the full aid year, while applicable private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars report students enrolled during the 12-month period receiving aid during the full aid year.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $48,001–$75,000 income range who received any Title IV federal aid, including grants, work-study, or loans. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students, and to public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.
Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the fall cohort whose residence or tuition-rate status is unknown.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received federal student loans, including Title IV subsidized and unsubsidized loans but excluding PLUS and other loans made directly to parents.
A derived headcount of men classified as Asian, Native Hawaiian, or Other Pacific Islander, using the combined current and legacy Asian/Pacific Islander race definitions.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living in institution-owned or controlled on-campus housing, paying the in-state or in-district tuition rate, and receiving federal, state, local, or institutional grant or scholarship aid; students receiving only other grant aid are excluded. Populated only for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year.

Typical full-academic-year in-state tuition and required fees, in dollars, for a full-time student enrolled in a law doctor's professional practice program (L.L.B. or J.D.) and meeting the institution's or state's residency requirements.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan during the full aid year; applicable to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions on standard term calendars reporting a fall cohort, and to public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific/contact-hour calendars reporting a 12-month enrollment period.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received federal loans, including Title IV subsidized and unsubsidized loans but excluding parent PLUS and other loans made directly to parents.

Average net price is the average total cost of attendance minus federal, state/local, and institutional grant or scholarship aid, in dollars, for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying the in-state or in-district rate who received Title IV federal aid, grouped by family income over $110,000. It is applicable to public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort across the full aid year.

Indicates whether each 6-digit CIP program offering a 2-year but less than 4-year certificate can be completed entirely via distance education (1 = offered, 0 = not offered), based on programs reported in the 12-month completions data. For 2-digit CIP categories and the institutional grand total, it reports the number of such programs offered; it is populated when the institution reports a nonnegative total for these certificates.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $48,001–$75,000 income range who received any Title IV federal aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or their institution; private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard calendar systems report fall enrollees receiving aid during the full aid year, while eligible private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars report students enrolled during the 12-month period receiving aid during that aid year.
Typical annual in-state tuition and required fees, in dollars, for a full-time Pharmacy (Pharm.D.) first-professional student who meets the institution’s residency requirements.

Count of students in the total revised cohort who are excluded from the 150%-of-normal-time outcome calculation because they left without graduating or transferring due to death or permanent disability, military service, qualifying federal foreign-aid service, or an official church mission; students who returned before the 150% status point may still be included.

Total dollar amount of federal, state, local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $30,001–$48,000 income range who received Title IV aid and paid in-state or in-district tuition. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort over the full aid year.

Number of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid during the full aid year; the income category is based on income used to determine the student’s Expected Family Contribution. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars reporting aid for a fall cohort.

Number of students in the specified cohort (total, bachelor's, or other-than-bachelor's) who completed a bachelor's or equivalent degree within 150% of the institution's normal completion time; reported for four-year institutions only.

Average base salary in dollars for full-time, non-medical instructional staff on 10-month contracts, including staff whose duties are instruction alone or combined with research and/or public service; excludes supplements, overloads, bonuses, and additional administrative or other stipends.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $0–$30,000 income category who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid during the full aid year; reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard-term calendars for fall cohorts, and by public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour calendars for students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Typical in-state required fees charged for a full-time first-professional podiatry student for the full academic year. In-state applies to students meeting the state or institution’s residency requirements, and required fees are mandatory charges beyond tuition.

The ratio of fall FTE students to FTE instructional staff, excluding graduate or professional students and instructional staff teaching in stand-alone graduate or professional programs; FTE counts treat each part-time student or staff member as one-third of a full-time equivalent, and medical school employees are excluded.

Total dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from families with income below $30,000 who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received any Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions using standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.
Identifies the institution’s BEA geographic region, using codes for U.S. service schools, the eight BEA regions covering the 50 states and District of Columbia, outlying areas, or not available.

Headcount of men who are nonresident aliens—temporary visa holders without permanent-resident status; resident aliens and other noncitizens with legal immigrant status are reported in the applicable racial/ethnic categories instead.

Count of male applicants who are first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including early-decision, early-action, and prior-summer entrants; applicants may enroll full or part time. Reported for institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.
Percentage of all undergraduates who were full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking students in the fall cohort.
Percentage of all undergraduate students represented by the unduplicated full-year cohort of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates.

Total amount of grant and scholarship aid, in dollars, received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the institution-defined income band of $0–$30,000 who received Title IV federal student aid; the income measure is the amount used to determine Expected Family Contribution. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific/contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus and not with family who received grant or scholarship aid from federal, state, local, or institutional sources; students receiving only other grant aid are excluded. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition whose income used to determine Expected Family Contribution falls in this income band and who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid during the full aid year; applicable only to public institutions with standard term calendars reporting aid for students enrolled in the fall.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus with family who pay in-state or in-district tuition and receive federal, state, local, or institutional grant or scholarship aid; students receiving only other grant aid are excluded. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students' aid for the full aid year.

Average dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, in the specified income band used to determine Expected Family Contribution, who received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard academic calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received institutional grants, scholarships, or fellowships designated and funded by the institution or its departments.
Headcount of men enrolled for credit during the 12-month period, using the combined Asian and Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander race/ethnicity category.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $48,001–$75,000 income range who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report aid for fall enrollees over the full aid year.

Categorical indicator assigning Title IV-participating institutions to the automatic comparison group used in the IPEDS Data Feedback Report when an institution did not provide its own group. Groups are based on institutional control, degree-granting status, institution category or Carnegie classification, program area for many nondegree-granting institutions, enrollment size, and special classifications such as tribal colleges, service institutions, and institutions in other jurisdictions; small groups may be combined.

Average dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $30,001–$48,000 income level who received Title IV federal student aid. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students with aid received during the full aid year, and to public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid year.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the fall cohort.

Indicator of whether all Doctor's degree-professional practice programs within a 6-digit CIP code can be completed entirely through distance education; 1 means yes and 0 means no. For 2-digit CIP and institution-wide summary records, values instead indicate whether any programs are offered (1) or none are offered (0).

Average base salary in dollars for full-time, non-medical instructional staff who are men and work under 10-month contracts. Instructional staff perform instruction only or instruction combined with research and/or public service; supplements, overloads, bonuses, and stipends are excluded.

Headcount of men and women enrolled for credit during the 12-month reporting period who are nonresident aliens—non-U.S. citizens or nationals in the country temporarily on a visa; resident aliens and other permanent or legal immigrants are counted in the appropriate racial/ethnic categories instead.

Average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying the in-state or in-district rate, receiving Title IV federal aid, and reporting family income of $30,001–$48,000; it is the total cost of attendance less average federal, state/local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid. Applicable to public institutions with standard-term calendar systems that report aid for a fall cohort over the full aid year.
Headcount of male staff classified as nonresident aliens—non-U.S. citizens or nationals in the country temporarily on a visa without the right to remain indefinitely.

A headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $30,001–$48,000 income range who received any Title IV federal aid and were awarded grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or the institution; private or other-source grants are excluded. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard-term calendars that report fall-enrolled students receiving aid during the full aid year, and for applicable private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

A categorical classification of institutions by student-population size and residential character, using FTE enrollment (full-time plus one-third part-time); for four-year institutions, residential character reflects the share of degree-seeking undergraduates attending full-time and living in institutionally owned, operated, or affiliated housing. Exclusively graduate institutions are excluded, and two-year institutions are classified by FTE size only.

Headcount of full-time, first-time undergraduate students enrolled in degree- or certificate-seeking programs who received any financial aid, including grants, loans, scholarships, waivers, benefits, and other non-family assistance.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students awarded federal grant aid other than Pell Grants, including programs such as SEOG and other federal student aid grants.

Headcount of students enrolled for credit during the 12-month period who took only distance education courses; courses may use online, broadcast, or other qualifying technologies, and occasional campus visits for orientation, testing, or support do not disqualify them.

A categorical classification of an institution’s graduate instructional profile, based on the graduate degrees it awarded, the breadth of fields represented, and the concentration of degrees across broad disciplines. It applies to institutions awarding at least one graduate-level degree and distinguishes postbaccalaureate from doctoral institutions, including medical/veterinary distinctions for certain doctoral categories.

Average dollars of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from families with income of $110,001 or more who received Title IV federal student aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall enrollment with aid awarded during the full aid year, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour/occupational calendars that report a 12-month enrollment period with aid awarded during the full aid year.

Identifies the U.S. congressional district containing the institution, using a FIPS state code plus a district code; at-large districts use 00, areas with nonvoting delegates use 98, and areas without congressional representation use -2.

Headcount of full-time, non-medical instructional staff on 11-month contracts, as of November 1. Instructional staff work in instruction alone or in instruction combined with research and/or public service; medical-school staff are excluded, except staff in affiliated health or allied-health schools and departments.

Unduplicated headcount of full-time, first-time undergraduate students enrolled for credit and seeking a degree or certificate during the full-year cohort reporting period; each student is counted once regardless of when they enrolled.

Categorical classification of institutions by full-time-equivalent enrollment size and residential character, using fall enrollment and, for four-year institutions, the share of degree-seeking undergraduates living in institutionally owned, operated, or affiliated housing. It applies to associate’s degree-granting two-year and bachelor’s degree-granting four-year institutions; exclusively graduate/professional institutions are not classified, and four-year categories also distinguish primarily nonresidential, residential, and highly residential institutions.

Dollar amount of other federal student aid, excluding required matching portions, applied as a discount or allowance against auxiliary enterprise revenues; combined with net auxiliary sales and services, it represents gross auxiliary enterprise revenue.
Total dollars of non-Pell federal grant aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including grants such as SEOG and other federal student aid programs.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living on campus, charged the in-state or in-district tuition rate, and receiving any Title IV federal student aid during the full aid year. Populated for public institutions with standard academic calendars that report aid for a fall-enrolled cohort.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate in the specified income range who received Title IV aid and paid in-state or in-district tuition. Populated for public institutions with standard term-based calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.

Headcount of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted SAT scores, including students entering in the prior summer; reported for institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

Headcount of women in the cohort who are U.S. nonresidents—noncitizens or nationals present temporarily on a visa without indefinite-residency rights; permanent residents and other eligible noncitizens are classified in the applicable racial/ethnic categories instead.

Total dollar amount of Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits received by graduate-student recipients, including eligible spouses or dependents, as reported to the institution. Excludes Yellow Ribbon matching institutional aid and benefits not awarded or certified through the institution.

Derived fall headcount of men and women enrolled for credit, combining Asian and Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander race/ethnicity categories; enrollment is measured at the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15.

Annual in-state required fees in dollars for a full-time first-professional optometry student. In-state means the student meets the institution’s or state’s residency requirements; required fees are mandatory charges beyond tuition.
Headcount of male full-time, non-medical instructional staff on 12-month contracts, as of November 1; instructional staff perform instruction alone or combined with research and/or public service.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students awarded loans requiring repayment, including federal, institutional, and private student loans but excluding loans made directly to parents.

Average dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid awarded per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate in the $75,001–$110,000 income group who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report on a fall cohort and track aid awarded throughout the full aid year.

Total dollar amount of federal, state, local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $75,001–$110,000 income range who received Title IV aid and paid in-state or in-district tuition. Populated for public institutions using standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.

Total dollars of federal, state/local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $110,001-or-more income group who received Title IV federal student aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic-term calendars and reporting fall-enrolled students for the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled over the 12-month aid period.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received student loans, including federal, institutional, and private loans to students but excluding parent loans.

Headcount of women employed full time as instructional faculty whose major assignment is instruction (including instruction combined with research or public service) but who do not have faculty status; graduate, instructional, and research assistants are excluded.

Typical in-state tuition and required fees in dollars for a full-time first-professional Optometry (O.D.) student for the full academic year. It applies to students meeting the institution's or state's residency requirements.

Total dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant or scholarship aid awarded during the full aid year to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received such aid; other grant-aid sources are excluded. It is reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars for fall-enrolled students, and by public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, clock-hour, or primarily occupational calendars for students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $0–$30,000 income group who received Title IV aid. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students’ aid for the full aid year, and to public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during a 12-month period and aid received throughout that period.

Categorizes postsecondary employees by IPEDS/SOC occupation and, for faculty, by tenure status. Faculty are staff whose principal activity is instruction, research, or public service (excluding graduate, instruction, and research assistants); tenure-status categories include tenure-track, not-on-tenure-track, multi-year contract, annual contract, and less-than-annual contract.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the financial-aid cohort. For institutions using standard academic terms, it reflects enrollment at the official fall reporting date; for program reporters without standard terms, it is an unduplicated count of students enrolled during the full 12-month reporting period.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $30,001–$48,000 income range who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received any Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort over the full aid year.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students with income from $0 to $30,000 who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid during the full aid year. It applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students, and to public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received institution-funded scholarships or fellowships, including awards targeted by residency, major, athletics, or other criteria.

Categorical Carnegie classification of an institution’s undergraduate instructional program, based on whether it awards associate’s and/or bachelor’s degrees, the share of bachelor’s majors in arts and sciences versus professional fields, and the extent of graduate-degree overlap with undergraduate fields. Categories distinguish associate’s institutions, associate’s-dominant institutions, and bachelor’s institutions ranging from arts-and-sciences-focused to professions-focused, each further classified as having no, some, or high graduate coexistence.

Categorical identifier for the NCES-created Data Feedback Report comparison group, assigned to institutions participating in Title IV federal financial aid programs. Groups reflect institutional control, degree-granting status, institution category, Carnegie classification, program mix, enrollment size, and special populations such as tribal colleges, U.S. service institutions, and institutions in other jurisdictions; distance-learning-only institutions are classified by Carnegie group rather than placed in a single universal group.

Binary indicator of whether all programs within a 6-digit CIP code offering certificates of 2 years but less than 4 years can be completed entirely through distance education, based on programs reported in the 12-month completions period; zero includes programs offered with no awards. For 2-digit CIP and institution-total records, the value instead summarizes whether any such programs are offered (1 = high/total offered, 0 = none).

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received any Title IV federal student aid and were awarded grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state or local government, or the institution; awards from private or other sources, loans, and Federal Work-Study alone are excluded. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students with aid during the full aid year, and to public or private institutions using continuous or program-specific calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Percentage of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted ACT scores, including students who first enrolled in the preceding summer; reported for institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

The 75th-percentile ACT Math score among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted ACT scores, including students admitted in the prior summer. Reported for institutions without an open-admission policy when test scores are required for admission.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, whose aid-eligibility income is $110,001 or more and who received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars reporting on fall-enrolled students’ aid received during the full aid year.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who live off campus, not with family, and received Title IV federal aid during the full aid year; populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars reporting aid for a fall cohort.

Represents fringe-benefit coverage and expenditures standardized to a 9-month contract, combining 9/10-month and 11/12-month contracts. For benefits based on salary, 11/12-month expenditures are converted to 9-month equivalents; for other benefits they are summed directly, and average expenditure is calculated per covered person.

Headcount of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted ACT scores, including students who first enrolled in the preceding summer; reported for institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

Average dollar amount of federal student loans awarded per non-degree/non-certificate-seeking undergraduate student, including Title IV loans made directly to the student but excluding PLUS and other loans not made directly to the student; this population includes credit-enrolled students not seeking a degree or credential, including eligible high school students.
Headcount of men in the cohort who are Asian, Native Hawaiian, or Other Pacific Islander, using a combined race/ethnicity category.
Percentage of all undergraduates represented by the fall cohort of full-time, first-time undergraduate degree- or certificate-seeking students.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students from households with income of $0–$30,000 who received any Title IV federal aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or institution; private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions report this for fall-enrolled students receiving aid during the full aid year, while qualifying private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars report students enrolled during the 12-month period. Grants or scholarships from private or other sources alone, loans, and Federal Work Study do not qualify.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $110,001-or-more income group who paid in-state or in-district tuition, received any Title IV aid, and received grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or the institution. Applicable only to public institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students' aid over the full aid year; excludes private-source aid, loans, and Federal Work-Study when not accompanied by qualifying grant or scholarship aid.

Number of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received Title IV federal grant aid and had income of $110,001 or more. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall-enrolled cohort over the full aid year.

Indicates whether the institution has a tenure system, based on reporting at least one tenured or non-tenured, tenure-track employee; otherwise it is classified as having no tenure system. Used to distinguish employees who are non-tenured and not on a tenure track from employees at institutions without a tenure system.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV federal aid and any grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or the institution; private-source grants, loans, and Federal Work-Study alone are excluded. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendar systems that report fall-enrolled students' aid received during the full aid year, and broken out by income level used to determine Expected Family Contribution.

Published dollar amount of required fees charged to full-time, first-time undergraduate students who do not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements, for the full academic year; it is an out-of-state fee component rather than total tuition and cost of attendance.
Unduplicated headcount of full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the full-year cohort who pay in-state tuition rates.

Indicates whether the institution offered a Doctor’s degree–research/scholarship program in each 6-digit CIP category during the 12-month completions period, including programs with no awards: 1 means offered and 0 means not offered. For 2-digit CIP categories and the institution grand total, the value is a count of offered programs rather than a yes/no indicator.
Annual out-of-state required fees, in dollars, for a full-time first-professional optometry student. Required fees are mandatory charges beyond tuition that apply to nearly all students.

Estimated dollar amount of other expenses (such as transportation, laundry, entertainment, and furnishings) for full-time, first-time undergraduate students living off campus with family during the full academic year; excludes tuition and fees, books and supplies, and room and board.

Categorical classification of an institution’s enrollment profile based on the mix of undergraduate and graduate students, using full-time-equivalent enrollment (full-time headcount plus one-third of part-time headcount). Categories distinguish exclusively undergraduate two-year or four-year institutions, institutions with undergraduates and graduate students by the graduate FTE share (under 10%, 10–24%, 25–49%, or at least 50%), and exclusively graduate institutions.
Typical annual tuition and required fees, in dollars, charged to full-time first-professional Medicine (M.D.) students who meet the institution’s in-state residency requirements.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at all income levels who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid during the full aid year. It applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report a fall cohort, and to public or private institutions using continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduates whose financial-aid income used for EFC determination was $0–$30,000 and who received Title IV federal aid during the full aid year. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars for fall enrollees, and by public or private institutions with continuous, program-based, or contact-hour calendars for students enrolled during the 12-month reporting period.

Measures the total dollar amount of federal, state/local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received Title IV federal student aid, across all income levels. Populated only for public institutions using standard term calendars that report aid for a fall-enrolled cohort over the full aid year.

Typical dollar amount of required fees charged for the full academic year to full-time in-state Osteopathic Medicine doctor's professional practice students; fees are mandatory charges separate from tuition.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate in the specified income bracket who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting a fall cohort and aid awarded throughout the full aid year; income is the amount used to determine the student’s Expected Family Contribution.

Average dollar amount of Title IV subsidized and unsubsidized federal student loans awarded per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate student; excludes PLUS and other loans made directly to parents.

Average net price in dollars after federal, state, local, and institutional grants and scholarships for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates with income of $30,001–$48,000 who received Title IV aid. The column applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting a fall cohort and full aid year, and to public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or primarily clock-hour calendars reporting a 12-month aid period; for the latter, the amount reflects the cost and aid for the largest program over its program length.

Total dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $48,001–$75,000 income group who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report financial aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year; income is based on the adjusted gross income used to determine Expected Family Contribution.

Average dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid awarded per full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate in the $0–$30,000 income group who received Title IV aid; it excludes loans and work-study from the amount being averaged. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard-term calendars that report fall enrollment with aid awarded during the full aid year, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, clock-hour, or primarily occupational calendars that report enrollment over the full 12-month aid period.

SAT Writing score at the 25th percentile for first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted SAT scores. Reported for institutions without an open-admission policy when test scores are required for admission.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $110,001-or-more income group who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions using standard-term calendars that report fall-enrolled students' aid for the full aid year.

Indicates whether the institution reports student charges for a full academic year or by program, and whether graduation, retention, and financial-aid data use a fall cohort or a full-year cohort. Institutions with standard academic terms generally use full-year charges and a fall cohort of full-time, first-time degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduates; institutions with nontraditional, continuous, or program-length calendars generally use program charges and a full-year cohort of full-time, first-time entrants tracked over the 12-month period.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $30,001–$48,000 income level who received Title IV federal grant aid during the full aid year. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard calendars that report a fall cohort, and for applicable private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during a 12-month period.

Average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from families with income over $110,000 who received Title IV federal aid; it is the average cost of attendance after grants and scholarships, for the full academic year or the reported program length. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or other nonstandard calendars reporting students and aid over the full 12-month aid period.
Count of full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received Pell grants.

Counts full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who enrolled in the fall and received Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid during the full aid year, whose EFC-determining income was $110,001 or more; applicable to public institutions on standard term calendars.

Average base salary, excluding supplements, overloads, bonuses, and additional administrative or other stipends, for full-time, non-medical instructional staff whose contracts cover 12 months. Instructional staff includes those in instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service; staff in medical-school components are excluded, while health or allied-health staff are excluded only when affiliated with a medical school.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received any Title IV federal aid and were awarded grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or the institution; students receiving only private/other grants, loans, or Federal Work-Study are excluded. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard calendars reporting fall-enrolled students’ aid for the full aid year, and to private institutions using clock-hour, primarily occupational credit-hour, continuous, or program-specific calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Total grant and scholarship dollars from federal, state or local governments and institutional sources received during the full aid year by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received such aid; other grant sources are excluded. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting on fall-enrolled students, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-differing, or primarily contact-hour/occupational calendars reporting on students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Headcount of students in the specified cohort (total, bachelor's, or other-than-bachelor's) at four-year institutions who received neither a Pell Grant nor a subsidized Stafford Loan and completed a bachelor's or equivalent degree within 150% of the program's normal completion time.

Number of Pell Grant recipients in the specified cohort who completed an associate degree, certificate, or other award within 150% of the institution’s normal completion time; for four-year institutions, this applies to non-bachelor’s awards, while for two-year or less-than-two-year institutions it applies to the cohort’s award. The cohort may be total, bachelor’s, or other-than-bachelor’s, as indicated by PSGRTYPE.

Indicates how work experience is used in admissions decisions for entering first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students at institutions without an open-admission policy: required for admission, considered if submitted but not required, or not considered even if submitted.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant or scholarship aid received during the full aid year by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received such aid; other grant sources are excluded. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant or scholarship aid awarded during the full aid year to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received such aid; other grant sources are excluded. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars using fall-enrolled students, and by public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars using students enrolled during the 12-month reporting period.

Estimated dollar amount for a full academic year of other expenses—such as laundry, transportation, entertainment, and furnishings—used in financial-aid calculations for full-time, first-time undergraduate students living off campus and not with family; it excludes tuition and fees, books and supplies, and room and board.

Total dollar amount of Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits awarded through the institution to all student recipients, including eligible spouses and dependents; it covers only benefits known to and certified through the institution, excludes benefits awarded elsewhere and Yellow Ribbon institutional aid.

Annual published required fees, in dollars, charged to full-time, first-time, first-year undergraduate students residing in the institution’s locality; this in-district rate may be lower than the institution’s in-state rate and covers the full academic year.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living in institution-controlled on-campus housing who received Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars with a fall cohort and full aid-year reporting, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-variable, or primarily clock-hour/occupational calendars with 12-month enrollment and full aid-year reporting.
Reports the total length of the institution’s fourth-largest program, measured in clock hours or credit hours.

Annual food and housing charges in dollars for a full-time, first-time undergraduate student living off campus and not with family, as used by the financial aid office for the full academic year; this differs from on-campus or living-with-family food and housing charges.

Categorical classification (codes 1–6) based on degree/certificate offerings and completions: degree-granting institutions are grouped as graduate-only, primarily baccalaureate-or-above, not primarily baccalaureate-or-above, or associate’s/certificates, while nondegree-granting institutions are grouped as above-baccalaureate or sub-baccalaureate. It is not applicable for inactive institutions and administrative units; non-Title IV institutions that did not respond to the relevant components are not reported.

A categorical classification of institutions by FTE enrollment size and residential character. It covers associate’s degree-granting institutions by size, and bachelor’s-or-higher institutions by degree-seeking student FTE size plus the share of degree-seeking undergraduates living on campus and attending full time; exclusively graduate/professional institutions receive a separate category, while institutions with no undergraduates are otherwise excluded.

Typical annual out-of-state required fees, in dollars, for full-time students enrolled in an optometry doctor's professional practice program; fees are mandatory charges beyond tuition for students who do not meet state or institutional residency requirements.
Annual out-of-state tuition and required fees in dollars for a full-time first-professional podiatry student who does not meet state or institutional residency requirements.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded per full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate paying in-state or in-district tuition and receiving Title IV aid, across all income levels. Populated for public institutions with standard calendar systems that report aid for a fall-enrolled cohort over the full aid year.

The median (50th percentile) ACT Composite score among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students whose institution requires admission test scores; applies to institutions without an open-admission policy and includes students who first enrolled in the prior summer.

Annual in-state tuition and required fees, in dollars, for a full-time student enrolled in a podiatry doctor's degree—professional practice program who meets the institution's or state's residency requirements.

The median SAT Math score among submitted scores for first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including those who first enrolled in the preceding summer; reported when test scores are required at institutions without an open-admission policy.
A 3-digit geographic code identifying the Combined Statistical Area associated with the institution's address. It is not applicable when the institution is not located in a CSA.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who were awarded Pell Grants.

ACT Writing score at or below which 25% of score-submitters fall, reported for first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students (including those who entered the prior summer); populated when the institution requires admission test scores and does not have an open-admission policy.
Headcount of men and women in the cohort who are classified as Asian, Native Hawaiian, or Other Pacific Islander, using combined current and historical race/ethnicity categories.
Annual dollar amount of required fees charged to full-time undergraduate students who do not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements.

Annual dollar amount of required fees charged to full-time, first-professional dentistry students who do not meet the applicable state or institutional residency requirements. Required fees are mandatory fixed charges beyond tuition.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received during the full aid year by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received such aid; other grant sources are excluded. It is reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars for fall-enrolled students, and by public or private institutions using continuous, program-differentiated, or primarily contact-hour calendars for students enrolled during the institution’s 12-month reporting period.

Total base-salary outlays in dollars for full-time male instructional staff on 11-month contracts, counted as of November 1; excludes medical-school staff and supplements, overloads, bonuses, and stipends for other responsibilities.

Total clock-hour instructional activity provided to undergraduate students enrolled in occupational programs over the 12-month reporting period, calculated as the clock hours completed by each student and summed across students; this is an activity measure, not a headcount.

Headcount of women classified as Asian, Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander, using a combined race/ethnicity definition that reconciles newer categories with the former Asian/Pacific Islander category.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received any financial aid, including grants, scholarships, loans to students, work-study, and other aid; parent PLUS loans are excluded.

Average base salary in dollars for full-time, non-medical instructional staff who are women and work under 9-month contracts, as of November 1. Instructional staff includes employees whose function is instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service; supplements, overloads, bonuses, and additional administrative stipends are excluded.

Average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from households with income over $110,000 who received Title IV federal aid, after subtracting average federal, state/local, and institutional grants and scholarships from cost of attendance. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students with aid over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report a 12-month aid period; for the latter, it may represent the cost for the institution’s largest program.

Identifies the U.S. congressional district where the institution is located, using a FIPS-based numeric code that combines the state code with the district code. At-large districts use district code 00, nonvoting-delegate jurisdictions use 98, and areas without congressional representation use -2.

Indicates whether a master's program is offered at the 6-digit CIP level, based on master's degree completions during the 12-month reporting period; summary records report the total number of programs offered within a 2-digit CIP category or institution-wide.

Reports the dollar amount of fixed, generally mandatory fees charged for a full-time Chiropractic (D.C. or D.C.M.) professional-practice student who meets the institution’s or state’s in-state residency requirements, for the full academic year.

Headcount of women who are full-time, non-medical instructional staff (instruction, or instruction combined with research and/or public service) working under a 9-month contract as of November 1; excludes staff in medical schools, associated hospitals, and unaffiliated health or allied-health departments.

Indicates whether the institution offers adult basic education or high school equivalency instruction, such as basic reading, writing, and arithmetic courses for students age 16 or older that are not part of a postsecondary degree, academic, occupational, or vocational program.

Average net price, in dollars, for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying the in-state or in-district rate, in the $75,001–$110,000 income group, who received Title IV federal aid; it is total cost of attendance minus average federal, state/local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid. Applicable to public institutions with standard calendar systems that report aid for fall-enrolled students awarded aid during the full aid year.

Headcount of male U.S. nonresident students enrolled for credit at four-year institutions on the official fall reporting date (or October 15); temporary visa holders are included, while permanent residents and other eligible noncitizens are reported in the appropriate racial/ethnic categories.

Total dollars of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state/local, and institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $0–$30,000 income level who received Title IV aid and paid in-state or in-district tuition. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting aid for a fall cohort received throughout the full aid year.

Total dollars of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at all income levels who received Title IV aid. It applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report a fall cohort with aid awarded throughout the full aid year, and to public or private institutions using clock-hour, continuous, or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during a 12-month period with aid awarded throughout the full aid year.

Total dollar amount of nonfederal loans awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including institutionally and privately sponsored loans but excluding loans made directly to parents.

Average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, in the $30,001–$48,000 income group, who received Title IV federal aid. It applies to public institutions with standard academic calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the full-year cohort whose home state or residence—and therefore applicable tuition rate—is unknown. The denominator is the unduplicated count of students in that cohort.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus with family, paying in-state or in-district tuition, and receiving grant or scholarship aid from federal, state, or local governments or the institution; students receiving only other grant aid are excluded. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students’ aid for the full aid year.
Classifies the institution as public, private not-for-profit, or private for-profit based on its ownership and primary source of funding.

The 25th-percentile SAT Math score among submitted scores for first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including students who began in the preceding summer. Populated when test scores are required for admission at institutions without an open-admission policy.

Dollar amount of institutional scholarships and fellowships, including athletic scholarships and institutional matching funds, applied as discounts or allowances against auxiliary-enterprise charges such as room and board.
Average tuition charged for the full academic year to full-time undergraduate students who reside in the institution's local district; amounts are in dollars.

Combined base-salary outlays in dollars for full-time women instructional staff as of November 1, excluding medical-school staff, supplements, overloads, bonuses, and additional administrative or other stipends.
Average dollar cost of books and supplies for a typical full-time, first-time undergraduate student over the full academic year or program, excluding unusual costs for minority specialty groups.
Average full academic-year tuition charged to full-time graduate students who do not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements, reported in dollars.

Average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from families with income over $110,000 who received Title IV federal aid, calculated as average cost of attendance minus average grant and scholarship aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall enrollment and full-year aid, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or other nonstandard calendars reporting a 12-month aid period; the amount covers the full academic year or the length of the institution’s largest program, as applicable.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving grant or scholarship aid from federal, state or local governments, or the institution, excluding students receiving only other grant sources; populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard-term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students' aid over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars reporting enrollment and aid over the 12-month aid period.

FIPS-based geographic identifier for the congressional district containing the institution, with the state’s two-digit FIPS code followed by a two-digit district code. District code 00 denotes a state with one at-large representative, 98 denotes territories or the District of Columbia with a nonvoting delegate, and -2 denotes areas with no congressional representation.
Count of students enrolled for credit during the 12-month reporting period who took no courses delivered exclusively through distance education.

Headcount of women who are nonresident aliens (temporary visa holders without indefinite right to remain) enrolled for credit at four-year institutions on the official fall reporting date or October 15.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received loans to students or grant/scholarship aid from the federal government, state or local government, or the institution. It excludes federal work-study, parent loans, and aid from private or other sources.

Headcount of undergraduate students receiving Department of Defense Tuition Assistance Program benefits, including eligible spouses or dependents when known to the institution; excludes benefits not awarded or certified through the institution.

Total dollar amount of nonfederal, institutionally or privately sponsored loans received by full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students; excludes loans made directly to parents.

Total dollars of federal, state, local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received Title IV aid and whose financial-aid income was $75,001–$110,000. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour/occupational calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Total base salary outlays in dollars for full-time women instructional staff, excluding medical staff and supplements, overloads, bonuses, and additional administrative stipends; salaries under contracts of other lengths are expressed as equivalent to a 9-month contract. Instructional staff perform instruction alone or combined with research and/or public service.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $110,001-or-more income group who received Title IV aid and paid in-state or in-district tuition. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting aid for a fall cohort across the full aid year.

Total dollars of federal, state/local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $48,001–$75,000 income group who received Title IV aid. It applies to private nonprofit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students, and to public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the full 12-month aid year.

Headcount of male, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students enrolled part time in the most recent fall period, including students who began in the preceding summer and those admitted through early decision or early action. Reported for institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $0–$30,000 income category who received Title IV federal grant aid. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students for the full aid year, and to qualifying private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from families with income of $110,001 or more who received Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report a fall cohort over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report a 12-month cohort over the full aid year.

Count of Pell Grant cohort students who left the institution before 150% of normal time without graduating or transferring and were excluded because of documented death or permanent disability, military service, qualifying federal foreign-aid service, or an official church mission.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received Title IV aid, grouped by the income used to determine their Expected Family Contribution. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report financial aid for a fall cohort over the full aid year.

Average dollar amount of federal grants and educational assistance received per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate student, including Pell, SEOG, and other federally sponsored aid.

Total institutional expenses in dollars for academic support, student services, and institutional support, including libraries and academic administration, student-facing services such as admissions and financial aid administration, and general administrative and operational support.

Percentage of non-degree/non-certificate-seeking undergraduate students awarded federal loans made directly to the student, including Title IV student loans and specified health-profession loans but excluding PLUS and other loans not made directly to the student.

Average annual base salary in dollars for full-time, non-medical instructional staff on 9-month contracts, measured as of November 1. Instructional staff perform instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service; supplements, overloads, bonuses, and stipends for other responsibilities are excluded.

Total dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, across all income levels, among those who received any Title IV federal student aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students' aid received throughout the full aid year.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living in institution-owned or controlled on-campus housing, paying in-state or in-district tuition, and receiving Title IV federal aid; populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort and the full aid year.

Count of students in the revised graduation-rate cohort after excluding those who died or became permanently disabled, entered military or qualifying federal foreign-aid service, or served an official church mission; this adjusted cohort is the denominator for graduation and transfer-out rates.

Average dollars of attendance cost remaining after federal, state, local, and institutional grant or scholarship aid, for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received such aid during the full aid year; other grant sources are excluded. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-differing, or primarily contact-hour/occupational calendars reporting students enrolled throughout the 12-month aid period; it reflects a full academic year for the former and the length of the largest program for the latter.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates awarded any Title IV federal aid (grants, work-study, or loans), across all income levels. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students for the full aid year, and for public or private institutions using clock-hour, primarily occupational, continuous, or program-varying calendars reporting students enrolled over the 12-month aid period.

Headcount of male U.S. nonresident high school students enrolled for college credit during the 12-month reporting period; these temporary visa holders are counted as part of unduplicated non-degree/non-certificate-seeking enrollment and are distinct from permanent residents, who are reported in racial/ethnic categories.

The 25th-percentile ACT English score among submitted ACT scores for first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including those who began in the preceding summer. It is reported only by institutions without an open-admission policy when test scores are required for admission.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid whose financial-aid income used to determine EFC falls in the $0–30,000 range. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report a fall cohort, and for public or private institutions with continuous or program-differing calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid year.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the specified income range who received any Title IV federal aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or institution; private-source grants, loans, and work-study alone are excluded. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard calendars that report fall-enrolled students with aid awarded during the full aid year, and to certain private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or clock-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the full 12-month period.

Typical full academic-year out-of-state tuition and required fees, in dollars, for a full-time doctor's professional practice student in Dentistry; applies to students who do not meet the state's or institution's residency requirements.

Out-of-state required fees charged for a full-time first-professional student for the full academic year. These are mandatory fixed fees beyond tuition for students who do not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements.

Counts full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition whose income falls between $75,001 and $110,000 and who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid during the full aid year. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students and their aid for the full aid year.

SAT Evidence-Based Reading and Writing score at the 25th percentile among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted SAT scores, for institutions that require test scores for admission and do not have an open-admission policy; includes students admitted in the preceding summer and entering that fall.

Indicates whether the institution offers a first-professional degree program requiring at least two years of prior college work and six or more total years of college-level study, in fields such as medicine, law, dentistry, pharmacy, and theology.

Total contracted work months, which may differ from months paid, for full-time male instructional staff as of November 1; excludes medical-school staff and includes instruction-only staff and those combining instruction with research and/or public service.

Headcount of women enrolled for credit during the 12-month period, combining the Asian and Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander race/ethnicity categories (including institutions using the former Asian/Pacific Islander category).

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received grant or scholarship aid from federal, state or local governments or the institution; students receiving only other grant sources are excluded. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students and aid awarded throughout the full aid year.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $75,001–$110,000 income range who paid in-state or in-district tuition, received any Title IV aid, and were awarded grant or scholarship aid from federal, state/local, or institutional sources. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students' aid received during the full aid year; private institutions, nonstandard calendars, and students receiving only private-source aid, loans, or work-study are excluded.

Count of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking students who were enrolled part time at the prior fall reporting date, including students first enrolled in the preceding summer and those with unknown entry intent; at four-year institutions, the cohort is limited to bachelor’s degree seekers. For continuous-enrollment institutions using a full-year cohort, it covers students enrolled from August 1 through October 31, and status is based on prior-fall enrollment even if it later changes.

Number of subsidized Stafford Loan recipients who did not receive Pell Grants and completed an associate degree or certificate (or another non-bachelor's award) within 150% of the program's normal completion time, covering the applicable cohort for four-year institutions and the cohort for two-year or less-than-two-year institutions.

Categorical NCES-assigned comparison group for institutions participating in Title IV federal aid programs, based on degree-granting status, institutional control, institution category, Carnegie Classification, largest program, enrollment size, and special classifications such as tribal colleges, service institutions, and other jurisdictions. It represents an automatic comparison group rather than an institution-selected group; distance-learning-only institutions may be classified separately or by Carnegie Classification depending on the reporting cycle.

Identifies whether the institution reported doctor's and professional degree completions using the old classification (master's, doctor's, and first-professional degrees) or the new postbaccalaureate classification (master's, research/scholarship doctor's, professional-practice doctor's, and other doctor's degrees), which reclassifies first-professional degrees and related certificates into graduate-level categories.

Typical full academic-year out-of-state tuition and required fees, in dollars, for a full-time student enrolled in a doctor's professional practice program (such as medicine), as defined by the institution. Applies to students who do not meet the applicable state or institutional residency requirements.

Identifies the method used to allocate combined completions among separately reported parent and child institutions: proportional student FTE, proportional faculty/staff FTE, equal shares across institutions, or proportions submitted by the parent institution.
Typical dollar amount of required fees charged for the full academic year to full-time, out-of-state students enrolled in a doctor's professional practice program, such as dentistry.

For each 6-digit CIP code, indicates whether all postbaccalaureate certificate programs in that CIP can be completed entirely via distance education (1 = yes, 0 = no), based on 12-month completions reporting, including programs with zero awards; 2-digit CIP and institution-total records instead aggregate the number of programs offered (1 = high) or indicate none (0).
