Annual dollar amount of required fees charged to full-time undergraduate students who meet the institution's or state's in-state residency requirements. Required fees are mandatory charges beyond tuition.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the fall cohort who pay in-state tuition rates.

Typical full-year tuition and required fees charged to full-time students in Osteopathic Medicine (D.O.) professional-practice programs who meet the institution's or state's in-state residency requirements; full-time status is defined by the institution.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who live off campus and not with family and received grant or scholarship aid from federal, state or local governments or the institution (excluding students with only other grant aid); populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded per full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate in the $110,001-or-more income group who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report fall-enrolled students’ aid over the full aid year.

Total dollar amount of federal, state, local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received Title IV aid and whose financial-aid income used to determine EFC was $75,001–$110,000. It applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students’ aid for the full aid year, and to public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour/occupational calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid year.

Identifies the staff member’s primary occupational activity, based on the institution’s classification and normally the activity receiving the most time, along with whether the staff member is full- or part-time. Faculty are staff whose principal activity is instruction, research, or public service; casual employees, work-study students, and graduate, instructional, or research assistants are excluded.

Average dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state/local, or institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at all income levels who received Title IV aid. It applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall enrollment and aid for the full aid year, and to public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars reporting enrollment over a 12-month period.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying the in-state or in-district rate who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid and fall within the specified income range. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students' aid over the full aid year.

Average dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state/local, or institutional sources awarded per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate in the $75,001–$110,000 income band who received Title IV aid and paid the in-state or in-district tuition rate. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort across the full aid year; income is the amount used to determine the student’s Expected Family Contribution, including parent and student income for dependents and student income for independents.

SAT Evidence-Based Reading and Writing score at the 75th percentile among submitted scores for first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students; reported when test scores are required for admission at institutions without an open-admission policy.

The published in-state tuition amount, in dollars, charged for the full academic year to full-time, first-time undergraduate students who meet the state or institution’s residency requirements. It applies to degree-granting institutions reporting these students for the academic year, including institutions with nontraditional academic calendar systems.

The median (50th percentile) ACT Math score among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted ACT scores, including students entering in the prior summer. Reported only by institutions without an open-admission policy that require test scores for admission.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students awarded student loans, including Title IV, institutional, and private loans to the student but excluding parent loans such as PLUS.

Annual dollar charges used for financial-aid purposes for on-campus room and board for full-time, first-time undergraduate students, including a typical shared-room charge and a meal-plan charge for a specified number of meals per week.

Average dollar amount of institution-funded scholarships and fellowships awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including awards targeted by factors such as state of residence, major, or athletics.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $0–$30,000 income group who received any Title IV federal aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or institution; private-source grants, loans, and work-study alone are excluded. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard calendars that report fall-enrolled students' aid over the full aid year, and to eligible private institutions using continuous or program-differentiated calendars that report a 12-month enrollment period.

Indicates whether the institution offers physical facilities for an academic library, including facilities supporting the library’s collections, staff, and scheduled services; it is not a count or dollar measure.

A categorical classification of institutions by degree-granting status, highest award level, and whether awards are primarily at the bachelor's level or above: degree-granting graduate without undergraduate degrees (1), primarily baccalaureate or above (2), not primarily baccalaureate or above (3), associate's and certificates (4), nondegree-granting above-baccalaureate (5), or nondegree-granting sub-baccalaureate (6). It is derived from institutional offerings and completions; inactive institutions and administrative units are not applicable, while non-Title IV institutions that did not report the required components are not reported.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students awarded federal grants or federally sponsored educational assistance, including Pell Grants and SEOG.

Headcount of female, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students enrolled part time in the most recent fall period, including students who began in the preceding summer and those admitted through early decision or early action; applies to institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

Indicator of whether at least one certificate program in the 300–899 clock-hour or 9–29 semester/trimester (13–44 quarter) credit-hour range, within a six-digit CIP code, can be completed entirely through distance education; 1 means yes and 0 means no program is offered. For two-digit CIP and institution-total records, it is an aggregate count of programs offered in this category, based on the 12-month completions reporting period.

Average net price in dollars per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate in the specified income range who pays the in-state or in-district tuition rate and received Title IV federal aid; it reflects total cost of attendance minus average federal, state/local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort awarded throughout the full aid year.

Average dollar amount of nonfederal loans sponsored by the institution or private sources and awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students; excludes loans made directly to parents.

Indicates whether the institution offers bachelor's degrees or equivalent awards, typically requiring four to five years of full-time equivalent college-level study, including qualifying cooperative and accelerated programs.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving Title IV federal student aid whose financial-aid income used to determine Expected Family Contribution falls between $30,001 and $48,000. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students for the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the full 12-month aid year.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $75,001–$110,000 income range who received any Title IV federal aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or institution. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard calendars that report fall-enrolled students with aid awarded during the full aid year, and to applicable private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid year.
Annual dollar amount of required fees charged to full-time graduate students who meet in-state residency requirements. The fees are mandatory charges separate from tuition.

Categorical comparison-group classification assigned by NCES for institutions that did not provide their own Data Feedback Report comparison group. It covers Title IV-participating institutions and groups them by degree-granting status, control, sector characteristics such as Carnegie classification or highest degree, size, region, locale, largest program, and special populations including tribal, distance-learning, service, and other-jurisdiction institutions.

Aggregate dollar amount of federal, state, local, and institutional grant or scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received Title IV aid and whose financial-aid income was $48,001–$75,000. Reported for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars based on fall enrollment, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars based on enrollment during the 12-month aid period; aid may have been received at any time during that full aid year.

Estimated dollar amount for a full academic year of other expenses—such as laundry, transportation, entertainment, and furnishings—for full-time, first-time undergraduate students living off campus with family; excludes tuition and fees, books and supplies, and room and board.

Categorizes institutions by their fall enrollment profile: exclusively undergraduate two-year or four-year, very high/high/majority undergraduate, majority graduate, or exclusively graduate. For institutions enrolling both levels, the categories reflect the graduate share of full-time-equivalent enrollment (full-time headcount plus one-third of part-time headcount), while exclusively undergraduate categories distinguish two-year from bachelor's-or-higher institutions.

Fall credit-enrollment headcount of students identified as another gender, reported only in aggregate for undergraduate and graduate levels (not by full-/part-time status or detailed degree-seeking categories). The value is blank when an institution cannot report another-gender enrollment and zero when it can report it but has none.

Total dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, receiving Title IV aid, and whose income used to determine expected family contribution was $48,001–$75,000. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort across the full aid year.

The per-credit-hour charge in dollars for part-time graduate students who do not meet the state's or institution's residency requirements; part-time graduate enrollment is defined as 8 or fewer semester or quarter credits.

Total dollar amount of non-Pell federal grant aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including grants such as SEOG and other federal student aid programs.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus with family who received grant or scholarship aid from federal, state, local, or institutional sources; students receiving only other grant aid are excluded. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard calendar systems using fall enrollment cohorts, and by public or private institutions with continuous, program-different, or contact-hour calendars using a 12-month enrollment period.
Identifies the institution’s control and affiliation category: public, private for-profit, private not-for-profit independent, or private not-for-profit with a religious affiliation.
Measures the total length of the institution’s second-largest program, reported in either clock hours or credit hours.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who live off campus with family and received Title IV federal aid during the full aid year; populated for public institutions with standard-term calendar systems reporting aid for a fall-enrolled cohort.

Dollar total of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources awarded across all income levels to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort over the full aid year.

Headcount of Direct Subsidized Loan recipients who did not receive Pell Grants and completed a bachelor’s degree or equivalent within 150% of the institution’s normal completion time; reported for four-year institutions and the applicable cohort.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in all income levels who paid in-state or in-district tuition, received any Title IV federal student aid, and were awarded grant or scholarship aid from federal, state/local, or institutional sources; private grants, loans, and work-study alone do not qualify. Populated for public institutions with standard academic calendars that report aid for fall enrollees across the full aid year.

Total dollar amount of Department of Defense Tuition Assistance benefits awarded through the institution to graduate students, including eligible spouses or dependents; excludes benefits not awarded or certified through the institution.

Published in-state tuition and required fees for full-time, first-time undergraduate students for the full academic year; in-state means students meeting the applicable state or institutional residency requirements.

Indicates whether a Doctor's degree-other program is offered based on 12-month completions reporting: at the 6-digit CIP level, 1 means offered even if no degrees were awarded and 0 means not offered. At 2-digit CIP and grand-total records, the value is the count of programs offered rather than a binary indicator.

Headcount of full-time women who are first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students enrolled in the institution’s fall entering cohort, including students admitted through early decision or early action and those who began in the preceding summer; applicable to institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

Identifies whether fall enrollment race/ethnicity data use the new categories, the old categories, or a mixture of both; nonresident alien and race/ethnicity unknown categories are common to both methods.
Fall headcount of male U.S. nonresident students enrolled for credit, measured as of the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV federal aid and any grant or scholarship aid from federal, state/local, or institutional sources; private-source grants, loans, and work-study without qualifying grant aid are excluded. Applies to public institutions with standard-term calendars that report fall-enrolled students' aid for the full aid year.

Typical full-academic-year tuition and required fees, in dollars, charged to full-time Pharmacy doctoral professional-practice students who do not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid and whose aid-determined income falls in this bracket; populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students' aid received during the full aid year.

Estimated full-academic-year amount for laundry, transportation, entertainment, furnishings, and other expenses for full-time, first-time undergraduate students living off campus and not with family; tuition, fees, room and board are excluded.
Headcount of full-time, non-medical instructional staff whose contract covers 10 months, as of November 1; includes staff performing instruction alone or combined with research and/or public service.

Indicates whether the institution offers recreational or avocational programs for personal interest or leisure that do not provide postsecondary credit, lead to a formal award or degree, or develop occupationally specific skills.

Total dollar amount of repayable student loans awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including federal, institutional, and private loans but excluding parent loans such as PLUS.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the fall cohort who pay in-state tuition rates.

Headcount of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students enrolled either full or part time in the most recent fall period, including students who began in the preceding summer and those admitted through early decision or early action; reported for institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

Dollar amount of required fees charged for the full academic year to full-time, first-time undergraduate students residing in the institution’s local district; it covers fees separate from tuition and may be lower than the in-state rate.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded per full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate in the $48,001–$75,000 income band who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received any Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students’ aid over the full aid year.

Counts full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received Title IV federal aid and whose student or parent income used to determine EFC was $0–$30,000. Populated only for public institutions with standard term calendars that report a fall cohort and aid awarded during the full aid year.

Count of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students admitted for the fall period whose gender is unknown, including full- and part-time students, early decision/action applicants, and students beginning in the preceding summer. Populated for institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received federal grant aid other than Pell Grants, including programs such as SEOG and other federal student aid.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV federal aid (grants, work-study, or loans) during the full aid year, categorized by family income of $48,001–$75,000; reported only by public institutions with standard term calendars for students enrolled in the fall.

Count of students in the revised cohort who received neither a Pell Grant nor a Direct Subsidized Loan and were excluded from noncompletion outcomes because they left within 150% of normal time for a documented reason such as death or permanent disability, military or active-duty service, federal foreign-aid service, or an official church mission.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received state or local government grants, scholarships, or waivers.

Typical annual in-state required fees, in dollars, charged to a full-time first-professional pharmacy student who meets the state or institution’s residency requirements. Required fees are mandatory charges beyond tuition.

Total dollar amount of federal, state, local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the specified income range who pay in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV federal aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort across the full aid year.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $0–$30,000 income bracket who received any Title IV federal aid and any grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or the institution; students receiving only private/other-source aid, loans, or Federal Work-Study are excluded. Applicable to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard calendars that report fall-enrolled students with aid awarded during the full aid year, and to qualifying private institutions using continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students receiving any student loan or grant/scholarship aid from the federal government, state or local government, or the institution. Excludes federal work-study, parent loans, and grants or scholarships from private or other sources.

Average base salary in dollars for full-time women instructional staff on 11-month contracts, as of November 1; includes staff whose duties are instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service, and excludes medical-school staff and supplements, overloads, bonuses, and additional administrative stipends.

The 25th-percentile SAT Writing score among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted SAT scores, including students admitted the preceding summer. Reported only by institutions without an open-admission policy when test scores are required and at least 60% of these enrolled students submitted scores.

The 25th-percentile ACT Math score among enrolled first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted ACT scores. Reported only by institutions without open admission policies where ACT scores are required and at least 60% of these students submitted scores; includes students admitted the preceding summer.

Average base salary in dollars for full-time male instructional staff on 9-month contracts, covering instruction or instruction combined with research and/or public service; excludes medical-school staff and supplements, overloads, bonuses, and administrative stipends.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students receiving federal grant aid other than Pell Grants.

Percentage of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received any financial aid, including grants, loans, scholarships, waivers, benefits, employer aid, and other non-family assistance.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate in the $30,001–$48,000 income range who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students’ aid awarded during the full aid year.

Counts full-time instructional staff across all academic ranks, including employees whose primary assignments combine instruction with research and/or public service; full-time status is institution-defined at the snapshot date.
Headcount of full-time, first-time undergraduate degree/certificate-seeking students who were awarded Pell Grants, including eligible students in academic, occupational, or vocational programs.

Indicates whether post-master’s certificate programs in a 6-digit CIP code can all be completed entirely through distance education, based on programs offered during the 12-month completions period; 1 means offered and 0 means not offered, including programs with no awards. For 2-digit CIP and institution-total records, the value is an aggregate count of programs offered rather than a yes/no indicator.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from families with income of $110,001 or more who received Title IV federal grant aid (including Pell, FSEOG, ACG, National SMART, or TEACH grants). Reported for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard calendars with fall enrollment and full-aid-year aid reporting, and for eligible private institutions using continuous or program-specific calendars with 12-month enrollment and full-aid-year aid reporting.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid during the full aid year. Populated for public institutions with standard term-based calendar systems that report fall-enrolled students and their aid over the full aid year.

Headcount of institution-defined full-time employees on the payroll as of November 1, excluding staff employed by or working in an M.D./D.O. medical school component or freestanding medical school; hospital-only and other health or allied-health staff are excluded only when covered by the medical-school exclusion.

Total operating and maintenance of plant expenses, in dollars, covering services and costs for maintaining campus grounds, buildings, facilities, security, utilities, repairs, insurance, leasing, and related activities. In older reporting periods, this natural expense category may be zero because O&M was also reported as a separate functional category; later reporting allocates these expenses across functions.

Average dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state/local, or institutional sources for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $110,001-or-more income group who pay in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall-enrolled cohort across the full aid year.
Indicates whether the institution's academic library offers access to digital or electronic resources.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received federal grants or federally sponsored educational assistance, including Pell Grants and SEOG.

A categorical indicator identifying institutions in the current IPEDS universe by Title IV participation and whether they are primarily postsecondary: values 1 and 3 denote Title IV institutions in the First Look universe, with 1 primarily and 3 not primarily postsecondary; other values cover related non-Title-IV or nonpublic categories, while 9 indicates an inactive institution. It is generally limited to institutions open to the public, with specified military-academy and Coast Guard exceptions.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or institution, with financial-aid income used for EFC determination in the stated income range. Applicable only to public institutions with standard term calendars reporting a fall cohort and aid awarded throughout the full aid year; students receiving only private/other grants, loans, or work-study are excluded.

Indicates how an institution uses other tests (such as Wonderlic or WISC-III) in selecting entering first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students: required, considered if submitted, or not considered; applicable only to institutions without an open-admission policy.
Reports the full-academic-year tuition and required fees, in dollars, charged to full-time first-professional theology students who do not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements.

Average dollar net price (cost of attendance minus federal, state/local, and institutional grants or scholarships, excluding other aid) for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received such aid during the full aid year. It applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall enrollment, and to public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or primarily clock-hour calendars; the amount reflects a full academic year or the reported program length.

Indicates whether each 6-digit CIP program leading to a doctor's degree—professional practice is offered entirely via distance education (1 = offered, 0 = not offered), with 2-digit CIP and institution-level records reporting counts of such programs. It applies when the institution reports a nonnegative number of these degrees in the 12-month completions period; distance education means all required coursework can be completed through distance education courses.

Indicates whether the institution offers a postsecondary certificate, diploma, or other award below the baccalaureate level requiring at least 1 but less than 2 full-time-equivalent academic years, 30–59 semester or trimester credits, 45–89 quarter credits, or 900–1,799 clock hours.

Typical tuition and required fees charged for a full-time Chiropractic (D.C. or D.C.M.) doctor's professional practice student who does not meet the institution's or state's residency requirements, for the full academic year.

Dollar amount of revenue received from the federal government through appropriations, grants, and contracts, including funding for research, training, and similar activities. Federal Pell and similar student aid grants are included only when the institution records them as student aid expense or as grant revenue/allowances; they are excluded when treated as agency transactions.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living in institution-owned or controlled on-campus housing, paying in-state or in-district tuition, and receiving federal, state, local, or institutional grant or scholarship aid; students receiving only other grant sources are excluded. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students' aid received during the full aid year.

Headcount of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate applicants whose gender is unknown for the institution’s most recent fall admission period, including early decision, early action, and students who began in the preceding summer; reported only by institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

A 5-digit code identifying the Core Based Statistical Area associated with the institution’s address; institutions not associated with a CBSA have a not-applicable value. Use CBSATYPE to distinguish metropolitan from micropolitan statistical areas.

Headcount of students enrolled for credit exclusively in distance education courses and residing outside the United States, measured as of the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15.

Total dollars of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, whose financial-aid income used for EFC determination was $110,000 or more and who received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort over the full aid year.

Average dollar amount of Department of Defense Tuition Assistance benefits received by undergraduate student recipients, including eligible spouses or dependents; covers only benefits awarded or certified through the institution and known to it.

Average dollar amount of institutional scholarships and fellowships received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including institution-designated awards such as those based on residency, major, or athletics.

A categorical code for the institution’s geographic urbanization level, based on its physical address and ranging from large city to remote rural; codes distinguish city, suburb, town, and rural locations by population size or distance from urban areas. It is blank for institutions in American Samoa, the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, Guam, and the Virgin Islands, which are outside the coding scheme.

Reports the published tuition amount for a full academic year charged to full-time, first-time undergraduate students who do not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements (out-of-state students).

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates whose living arrangement is unknown and who received federal, state, local, or institutional grant or scholarship aid; students receiving only other grant aid are excluded. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students for the full aid year, and to public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.
Typical dollar amount of required fees charged for a full-time first-professional student who meets the institution’s or state’s in-state residency requirements, covering the full academic year.

Total dollar amount of Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits awarded or certified through the institution to graduate student recipients, including eligible spouses or dependents. It includes only benefits known to and processed by the institution, excludes benefits certified elsewhere and Yellow Ribbon institutional aid, and covers tuition and fees, books and supplies, and housing payments.

Headcount of men and women of Hispanic or Latino/Hispanic origin enrolled for credit at the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15, combining the newer and older Hispanic ethnicity categories.

Average dollars of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded over the full aid year to aid recipients among full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition; applies to public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students and full-year aid.

Total dollar amount of federal, state, local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, receiving Title IV aid, and whose financial-aid income used to determine EFC is $0–$30,000. Populated for public institutions with standard academic calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the fall cohort who pay in-district tuition rates.

A categorical classification of an institution’s undergraduate profile, combining the share of undergraduates enrolled part-time versus full-time, first-year students’ academic preparation or selectivity, and the share of entering undergraduates who are transfer students. It applies to degree-granting institutions and distinguishes two-year associate’s institutions from four-year bachelor’s-or-higher institutions; classifications are snapshots of institutional attributes and behavior.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received any federal, state, local-government, or institutional grant aid.

Identifies the basis used to allocate combined parent-and-child institution finance data: student FTE; faculty/staff FTE from Fall Staff or Employees by Assigned Position data; full-time faculty from Fall Staff data; equal shares across institutions; or proportions submitted by the parent institution. FTE-based methods count full-time staff plus one-third of part-time staff.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $48,001–$75,000 income range who received Title IV aid. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars for fall-enrolled students, and by public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or clock-hour calendars for students enrolled during the full 12-month aid year.
Total dollar amount of federal, state, local, and institutional grant aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students.

Indicates whether the institution is a member of the Department of Defense Voluntary Educational Partnership Memorandum of Understanding, a voluntary program intended to expand and improve postsecondary opportunities for servicemembers worldwide.

Coded categorical measure of the institution’s highest degree level offered, derived from its reported program-level offerings; includes codes for institutions offering other undergraduate or certificate levels and for institutions with no matching reported offering.
Annual dollar charge for on-campus meals and housing used in financial-aid cost calculations for full-time, first-time undergraduate students.

NCES-created categorical comparison group for institutions participating in Title IV federal student aid programs, based on degree-granting status, control, institution type, Carnegie classification or highest degree offered, largest program, enrollment size, and special institutional characteristics; it is used for automatic Data Feedback Report comparisons when an institution does not provide its own group.

Typical dollar amount of mandatory fees charged for the full academic year to a full-time optometry (doctor's professional practice) student who meets the institution's or state's in-state residency requirements.

Count of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate applicants of another gender for the fall admissions cohort, including early decision/action applicants and students who began in the preceding summer; applies to institutions without an open-admission policy. The value is blank when the institution could not report another-gender data and is zero when it could report the category but had no such applicants.

Typical full academic-year tuition and required fees charged to full-time veterinary medicine (doctor's professional practice) students who do not meet the institution's or state's residency requirements; reported as a dollar amount.

Fall headcount of women enrolled for credit who are Hispanic or Latino, combining the newer and older Hispanic ethnicity categories; enrollment is measured as of the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15.

Average net price in dollars per student for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, in the specified income range, who received Title IV federal aid; it is total cost of attendance minus average federal, state/local, and institutional grant or scholarship aid. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendar systems that report aid for a fall cohort awarded throughout the full aid year.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received repayable student loans, including Title IV, institutional, and private loans but excluding PLUS and other loans made directly to parents.

The published dollar amount of in-state tuition and required fees for full-time, first-time undergraduate students for the full academic year, applying the institution or state residency requirements.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $48,001–$75,000 income range who paid in-state or in-district tuition, received any Title IV federal aid, and received grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or the institution; private-source grants, loans, and work-study alone are excluded. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students’ aid awarded throughout the full aid year.

Percentage of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted ACT scores, including students entering in the preceding summer; reported for institutions without an open-admission policy when admission requires test scores and at least 60% of this cohort submitted scores.

Typical dollar amount of required fees, excluding tuition, charged for a full-time first-professional student in an osteopathic medicine program who meets in-state residency requirements, for the full academic year.
Headcount of part-time graduate students, excluding students in doctor's degree–professional practice programs; populated when the institution enrolls part-time students.

Headcount of nonresident aliens enrolled for credit on the institution’s official fall reporting date (or October 15); this category covers temporary visa holders and excludes resident aliens and other noncitizens admitted for permanent resident status.

Count of full-time women in instructional roles, excluding medical-school staff, whose contracts cover fewer than 9 months, measured as of November 1. Instructional staff includes employees performing instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service.

Indicates whether the institution uses the older postbaccalaureate classification (master’s, doctoral, and first-professional degrees) or the newer classification (master’s, research/scholarship doctoral, professional-practice doctoral, and other doctoral degrees); under the newer method, students in first-professional programs are classified as graduate students in enrollment reporting.

Total dollars of federal, state, local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received during the full aid year by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $75,001–$110,000 income group who received Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard-term calendars that report on fall-enrolled students, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour calendars that report on students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Headcount of full-time men in instructional roles, excluding medical-school staff, as of November 1, whose contracts cover 9, 10, 11, or 12 months. Instructional staff includes employees whose function is instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service.

Identifies which full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate cohort the record represents: the combined cohort, the bachelor's-or-equivalent subcohort, or the other degree/certificate-seeking subcohort for four-year institutions, or the combined cohort for two-year and less-than-two-year institutions. Full-time means at least 12 semester or quarter credits or 24 clock hours per week, and first-time means no prior postsecondary enrollment except permitted summer or advanced-standing enrollment.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received grant or scholarship aid from federal, state or local governments or the institution; students receiving only other grant sources are excluded. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students’ aid over the full aid year.

Total base salary outlays, excluding supplements, overloads, bonuses, and administrative stipends, for full-time male instructional staff on 9-month-contract-equivalent terms. Instructional staff perform instruction alone or combined with research and/or public service; medical-school staff are excluded, but staff in affiliated health or allied-health departments are included.

FIPS-based congressional district identifier for the institution's location, combining the state code with a district code: 00 for states represented at large, 98 for U.S. territories with nonvoting delegates, and -2 for entities without congressional representation.

Annual dollar amount of required fees charged to a full-time, first-professional Chiropractic (D.C. or D.C.M.) student who meets in-state residency requirements. Required fees are mandatory charges separate from tuition.
Total dollar amount of federal, state, local, and institutional grant aid received by full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students.

Total base salary outlays in dollars for full-time instructional staff as of November 1, excluding medical-school staff and supplements, overloads, bonuses, and stipends for additional responsibilities.
Dollar amount of discounts and allowances funded by endowments and gifts and recorded as reductions to tuition and fee revenue and auxiliary-enterprise revenue.

Headcount of women enrolled for credit in the fall who are nonresident aliens (in the United States temporarily on a visa); applicable to four-year institutions, while resident aliens and other permanent-status noncitizens are counted in their reported racial/ethnic categories.

Indicates whether the institution offers for-credit developmental education courses or programs that build reading, writing, or math skills for students academically underprepared for college-level credit-bearing coursework.

Institution-level indicator showing whether the institution has a tenure system, inferred from reporting at least one tenured or non-tenured faculty member on a tenure track; otherwise it indicates no tenure system.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $30,001–$48,000 income range who received Title IV federal grant aid during the full aid year; reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars for fall-enrolled students, and by private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour calendars for students enrolled during the institution’s 12-month reporting period.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying the in-state or in-district tuition rate who received Title IV federal student aid and whose income used to determine Expected Family Contribution was $110,001 or more. Applies to public institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students' aid for the full aid year.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid, grouped by the income used to determine Expected Family Contribution falling in the specified range. Populated only for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year; income includes parents’ and the student’s adjusted gross income for dependent students and the student’s adjusted gross income for independent students.

Total dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local governments and institutional sources awarded during the full aid year to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received such aid. Applies only to public institutions with standard calendar systems that report aid data for fall-enrolled students; excludes other grant-aid sources.

Headcount of institution employees/staff, excluding personnel in the medical-school component but including employees in postsecondary hospital or medical-center components and first-professional schools other than medicine. It includes institution-defined full-time and part-time staff and faculty, but excludes casual employees and College Work-Study students.

Indicates whether all Doctor’s degree–other programs within a 6-digit CIP code can be completed entirely via distance education: 1 means offered and fully online, and 0 means not offered or not fully online, based on programs reported in the 12-month completions period. For 2-digit CIP and institution-total records, it instead reports the total number of programs offered in this category.

Counts full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid whose financial-aid income falls in the 75,001–110,000 range. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report on fall enrollees, and for public or private institutions using continuous, contact-hour, or program-specific calendars that report on students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Published dollar amount of tuition and required fees for full-time, first-time undergraduate students who do not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements, covering the full academic year.
Average dollar amount of institution- or department-funded scholarships and fellowships awarded per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate student.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the fall cohort, including students in bachelor's, associate's, vocational, or technical programs.

Annual dollar amount charged to full-time undergraduate students who do not meet the applicable state or institutional residency requirements; a comprehensive fee covering tuition, required fees, room, and board, and sometimes books and supplies.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received any federal, state, local, or institutional grant aid.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition whose income used to determine Expected Family Contribution was $0–$30,000 and who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid during the full aid year. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report aid for students enrolled in the fall.

Counts full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus apart from family who received federal, state, local, or institutional grant or scholarship aid, excluding students receiving only other grant sources. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students with aid during the full aid year, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received federal student loans, including Title IV subsidized and unsubsidized loans but excluding parent loans such as PLUS.

Indicates whether the institution reported fall staff race and ethnicity using the new categories, the old categories, or a mixture of both; the new method reports Hispanic/Latino individuals regardless of race and assigns race categories only to non-Hispanic/Latino individuals, while nonresident alien and race/ethnicity unknown are common to both methods.

Counts full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $0–$30,000 income level who pay in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV federal grant aid during the full aid year; populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students.

Annual dollar charge to full-time undergraduate students who meet the institution's or state's in-state residency requirements; the comprehensive fee is a single amount covering tuition, required fees, room, and board, and may also include books and supplies.
Unduplicated headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the full-year cohort who paid in-district tuition rates.

Headcount of male high school students enrolled for college credit during the 12-month period whose race/ethnicity is unknown; these students are included in non-degree/non-certificate-seeking unduplicated 12-month enrollment.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition whose income used for Expected Family Contribution falls between $30,001 and $48,000 and who received Title IV federal aid (grants, work-study, or loans). Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students awarded aid during the full aid year.

Categorical classification of an institution by the undergraduate-versus-graduate enrollment profile, using full-time-equivalent enrollment (full-time headcount plus one-third of part-time headcount); exclusively undergraduate institutions are distinguished as two-year or four-year, while mixed institutions are grouped by the graduate share of FTE enrollment (<10%, 10–24%, 25–49%, or at least 50%), with a separate exclusively graduate category.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition whose income used to determine Expected Family Contribution was $48,001–$75,000 and who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid during the full aid year. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students and aid received throughout the full aid year.

Identifies the full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate cohort covered by the table: bachelor's and other-than-bachelor's degree seekers at four-year institutions, all degree/certificate seekers at two-year institutions, or all such students at less-than-two-year institutions.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $75,001–$110,000 income group who received any Title IV federal aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or institution; private-source grants, loans, and Federal Work Study alone are excluded. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard calendars reporting fall-enrolled students’ aid over the full aid year, and for applicable private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Headcount of male first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who enrolled full time in the most recent fall period, including students who began in the preceding summer and those admitted through early decision or early action; reported only by institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received any financial aid, including grants, loans, scholarships, waivers, benefits, employer aid, and other student assistance.

Counts full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $75,001–$110,000 income range who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid during the full aid year. Applicable to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard-term calendars that report fall-enrolled students, and to public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, clock-hour, or primarily occupational calendars that report students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Total dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, receiving Title IV aid, and whose aid-determining income is $75,001–$110,000. It is populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students awarded aid during the full aid year.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living in institution-controlled on-campus housing, paying in-state or in-district tuition, and receiving any Title IV federal aid during the full aid year, across all income levels. Populated only for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for students enrolled in the fall.

Total dollars of non-Pell federal grant aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including students in bachelor's, associate, vocational, or technical programs.

The institution’s total unrestricted net assets, in dollars, including both undesignated and board-designated funds and the unrestricted net investment in plant, property, and equipment after related debt.

Typical dollar amount of required fees for a full-time first-professional osteopathic medicine student for the full academic year, charged to out-of-state students who do not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements.

Total dollars in Department of Defense Tuition Assistance benefits awarded through the institution to all student recipients, including eligible servicemembers, spouses, and dependents. It excludes benefits not awarded or certified through the institution and reflects only amounts known to the institution.

The full academic-year dollar amount of required fees charged to full-time undergraduate students residing in the institution’s local area (in-district), excluding tuition. Undergraduates include students in associate, bachelor’s, and sub-baccalaureate vocational or technical programs; full-time means at least 12 semester or quarter credits, or 24 contact hours per week.
Total dollar amount of Pell Grant aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students.

SAT Math score at the 75th percentile among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students submitting SAT/ACT scores, including students admitted in the prior summer. Populated for institutions that require admission test scores and do not have an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students awarded loans they must repay, including federal, institutional, and private student loans but excluding parent loans such as PLUS.

Total dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $48,001–$75,000 income range who received Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall enrollees, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid year.

Average dollar amount of federal Title IV subsidized and unsubsidized student loans received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates; excludes PLUS and other loans made directly to parents.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received any financial aid, including grants, loans, scholarships, fellowships, assistantships, tuition waivers or discounts, veteran benefits, employer aid, and other non-family assistance.

Total base-salary outlays for full-time, non-medical instructional staff, including staff whose functions combine instruction with research or public service, expressed as the amount equivalent to 9-month contracts. Excludes supplements, overloads, bonuses, and administrative stipends, as well as staff in medical schools or their associated hospitals and affiliated health or allied-health departments.

Headcount of employees in the combined occupational group covering librarians, library technicians, archivists, curators, museum technicians, and academic affairs and other education services occupations.

The per-credit-hour tuition charge for part-time undergraduate students who do not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements; part-time means 11 or fewer semester or quarter credits, or fewer than 24 contact hours per week.

Number of subsidized Stafford Loan recipients who did not receive Pell Grants and completed a bachelor's degree or other credential within 150% of the program's normal completion time. It covers the applicable reported cohorts at four-year, two-year, and less-than-two-year institutions.

Headcount of first-time undergraduate students enrolled for credit and seeking a degree or certificate, including students in academic, occupational, vocational, or technical programs and those entering with prior college credit.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received federal grant aid other than Pell Grants, including programs such as SEOG and other federal student aid grants.

Categorical classification of institutions by enrollment size and residential character, using FTE enrollment calculated as full-time enrollment plus one-third of part-time enrollment. Two-year associate’s degree-granting institutions are classified by size; four-year bachelor’s-or-higher institutions are classified by size of degree-seeking enrollment and the share of degree-seeking undergraduates living on campus and attending full time, with a separate category for institutions enrolling only graduate or professional students.

Categorical classification of an institution's undergraduate instructional program, based on the types and distribution of awards and the extent to which graduate programs coexist in corresponding fields. It applies across institutions, including those with graduate education, and distinguishes associate's, baccalaureate/associate's, arts-and-sciences, professions, and balanced program profiles.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received any financial aid, including grants, scholarships, student loans, Federal Work-Study, and aid from private or other sources; parent loans are excluded.

Categorical classification of an institution’s enrollment profile based on the fall mix of undergraduate and graduate/professional students, using FTE enrollment calculated as full-time plus one-third of part-time enrollment. Categories range from exclusively undergraduate two-year or four-year institutions, through very high, high, or majority undergraduate (graduate/professional FTE under 10%, 10–24%, or 25–49%), to majority or exclusively graduate/professional institutions (at least 50% or all graduate/professional FTE).

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $48,001–$75,000 income range who pay in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV federal grant aid during the full aid year. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendar systems reporting aid for students enrolled in the fall.
The dollar amount of student aid funded by endowments and gifts that is applied as a discount or allowance to auxiliary enterprise revenues.

Average dollar amount of Department of Defense Tuition Assistance benefits awarded through the institution per student recipient, including eligible servicemembers and their spouses or dependents. It excludes benefits awarded or certified outside the institution and reflects only amounts known to the institution.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the specified income range who received Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students’ aid over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars reporting students enrolled over the 12-month aid year.

FIPS-based congressional district code for the institution’s location, combining the state code with a two-digit district code; “00” denotes an at-large district, “98” a nonvoting-delegate area, and “-2” an area without congressional representation.

A categorical profile of the undergraduate population based on attendance intensity (part-time versus full-time), entering first-time students’ SAT/ACT preparation, and the share of undergraduates who transferred from another institution. The part-time measure covers all undergraduates at two-year institutions and degree-seeking undergraduates at four-year institutions; the classification is a time-specific snapshot and does not measure educational quality.

Average dollar amount of federal grants and educational assistance awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including Pell Grants, SEOG, and comparable aid from other federal agencies.

The ACT Math score at or below which 25% of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students fall, reported when admission requires test scores and the institution does not have an open-admission policy; includes students who first enrolled in the preceding summer.

Indicates whether an institution offered an associate’s degree program in each 6-digit CIP category, based on the 12-month completions period; zero awards still count as a program offered. For 2-digit CIP categories and the grand total, it reports the count of programs offered rather than a yes/no indicator.

Headcount of all students receiving Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits known to and awarded or certified through the institution; eligible spouses and dependents may be included. Yellow Ribbon institutional aid is excluded.

Headcount of undergraduate students enrolled for credit and seeking a degree or formal certificate, including associate, bachelor's, and vocational/technical students; for standard-term institutions it reflects enrollment on the official fall reporting date, while for program reporters it is an unduplicated count of students enrolled during the full 12-month reporting period.

Average dollar amount of Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits awarded through the institution to graduate student recipients, including eligible spouses or dependents. It excludes Yellow Ribbon institutional aid and benefits not awarded or certified through the institution, reflecting only amounts known to the institution.
Reports the published dollar amount of tuition and required fees for entering first-time, first-year undergraduate students in the institution’s largest program.

Number of students in the adjusted cohort who did not receive a Pell Grant or Direct Subsidized Loan and completed an award within 150% of the institution-defined normal completion time; this is a headcount, not a percentage.

Total dollar amount of Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits received by undergraduate student recipients, including eligible spouses or dependents, based only on benefits awarded or certified through the institution. Excludes institutional matching aid provided through the Yellow Ribbon Program and benefits not known to or processed by the institution.

Total dollars of grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $0–$30,000 income group who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students’ aid over the full aid year.

Annual dollar amount of required fees charged to a full-time, first-professional dentistry student who meets the institution's in-state residency requirements. Required fees are mandatory charges beyond tuition.

Count of Direct Subsidized Loan recipients who did not receive Pell Grants and are excluded from the 150%-of-normal-time outcome cohort because they died or became totally and permanently disabled, entered active military service, joined a qualifying federal foreign-aid service, or served an official church mission; students may still be counted if they returned before the status date.

Total dollars of federal, state, local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the specified income band who pay in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions using standard-term calendars that report aid for a fall-enrolled cohort across the full aid year.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus with family, paying in-state or in-district tuition, who received Title IV federal aid during the full aid year; populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting aid for students enrolled in the fall.

Categorizes an institution’s finance-reporting relationship within a parent/child system: full parent reporting (1), partial system with current funds, revenues, and expenses reported by some child campuses but system-wide assets and liabilities reported by the parent (2), a partial system that also includes child campuses whose current funds, revenues, and expenses are reported by another partial campus (3; such reporting partial campuses are coded 6), or a partial system whose system-wide information is reported by an entity outside IPEDS (5).

Average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, in the specified income range, who received Title IV federal aid; it is total cost of attendance minus average federal, state/local, and institutional grant or scholarship aid. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report aid for students enrolled in the fall and awarded aid during the full aid year.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the fall cohort who are legal residents of the locality where the institution is located and therefore eligible for in-district tuition, if offered.

Combined base salary outlays in dollars for full-time, non-medical instructional staff who are women and work under 12-month contracts, counted as of November 1. Covers staff whose function is instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service; excludes supplements, overloads, bonuses, and additional administrative or managerial stipends, as well as staff employed in medical-school or standalone medical-school components.

Average net price is the annual or program-length cost of attendance minus average federal, state/local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $48,001–$75,000 income group who received Title IV aid. It applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard-term calendars that report fall-enrolled students with aid during the full aid year, and to public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report a 12-month aid period; the latter report costs for their largest program.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received Title IV federal grant aid, including Pell, FSEOG, ACG, National SMART, and TEACH Grants. Applicable to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard calendars that report fall-enrolled students over the full aid year, and to certain private institutions using continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled over a 12-month period.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the fall cohort who pay out-of-state tuition rates.

For each 6-digit CIP code, this is a binary indicator that a one-year, less-than-two-year certificate program is offered and all programs in that CIP can be completed entirely through distance education; a zero-award report still counts as offered. On 2-digit CIP and institution-total records, it is instead the count of such programs, with values representing total programs offered rather than a binary indicator.

Counts less-than-one-year certificate programs for which all required coursework can be completed via distance education, based on the 12-month completions reporting period; detail records indicate whether each program is offered, while category and grand-total records provide the number of programs offered.

Headcount of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate applicants who were admitted and enrolled either full or part time in the fall period, identifying as a gender other than men or women; reported for institutions without an open-admission policy, and left blank when the institution could not report this category (zero when it could report and had none).

The 25th-percentile ACT Composite score among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted ACT scores; populated for institutions that require admission test scores and do not have an open-admission policy.

Numeric FIPS-based code identifying the U.S. congressional district where the institution is located; it combines the two-digit state code with the district code. District code 00 denotes a state's at-large district, 98 denotes U.S. areas represented by a nonvoting delegate, and 99 denotes areas with no congressional representation.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates whose living arrangement is unknown and who received Title IV federal aid (grants, work-study, or loans). Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard-term calendars for fall-enrolled aid recipients, and by public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour/occupational calendars for students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Headcount of men among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who applied, were admitted, and enrolled either full or part time in the most recent fall period, including early decision, early action, and students who began in the preceding summer; reported only by institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $30,001–$48,000 income group who paid in-state or in-district tuition, received any Title IV federal aid, and received grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or their institution. Reported for public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students’ aid awarded throughout the full aid year; private institutions, for-profit institutions, and continuous or program-length calendar institutions are not applicable.

Categorical Carnegie classification of an institution’s enrollment profile based on fall enrollment: exclusively undergraduate two-year or four-year, very high/high/majority undergraduate, majority graduate/professional, or exclusively graduate/professional. For institutions enrolling both levels, categories reflect the graduate/professional share of total FTE enrollment, calculated as full-time enrollment plus one-third of part-time enrollment; the classification is based on the observed undergraduate versus graduate/professional mix rather than headcount alone.

Reports whether each post-master’s certificate program is offered via distance education, and at the two-digit CIP and institution-total levels, the number of such programs; it counts programs rather than certificates awarded. Distance education means all required coursework for completion can be completed through distance education courses.

Indicates whether the institution offers academic postsecondary instructional programs leading to a certificate, diploma, associate's, bachelor's, master's, doctoral, or first-professional degree, or providing credits applicable to such a degree.
Indicates whether the institution is designated as a land-grant college or university under the Morrill Acts.

Headcount of women employed full time in instructional roles (instruction alone or combined with research and/or public service), excluding medical-school staff, who were on 10-month contracts as of November 1.

Typical annual required fees, in dollars, charged to full-time in-state students enrolled in other first-professional programs. First-professional programs include fields such as law, medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, veterinary medicine, and theology; full-time status is defined by the institution.

Measures programs for Doctor's, other degrees in which all required coursework can be completed via distance education, based on the institution's 12-month completions reporting. At the 6-digit CIP level it is a 1/0 program-offered indicator, while 2-digit CIP and grand-total records report the count of such programs; it is populated when the institution reports a nonnegative total for the corresponding degrees.

The institution’s predominant calendar system: standard academic terms (semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, or other academic calendar), differing by program, or continuous enrollment. Standard-term institutions report graduation rates for a fall cohort and student charges for a full academic year, while institutions with calendars that differ by program or operate continuously report graduation rates for a full-year cohort and student charges by program.
Percentage of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received any federal, state, local, or institutional grant aid.
