Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $0–$30,000 income group who received any Title IV federal aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or institution; private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions report this for fall-enrolled students receiving aid during the full aid year, or for applicable continuous/program-based institutions for students enrolled during the full 12-month period.
Headcount of non-degree/non-certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received federal loans made directly to the student, excluding PLUS and other federal loans not designated to the student.

ACT Composite score at the 75th percentile among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted ACT scores, for institutions that do not have an open-admission policy and require test scores for admission; includes students entering the prior summer.

Total dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state, local, or institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received Title IV aid and whose financial-aid income used for EFC determination was in the specified range. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students’ aid over the full aid year, and to public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV aid and a grant or scholarship from the federal government, state/local government, or institution; students receiving only private/other grants, loans, or Federal Work-Study are excluded. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received any federal, state, local, or institutional grant aid.

Indicates whether at least one doctoral research/scholarship program in the CIP code can be completed entirely through distance education: 1 means offered and 0 means not offered. For 2-digit CIP and institution-total records, the values are summary indicators (1 = one or more programs offered; 0 = none), rather than a single 6-digit program result.

Unduplicated headcount of students enrolled for credit during the 12-month period who identified as another gender, reported only for undergraduate and graduate levels—not by full- or part-time status or detailed degree/certificate-seeking categories. The cell is blank when the institution could not report this category or when the count is fewer than 5, and is zero when the institution could report it but had no such students.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates with income used for Expected Family Contribution in the $30,001–$48,000 range who received any Title IV aid during the full aid year. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report a fall cohort, and to public or private institutions using continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled over a 12-month period.

Code identifying the award or completion level, ranging from short-term certificates and associate's degrees through bachelor's, master's, post-master's, and research, professional-practice, or other doctor's degrees. Certificate levels are based on program length in clock or credit hours.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living in institution-owned or controlled on-campus housing who received federal, state, local, or institutional grant or scholarship aid; students receiving only other grant aid are excluded. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students’ aid over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-differing, or primarily contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Indicates whether at least one Doctor's degree–professional practice program within a 6-digit CIP code can be completed entirely through distance education, based on programs reported in the institution’s 12-month completions data; it does not mean that all programs in the CIP are online. For 2-digit CIP and institution-total records, the value is an aggregate count of programs offered rather than a binary indicator.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the fall cohort who pay in-state tuition rates.

Headcount of students in the revised entering cohort used for six-year outcome tracking, including corrections for omissions or double counting. The cohort includes first-time and non-first-time entrants for academic-year reporters, while four-year institutions report full-time, first-time entrants.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $75,001–$110,000 income group who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received both Title IV federal student aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or the institution; private-source grants, loans, and work-study alone do not qualify. Reported only by public institutions with standard academic calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $75,001–$110,000 income range who received Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students, and for public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid year.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate at the in-state or in-district tuition rate, across all income levels, among students who received Title IV federal aid. Populated for public institutions with standard academic calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the fall cohort whose home state or residence cannot be determined from institutional records.

Headcount of male students enrolled for credit in a major field of study who are nonresident aliens—temporary visa holders without indefinite U.S. residency rights—at four-year institutions; resident aliens and other permanent-status noncitizens are counted in the applicable racial/ethnic categories instead.

Indicates whether certificate programs of less than 12 weeks (under 300 clock hours or the equivalent credits) in a 6-digit CIP code are offered and can be completed entirely through distance education, based on the institution’s 12-month completions reporting period; it measures program availability, not the number of awards. For 2-digit CIP and institution-total records, the value is an aggregate count of programs offered rather than a binary indicator, and it differs from categories allowing only some programs or programs with mandatory or optional onsite components.
Headcount of men and women classified as Asian, Native Hawaiian, or Other Pacific Islander, using the applicable current or legacy race/ethnicity definitions.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition whose living arrangement is unknown and who received Title IV federal aid during the full aid year; populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting aid for fall-enrolled students.
Number of students in the adjusted cohort who did not receive a Pell grant or subsidized Stafford loan and completed a degree or certificate within 150% of the program's normal completion time.

Typical full academic-year tuition and required fees, in dollars, charged to full-time first-professional Optometry (O.D.) students who do not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements.
Dollar amount of scholarships and fellowships funded by endowments and gifts and applied as discounts or allowances against auxiliary enterprise sales and services, such as room and board charges.

Headcount of degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who were awarded federal student loans made directly to the student, including Title IV loans but excluding PLUS and other federal loans not made directly to the student.

Headcount of full-time, non-medical instructional staff as of November 1, across all contract lengths, including staff whose duties are instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service. Excludes medical-school staff and staff working strictly in an associated hospital; health or allied health staff are excluded only when affiliated with the medical school.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $30,001–$48,000 financial-aid income range who received any Title IV federal student aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal, state/local, or institutional sources; grants from private or other sources alone, loans, and work-study are not counted. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard calendars that report fall-enrolled students with aid received during the full aid year, and for applicable private institutions using continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during a 12-month period with aid received during that full period.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students awarded federal grants or federally sponsored educational assistance, including Pell Grants, SEOG, veterans benefits, and other federal aid.

Total base-salary outlays in dollars for full-time, non-medical instructional staff on 11-month contracts, as of November 1; excludes supplements, overloads, bonuses, and stipends for other responsibilities.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid and whose financial-aid income used to determine EFC fell in this range; applicable only to public institutions with standard-term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students’ aid over the full aid year.

ACT Composite score at the 25th percentile among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted ACT scores. Reported for institutions without an open-admission policy that require test scores and where at least 60% of the relevant entering students submitted scores; includes students admitted in the preceding summer.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students receiving any student loans or grant/scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or the institution; excludes federal work-study, parent loans, and private or other-source grants.

The ACT Math score at or below which 25% of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted ACT scores fall. Populated for institutions that require admission test scores and do not have an open-admission policy; the cohort includes students who began in the preceding summer.

Total dollars of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state/local, or institutional sources received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $110,001-or-more income group who received any Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic terms that report fall-enrolled students, and for public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates awarded federal grant aid other than Pell Grants, including programs such as SEOG and other federal student aid grants.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received federal Title IV subsidized or unsubsidized loans; excludes PLUS and other loans made directly to parents.

Headcount of Pell Grant recipients in the selected cohort (total, bachelor's, or other-than-bachelor's for four-year institutions; two-year or less-than-two-year cohort otherwise) who completed the applicable degree or certificate within 150% of its normal completion time.

Average federal grant aid in dollars received by full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including Pell, SEOG, and other federally sponsored grants or educational assistance.

A headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received Title IV federal student aid and whose EFC-determining income fell within this income band. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students and aid awarded throughout the full aid year.

Estimated dollar amount for a full academic year of on-campus expenses such as laundry, transportation, entertainment, and furnishings for full-time, first-time undergraduate students; excludes tuition and fees, books and supplies, and room and board.

Categorical code assigning an institution to an automatic IPEDS Data Feedback Report comparison group, based on control, Carnegie classification or highest level of offering, geography, program concentration, and enrollment size. Populated for Title IV institutions; non-Title IV institutions are not applicable, and certain service schools and institutions in specified U.S. territories or freely associated states may be unclassified (typically codes 901 or higher).

Headcount of full-time, first-time undergraduate students enrolled for credit and seeking a degree or certificate, including students entering with prior college credits; the cohort is measured at the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15.

Counts bachelor's degree programs offered, based on programs with reported bachelor's awards or an explicit zero-awards indication during the 12-month reporting period. At the 6-digit CIP level, values indicate offered versus not offered; 2-digit CIP and institution-level records provide total program counts.

Headcount of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted ACT scores, including students who first enrolled in the preceding summer. Reported for institutions without open admission policies when ACT scores are required and at least 60% of this enrolled population submitted scores.
Average dollar amount of federal grants and federally sponsored educational assistance awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received federal grants or other federally sponsored educational assistance, including Pell and SEOG grants.

Total dollars of federal, state/local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving Title IV aid whose financial-aid income level is $48,001–$75,000. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received institution-funded scholarships or fellowships, including awards targeted by residence, major, athletics, or other criteria.

Out-of-state required fees charged for a full-time first-professional podiatry student for the full academic year; these are mandatory fixed charges beyond tuition for students who do not meet state or institutional residency requirements.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received federal Title IV student loans, excluding PLUS and other loans made directly to parents.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV federal aid during the full aid year, grouped by the financial-aid income level of $30,001–$48,000. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for students enrolled in the fall.

Headcount of U.S. nonresident high school students, including men and women, enrolled for college credit during the 12-month reporting period; these students are included in the unduplicated non-degree/non-certificate-seeking enrollment and are generally a subset of that total.

Identifies whether the institution used the old or new classification method to report 12-month enrollment in postbaccalaureate programs. The old method separates master's, doctor's, and first-professional programs, while the new method uses master's, research/scholarship doctorate, professional-practice doctorate, and other doctorate categories, with students formerly in first-professional programs generally reported as graduates.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $48,001–$75,000 income group who received any Title IV federal aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or their institution; private grant sources, loans, and work-study alone are excluded. Applicable to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard calendars that report fall-enrolled students with aid received during the full aid year, and to qualifying private institutions using continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Counts full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received grant or scholarship aid from federal, state or local governments or the institution; students receiving only other grant sources are excluded. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students’ aid for the full aid year, and to public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, clock-hour, or primarily occupational calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.
Average dollar amount of federal, state, local, and institutional grant aid received by full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students.

Combined base salary outlays in dollars for full-time male instructional staff as of November 1, excluding supplements, overloads, bonuses, and additional administrative or other stipends. Covers instructional staff whose function is instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service, excluding medical-school staff and staff working strictly in associated hospitals.

Total dollars of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant or scholarship aid awarded during the full aid year to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received aid from one of those sources; other grant aid sources are excluded. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report on fall-enrolled students, and to public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report on students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Percentage of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted SAT scores, including students who entered in the preceding summer; reported for institutions without an open-admission policy when admission test scores are required.
Indicates whether the institution charges different tuition and required fees for in-district, in-state, or out-of-state students.

Indicates whether the institution offered a certificate program lasting at least one year but less than two years, based on 12-month completions reporting. At the 6-digit CIP level, values are 1 for a program offered and 0 for not offered; 2-digit CIP and grand-total records report the number of such programs offered.

Typical full-year in-state tuition and required fees, in dollars, charged to a full-time student enrolled in a doctor's degree–professional practice Pharmacy (Pharm.D.) program; in-state means meeting the institution's or state's residency requirements.

The 75th-percentile SAT Writing score among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted SAT scores. Reported for institutions without an open-admission policy when at least 60% of enrolled students submitted scores; includes students admitted the prior summer.
Typical full-academic-year tuition and required fees charged to full-time, first-professional law students who meet the institution’s in-state residency requirements; reported in dollars.
Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the fall cohort, including students in bachelor's, associate, vocational, or technical programs.

Total dollars of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $48,001–$75,000 income range who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students’ aid received throughout the full aid year.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $75,001–$110,000 income range who received Title IV aid and paid in-state or in-district tuition. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort over the full aid year.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying the in-state or in-district tuition rate who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid during the full aid year; populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting aid for students enrolled in the fall.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received any federal, state, local, or institutional grant aid.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who were awarded student loans, including Title IV, institutional, and private loans but excluding PLUS and other loans made directly to parents.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV federal student aid and whose EFC-based income fell in the specified range; applicable to public institutions with standard calendar systems reporting fall-enrolled students' aid over the full aid year.

Annual dollar charge used for financial-aid purposes for room and board off campus and not with family, reported for full-time, first-time undergraduate students; room assumes a typical shared accommodation and board covers a specified number of weekly meals.

Average dollars of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid per full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate receiving Title IV aid whose financial-aid income is $48,001–$75,000. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars reporting students over the full 12-month aid period.

Headcount of full-time employees on the institution’s payroll as of November 1 who work in its M.D. and/or D.O. medical school component or a freestanding medical school. Excludes staff working strictly in an associated hospital or in separate health and allied-health schools or departments unless those units are housed within or governed by the medical school.
Average dollar amount of non-Pell federal grant aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students.

Identifies staff by IPEDS/SOC occupation category and institutional full-time or part-time status; classification is based on appointment status at the reporting snapshot, not contract length. Casual employees and College Work-Study students are excluded from the part-time staff category.

Counts full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition whose income used to determine Expected Family Contribution falls in this bracket and who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students who received aid at any time during the full aid year.
Headcount of students enrolled for credit as of the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15 who are not enrolled in any distance education courses.

Headcount of employees working in the medical-school component of a postsecondary institution or in a freestanding medical school, including institution-defined full- and part-time staff but excluding hospital-only employees, health or allied-health school staff, casual employees, and College Work-Study students.

Average dollar amount of student loans received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including Title IV, institutional, and private student loans but excluding parent loans such as PLUS.

Expenses for scholarships and fellowships other than salaries, benefits, and depreciation, including institutional payments to students or third parties for education-related goods or services not provided by the institution; reported net of discounts and allowances. The amount is in dollars.

Average dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $75,001–$110,000 income range who received any Title IV federal student aid. It applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students for the full aid year, and to public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled over the full 12-month aid year.

Indicates whether the institution offers the Yellow Ribbon Program, a voluntary program providing participating veterans and eligible beneficiaries additional institutional aid toward tuition and fees beyond Post-9/11 GI Bill in-state tuition and fee coverage, subject to Department of Veterans Affairs matching limits.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates with income used for financial-aid eligibility of $0–$30,000 who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid. It applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students with aid during the full aid year, and to public or private clock-hour, occupational, continuous-calendar, or program-specific-calendar institutions reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Indicates whether a postbaccalaureate certificate program was offered via distance education for each 6-digit CIP program, including programs with no awards during the 12-month reporting period. For 2-digit CIP categories and the institution grand total, it reports the number of such programs offered rather than a program-level indicator.

Typical full-academic-year out-of-state tuition and required fees, in dollars, for a full-time first-professional student enrolled in a Chiropractic (D.C. or D.C.M.) program. Out-of-state means the student does not meet the state or institution’s residency requirements.

The per-credit-hour tuition charge, in dollars, for part-time undergraduate students who reside in the institution’s local district; the rate may be lower than the in-state rate. Part-time undergraduates take 11 or fewer semester or quarter credits, or fewer than 24 contact hours per week.

For each 6-digit CIP code, indicates whether all associate’s degree programs in that CIP can be completed entirely through distance education (1 = yes, 0 = no), based on programs offered during the 12-month completions period, including programs with zero awards. For 2-digit CIP and institution-total records, the values are aggregate counts of programs offered rather than a yes/no indicator.

Categorical Carnegie classification of institutions based on degree production, research activity, disciplinary focus, and student type, including doctoral, master's, baccalaureate, associate's, special-focus, and tribal-college categories. It is a time-specific institutional classification; research-doctoral thresholds exclude professional-practice doctorates, and the standard doctoral, master's, baccalaureate, and associate's categories exclude special-focus institutions and tribal colleges.

Typical full-academic-year tuition and required fees, in dollars, charged to a full-time first-professional Veterinary Medicine (D.V.M.) student who does not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements.
Average Pell Grant dollars awarded per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate student.

Headcount of students enrolled for credit at the institution’s official fall reporting date (or October 15) whose gender is unknown or identified as another gender, covering undergraduate and graduate students combined; it is not reported by full- or part-time status or by detailed degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate categories.
Published dollar price of tuition and required fees for entering first-time, first-year undergraduate students in the institution’s largest program.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the fall cohort who are not legal residents of the state where they attend the institution.

Average net price in dollars (cost of attendance minus average grant and scholarship aid) for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the specified income band who received Title IV federal aid, including federal grants or loans. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students’ aid for the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-dependent, or contact-hour calendars reporting a 12-month aid cohort; the latter report costs for their largest program length rather than a full academic year.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the fall cohort who pay out-of-state tuition rates.

Headcount of degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including those in vocational or occupational programs; for standard-term institutions it covers enrollment on the official fall reporting date, while for program reporters it is an unduplicated count of students enrolled during the full 12-month reporting period.

12-month unduplicated headcount of men enrolled for credit during the reporting period who are U.S. nonresidents on a temporary visa or otherwise lack the right to remain indefinitely. Permanent resident and other eligible noncitizens are counted in their applicable racial/ethnic categories instead.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received institutional grants, scholarships, or fellowships funded by the institution or its departments.

Average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from families with income of $30,001–$48,000 who received Title IV federal aid, reflecting cost of attendance after grant and scholarship aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall enrollment and the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars reporting a 12-month enrollment period and the full aid year; program-length institutions report the corresponding cost for the largest program.

For two-year-but-less-than-four-year certificate programs reported in the 12-month completions period, this is a distance-education availability indicator: for each 6-digit CIP code, 1 means at least one program can be completed entirely via distance education and 0 means none can. On 2-digit CIP and institution-wide summary records, it is an aggregate count of programs offered rather than a binary indicator.

Combines 9/10-month and 11/12-month contracts into a 9-month-equivalent measure for fringe benefits; the covered count includes both contract groups, while expenditures are combined directly for fixed benefits or converted to a 9-month equivalent for salary-based benefits, with average expenditure equal to total expenditure per covered employee.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the fall cohort who are legal residents of the institution’s locality and therefore eligible for in-district tuition.

Headcount of students enrolled for credit exclusively in distance education courses whose student location is unknown or not reported, as of the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15.

The headcount of full-time, first-time undergraduate students enrolled in degree- or certificate-seeking academic, vocational, or occupational programs, including students with prior-summer attendance or advanced standing. Full-time means at least 12 semester or quarter credits or 24 clock hours per week.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus with family, across all income levels, who received Title IV federal aid during the full aid year. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard term calendars that report on fall enrollment, and for public or private institutions using continuous or program-specific calendars that report on students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Indicates whether the institution offers a doctor’s degree in professional practice, such as medicine, law, dentistry, or veterinary medicine, requiring at least six full-time-equivalent academic years including pre-professional preparation.

Total dollar amount of federal grants and federally sponsored educational assistance received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including Pell Grants, SEOG, veterans' benefits, and other federal aid.

Headcount of cohort students who completed an associate degree or other certificate/award requiring less than four academic years within 150% of the program’s normal completion time. It applies to the specified total, bachelor’s, or other-than-bachelor’s cohorts at four-year institutions and to cohorts at two-year or less-than-two-year institutions.

A flag identifying institutions whose first-time, full-time cohort data in the OM component are inconsistent with corresponding GR200 or GR150 data, or that failed to report completers for specified cohorts or transfer-out students for all cohorts.

Average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from families with income over $110,000 who received Title IV federal aid, calculated as cost of attendance minus average grant and scholarship aid. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars using fall enrollment and a full aid year, and by public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, clock-hour, or primarily occupational programs using a 12-month aid year; program-length institutions report the amount for the largest program.

Count of bachelor's degree-seeking cohort students who left between 150% and 200% of normal program time without graduating or transferring, and were excluded for death or permanent disability, military or active-duty service, qualifying federal foreign-aid service, or an official church mission. Students who returned before the 200% status date may still be included.

Headcount of full-time, non-medical instructional staff as of November 1 whose contracts cover 12 months, including staff performing instruction alone or combined with research and/or public service; excludes medical-school and standalone hospital staff, as well as health or allied-health staff not affiliated with the medical school.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates whose living arrangement is unknown and who received Title IV federal student aid at any time during the full aid year. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report a fall cohort, and for public or private institutions using continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during a 12-month aid period.

Indicates whether a postbaccalaureate certificate program is offered entirely via distance education, where all required coursework can be completed through distance education. At the 6-digit CIP level, values are 1 (offered) or 0 (not offered); 2-digit CIP and grand-total records report the count of such programs, for institutions reporting postbaccalaureate certificate completions in the 12-month period.

Total dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $30,001–$48,000 income category who received Title IV aid and paid in-state or in-district tuition. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year.
Reports the total length of the institution’s third-largest program, measured in clock hours or credit hours.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus and not with family who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid during the full aid year. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students, and to public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Annual dollar amount of required fees charged to full-time, first-time undergraduate students residing in the institution’s local district, reported as part of the full academic-year cost of attendance; this is the in-district fee amount, which may be lower than the in-state rate.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus and not with family, paying in-state or in-district tuition, who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid during the full aid year. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students.

The ACT Composite score at or below which 25% of ACT-reporting first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students fall, including students who first enrolled in the preceding summer; applicable when test scores are required for admission at institutions without an open-admission policy.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received any Title IV federal aid and any grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or their institution; students receiving only private grants, loans, or Federal Work-Study are excluded. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard term calendars reporting a fall cohort and aid received during the full aid year, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-differing, or primarily contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

The in-state tuition charge per credit hour for part-time undergraduate students who meet the state or institution’s residency requirements; undergraduates include students in associate, bachelor’s, or below-baccalaureate vocational or technical programs.

A derived race/ethnicity category for women that combines the Asian and Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander categories under the newer definitions with the combined Asian/Pacific Islander category under the older definition.

Average dollar amount of non-Pell federal grant aid awarded per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate student, including students in bachelor's, associate, vocational, or technical programs.

Headcount of men and women who are nonresident aliens—non-U.S. citizens or nationals temporarily in the country on a visa—enrolled for credit at four-year institutions on the official fall reporting date or October 15; permanent residents are counted in their reported racial/ethnic categories instead.
Dollar amount of discounts and allowances funded by endowments and gifts, including reductions applied to both tuition and fees and auxiliary enterprises.
Average dollar amount of state and local government grants, scholarships, and waivers received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students.

Indicates whether the institution offers for-credit remedial education courses or programs designed to develop the reading, writing, or math skills of students academically underprepared for college-level credit-bearing courses.

Average dollar amount of federal Title IV subsidized and unsubsidized loans received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students; excludes PLUS and other loans made directly to parents.

Total federal grant aid awarded, in dollars, to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates, including federal grants and federally sponsored educational assistance such as Pell Grants, SEOG, veterans’ benefits, and training vouchers.

Headcount of full-time, non-medical instructional staff working under a 9-month contract, as of November 1. Instructional staff include those performing instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service; medical-school and standalone hospital staff are excluded, as are health or allied-health staff unless affiliated with the medical school.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition whose living arrangement is unknown and who received grant or scholarship aid from federal, state or local governments or the institution; students receiving only other grant sources are excluded. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort awarded throughout the full aid year.

Annual dollar amount of required fees charged to full-time, first-time undergraduate students who reside in the institution’s locality (the in-district rate), as used in the financial-aid cost of attendance; this is fees only, separate from in-district tuition.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received any Title IV aid and were awarded federal, state/local, or institutional grant or scholarship aid; students receiving only private/other grants, loans, or Federal Work-Study are excluded. Reported for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard calendars using the fall cohort and full aid year, and for qualifying private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars using a 12-month enrollment and aid period.

Average dollar net price of attendance, after grants and scholarships, for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from families with income below $30,000 who received Title IV federal aid; Title IV aid includes federal grants or loans, while the net-price reduction covers federal, state/local, and institutional grants and scholarships. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard-term calendars that report fall-enrolled students over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report a 12-month aid period; the amount reflects a full academic year or the length of the institution's largest program, as applicable.
Average grant aid in dollars per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate student, including federal, state, local, and institutional grants.
Typical out-of-state required fees charged for a full-time Pharmacy doctoral professional practice student for the full academic year, reported as a dollar amount per student.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received federal grants or federally sponsored educational assistance, including Pell Grants, SEOG, veterans' benefits, and training vouchers.

Average net price in dollars after grant and scholarship aid is subtracted from total cost of attendance for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying the in-state or in-district rate, receiving Title IV aid, and having family income below $30,000; populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students’ aid received during the full aid year.

Total dollar amount of institution- or department-funded scholarships and fellowships awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including awards targeted by factors such as residence, major, or athletics.

Headcount of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted SAT scores, including students who first enrolled in the preceding summer; reported for institutions without an open-admission policy when admission test scores are required.

The SAT Math score at or below which 25% of submitting first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students fall; reported only by institutions without an open-admission policy when test scores are required for admission.

Percentage of the adjusted fall part-time cohort that re-enrolled at the institution in the following fall, either full- or part-time. The cohort consists of first-time degree- or certificate-seeking students (first-time bachelor's or equivalent degree-seeking undergraduates at 4-year institutions), including students first enrolled in the preceding summer; 2-year and less-than-2-year institutions may count students who completed a program before re-enrollment.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received federal grant aid other than Pell Grants, such as SEOG and other federal student aid programs.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received qualifying federal, state, local, or institutional grant or scholarship aid and whose living arrangement is unknown; students receiving only other grant aid are excluded. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students' aid awarded during the full aid year.

Total dollar amount of federal, state, local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students' aid over the full aid year.

Average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students paying the in-state or in-district rate and receiving Title IV federal aid, whose family income is over $110,000; it is the total cost of attendance minus average federal, state/local, and institutional grants and scholarships. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students awarded aid during the full aid year.

Total dollar amount of federal, state or local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, receiving Title IV aid, and whose income used to determine EFC was $75,001–$110,000. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for students enrolled in the fall and awarded aid throughout the full aid year.

Count of full-time, first-time degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $48,001–$75,000 income band who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report on fall enrollees, and to public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or primarily clock-hour calendars that report on students enrolled during the full 12-month aid year.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the specified income range who received Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the full 12-month aid year.

Typical full-year in-state tuition and required fees charged to full-time students enrolled in a podiatry doctor's degree professional practice program; in-state means students meeting the applicable state or institutional residency requirements.

Categorical code for the Carnegie classification of degree-granting, U.S. institutions accredited by a recognized agency, based on their degree offerings and conferral patterns; categories include doctoral/research, master's, baccalaureate, associate's, specialized, and tribal colleges and universities.

Counts bachelor's-level programs for which all required coursework can be completed via distance education, rather than counting degrees awarded. At the 6-digit CIP level it is a program-offered indicator; 2-digit CIP and institution grand-total records report the number of such programs, based on programs with reported bachelor's completions during the 12-month reporting period (including programs with zero awards).

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $30,001–$48,000 income range who received Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

A 5-digit geographic code identifying the metropolitan or micropolitan Core Based Statistical Area associated with the institution’s address. It is not applicable for institutions without an associated CBSA; use CBSATYPE to distinguish metropolitan from micropolitan areas.

Unduplicated 12-month headcount of men enrolled for credit who are nonresident aliens—non-U.S. citizens or nationals temporarily in the United States on a visa; resident aliens and other permanent-status noncitizens are counted in the applicable racial/ethnic categories instead.

Headcount of degree/certificate-seeking cohort members at two-year and less-than-two-year institutions who left between 150% and 200% of normal time without graduating or transferring, due to documented death or permanent disability, military service, qualifying federal foreign-aid service, or an official church mission; students who returned before the 200% status date may still be included.

Headcount of men and women of Asian, Native Hawaiian, or Other Pacific Islander race/ethnicity enrolled for credit during the 12-month reporting period. The derived category combines the newer Asian and Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander categories with the former combined Asian/Pacific Islander category.

Unduplicated headcount of full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students enrolled for credit during the full-year reporting period; each student is counted once regardless of when they enrolled.

Annual on-campus room and board charges in dollars, covering a typical full-time, first-time undergraduate student for the full academic year; room assumes shared accommodation and board covers a specified meal plan.

The per-credit-hour amount charged to part-time graduate students who meet the state or institution’s in-state residency requirements; part-time graduate enrollment is defined as 8 or fewer semester or quarter credits.

Identifies whether the institution reported 12-month enrollment beyond the bachelor's level using the old method, which grouped doctor's and first-professional programs, or the new method, which separates master's, research/scholarship doctorate, professional-practice doctorate, and other doctorate programs and no longer treats first-professional programs as a separate category.

Indicates whether a 12-week-to-less-than-one-year certificate program was offered during the 12-month reporting period, based on completions data; at the 6-digit CIP level, 1 means offered and 0 means not offered (including programs offered with no awards), while 2-digit CIP and grand-total records report the number of programs offered.

Identifies the method used to allocate combined enrollment among separately reported parent and child institutions: faculty/staff FTE proportions, equal shares across the institutions, or proportions submitted by the parent institution.

Average dollar amount of Department of Defense Tuition Assistance Program benefits awarded through the institution to undergraduate student recipients, including eligible spouses or dependents. It covers only benefits known to and awarded or certified through the institution, excluding payments made directly to the institution without institutional reporting.

Annual published tuition and required fees, in dollars, charged to full-time, first-time undergraduate students who meet the institution's in-state residency requirements; it covers the full academic year and is reported for degree-granting institutions, including those using nontraditional academic calendars.
Indicates whether the institution offers recreational or avocational instruction or programs; this is a checkbox-style offering indicator, not a measure of enrollment or program counts.

Headcount of men and women enrolled for credit who are nonresident aliens—non-U.S. citizens or nationals temporarily in the country on a visa without indefinite residency rights—at four-year institutions. Resident aliens and other eligible noncitizens with legal immigrant status are counted in the appropriate racial/ethnic categories instead.

Reports the ACT Composite score at the 75th percentile among score-submitters in the most recent entering group of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including students who began in the prior summer; applicable only to institutions that require admission test scores and do not have an open-admission policy.
Headcount of students in the adjusted cohort who earned a bachelor's degree by the four-year status point; students earning multiple awards are counted by their highest award attained.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from families with income of $0–$30,000 who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid; income is the amount used to determine Expected Family Contribution. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students’ aid over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-differing, or primarily contact-hour/occupational calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received Pell Grants.

Counts master's degree programs for which all required coursework can be completed via distance education, based on programs reported in the 12-month completions data; six-digit CIP records are coded as offered/not offered, while two-digit CIP and institutional grand-total records contain the number of programs offered.

Average annual net price in dollars for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates with family income of $75,001–$110,000 who received Title IV federal aid, calculated as cost of attendance minus average federal, state/local, and institutional grants and scholarships. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars using fall enrollment and full-aid-year aid data, and by public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars using a 12-month aid period; program-length institutions report the cost for their largest program.

12-month unduplicated headcount of women enrolled for credit who are nonresident aliens—non-U.S. citizens or nationals temporarily in the country on a visa without indefinite-residence rights. Resident aliens and other noncitizens admitted as legal immigrants are counted in the applicable racial/ethnic categories instead.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students receiving any student loans or grant/scholarship aid from the federal government, state or local government, or the institution; excludes federal work-study, parent loans, and private or other-source grants.

Headcount of first-time undergraduate degree/certificate-seeking students who graduated from high school within the prior 12 months, including students with prior summer enrollment or advanced standing.

Total dollar amount of Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits received by all student recipients, including eligible spouses and dependents, as known and certified through the institution. Excludes institutional matching aid provided through the Yellow Ribbon Program and benefits not awarded or certified by the institution.

Measures the average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from families with income of $0–30,000 who received Title IV federal aid, calculated as cost of attendance minus average grants and scholarships (not loans). The column applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students with aid received during the full aid year, and to public or private institutions with clock-hour, primarily occupational, continuous, or program-varying calendars that report students enrolled over a 12-month period; program-length institutions report a net price adjusted to the length of their largest program.

Total dollars in Title IV subsidized and unsubsidized federal student loans awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates; excludes PLUS and other loans made directly to parents.

Indicates whether each Associate’s degree program is offered entirely via distance education at the detailed 6-digit CIP level, and counts such programs at 2-digit CIP and institution-total summary levels. A program counts as offered even if it had no awards during the 12-month reporting period; distance education means all required coursework can be completed through distance education courses.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates with unknown living arrangement who pay in-state or in-district tuition and received grant or scholarship aid from the federal, state, or local government or the institution; populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars reporting aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year, excluding students awarded only other grant sources.

Total dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant or scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition within the specified income band; students must have received Title IV federal student aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting aid for a fall cohort over the full aid year.

Headcount of students enrolled for credit exclusively in distance education courses as of the official fall reporting date or October 15, whose location is in the same state or jurisdiction as the institution.

Total dollars in Department of Defense Tuition Assistance benefits awarded through the institution to undergraduate students, including eligible spouses or dependents. It covers only benefits known to and awarded or certified through the institution; payments made directly by the armed service without institutional reporting are excluded.

Code identifying the award level received by completers: short-term certificates, certificates of 12 weeks to less than 1 year, certificates of 1 to less than 4 years, associate’s, bachelor’s, master’s, doctoral, or postbaccalaureate/post-master’s certificates.

Estimated full-academic-year dollar amount for laundry, transportation, entertainment, furnishings, and similar expenses for full-time, first-time undergraduate students living off campus and not with family; excludes tuition and fees, books and supplies, and room and board.

Average dollar amount of federal, state, local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the specified income range who received Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting a fall cohort, and for public or private institutions using continuous or program-specific calendars reporting a 12-month aid-year cohort.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates enrolled in the fall, paying in-state or in-district tuition, who received Title IV federal aid during the full aid year and whose financial-aid income used to determine EFC was below $30,000. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-cohort aid data; income includes parents’ and the student’s adjusted gross income for dependent students, and the student’s adjusted gross income for independent students.

Indicates whether the institution offers a postsecondary award, certificate, or diploma requiring less than 900 clock hours, 30 semester or trimester credit hours, or 45 quarter credit hours. In later collections, the category is retained for institutions offering awards below the baccalaureate level requiring less than 300 clock hours, 9 semester or trimester credit hours, or 13 quarter credit hours, or 300–899 clock hours, 9–29 semester or trimester credit hours, or 13–44 quarter credit hours.
A 3-digit geographic code identifying the Combined Statistical Area associated with an institution’s address; it is not applicable for institutions outside a CSA.

Indicates whether the institution is accredited by a national institutional or specialized/programmatic accrediting agency; multiple agencies may apply. Institutional accreditation covers the institution as a whole, while specialized accreditation covers a program, department, school, or other specialized unit.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving any student loan or grant/scholarship aid from the federal government, state or local government, or the institution; excludes federal work-study, parent loans, and private or other-source grants.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition whose living arrangement is unknown and who received Title IV federal student aid during the full aid year. Populated for public institutions with standard academic calendars that report aid for students enrolled in the fall.
Total dollar amount of state and local grants, scholarships, and waivers received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students.

The median ACT English score among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted ACT scores for admission, including students entering in the preceding summer; reported only by institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

Identifies the student’s enrollment level: undergraduate (including degree/certificate-seeking, first-time, transfer-in, and non-degree/certificate-seeking students), graduate, or first-professional. Undergraduate includes associate’s, bachelor’s, and sub-baccalaureate vocational or technical programs; graduate students hold a bachelor’s or equivalent and study at the post-baccalaureate level, while first-professional students are enrolled in programs such as medicine, law, dentistry, pharmacy, or veterinary medicine.

Reports the institution’s operations and maintenance of plant expenses or deductions in dollars, covering campus grounds and facilities services such as utilities, repairs, security, insurance, and facility management; amounts charged to auxiliary enterprises, hospitals, and independent operations are included. Reporting conventions differ by accounting standard and collection period, so this column may be zero in legacy data when O&M was reported both as a functional and natural category and used as a balancing amount.

Average dollar amount of nonfederal, institutionally or privately sponsored student loans received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates; excludes loans made directly to parents.
Average tuition charged for the full academic year to full-time undergraduate students who do not meet the institution's or state's residency requirements; measured in dollars.

Average dollar amount of Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits awarded through the institution to undergraduate student recipients, including eligible spouses and dependents. Covers only benefits known to and awarded or certified through the institution; benefits not processed by the institution and matching Yellow Ribbon institutional aid are excluded.
Published dollar amount of tuition and required fees charged to entering first-time, first-year undergraduate students in the institution’s largest program.
Reports the full-academic-year dollar amount of published in-state tuition charged to full-time, first-time undergraduate students who meet the institution's or state's residency requirements.

Categorical code identifying the automatic peer-comparison group assigned to an institution for the Data Feedback Report, based on institutional control, Carnegie classification or highest level of offering, enrollment size, geographic region, and program concentration. It is populated for institutions participating in Title IV federal financial aid programs; non-Title IV institutions are not applicable, while certain service schools and institutions in specified U.S. territories or freely associated states were unclassified and generally receive codes of 901 or higher.

Average dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the income category of $110,001 or more who received Title IV aid. It applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard-term calendars reporting a fall cohort and full aid-year aid, and to public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars reporting students enrolled during a 12-month period and aid received throughout the full aid year.

Headcount of female first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who enrolled either full or part time in the most recent fall period, including students who began in the preceding summer and early-decision or early-action enrollees; reported only by institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

Number of students in the specified cohort who did not receive a Pell Grant or Direct Subsidized Loan and completed a bachelor's degree, other bachelor's award, or other credential within 150% of the program's normal completion time. The applicable cohort depends on the institution and award level, including total, bachelor's, and other-than-bachelor's cohorts at four-year institutions and the combined cohort at two-year or less-than-two-year institutions.

Published dollar amount of tuition and required fees charged to full-time, first-time undergraduate students residing in the institution’s local district, for the full academic year; in-district rates may be lower than in-state rates.

Unduplicated 12-month headcount of high school students enrolled in college courses for credit whose race/ethnicity is unknown for both men and women. These students are included in non-degree/non-certificate-seeking enrollment and should be a subset of that total.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $75,001–$110,000 income range who paid in-state or in-district tuition, received any Title IV aid, and received grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or institution. Applicable only to public institutions with standard term calendars reporting aid for a fall cohort over the full aid year; private institutions, nonstandard-calendar institutions, and students receiving only private-source aid, loans, or work-study are excluded.

Unduplicated 12-month headcount of for-credit students reported as gender unknown or another gender, covering undergraduate and graduate students without full-/part-time or detailed degree/certificate-seeking breakdowns; the value is blank when the another-gender count is fewer than 5.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV federal aid during the full aid year, whose income used to determine EFC falls within this income range. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for students enrolled in the fall.

Indicates whether the institution offers adult basic education, remedial instruction, or high school equivalency programs for students beyond compulsory high-school age; it is a program-offering indicator, not an enrollment or headcount measure.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at all income levels who received any Title IV federal student aid, including grants, work-study, or loans. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars for fall-enrolled students receiving aid during the full aid year, and by public or private institutions with continuous, program-differing, or contact-hour-based calendars for students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Measures the total dollar amount of federal, state/local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $30,001–$48,000 income range who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort over the full aid year.

For each 6-digit CIP code, this indicator shows whether the institution offered at least one certificate program of the specified length and all programs in that CIP code could be completed entirely through distance education; zero means no such program was offered. For 2-digit CIP and institution-level total records, it is a count of the qualifying programs, labeled 1-High, rather than a yes/no indicator, and it does not include CIP codes where only some programs can be completed entirely online.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students receiving any financial aid, including grants, loans, scholarships, fellowships, assistantships, tuition waivers or discounts, veterans’ benefits, employer aid, and other non-family support.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates with income of $110,001 or more who received Title IV federal student aid (grants, work-study, or loans). Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars for fall-enrolled cohorts, and by public or private institutions with continuous, clock-hour, or program-based calendars for students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, whose income used for EFC determination was $75,001–$110,000 and who received Title IV aid. Applicable to public institutions with standard term calendars reporting aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.

Headcount of men and women enrolled for credit during the 12-month reporting period who are non-U.S. citizens or nationals temporarily in the United States on a visa; permanent residents and other eligible noncitizens are reported in the applicable racial/ethnic categories instead.

Total dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $0–$30,000 income category who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students’ aid for the full aid year.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving any Title IV federal aid whose financial-aid income used to determine expected family contribution falls in the specified income range. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting a fall cohort and aid received during the full aid year, and to public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific/contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Headcount of women in the nonresident alien cohort: individuals in the United States temporarily on a visa who are not U.S. citizens or nationals and do not have permanent-resident status. Permanent residents and other eligible noncitizens are counted in the applicable racial/ethnic categories instead.

Published dollar amount of in-state tuition charged for the full academic year to full-time, first-time undergraduate students who meet the state or institution’s residency requirements; it covers tuition only, not books, room and board, or other expenses.

Headcount of full-time, non-medical instructional staff as of November 1 whose contracts cover 9, 10, 11, or 12 months; includes staff performing instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service.

Total dollars of qualifying federal, state or local government, and institutional grant or scholarship aid awarded during the full aid year to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received such aid. Applicable only to public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall-enrolled cohort; other grant-aid sources are excluded.

Identifies how combined parent-and-child financial position data (assets and liabilities) were allocated among separately reported institutions: faculty/staff FTE, total revenues, equal shares across institutions, or proportions submitted by the parent institution. Faculty/staff FTE may be based on Employees by Assigned Position or Fall Staff data.

Categorizes postbaccalaureate degree-granting institutions by the breadth and disciplinary concentration of graduate degrees awarded, distinguishing master's, research/scholarship doctoral, professional-practice doctoral, and other doctoral institutions. A single qualifying graduate degree can place an institution in the classification, so institutions with substantial master's or professional programs may be classified according to a modest research-doctoral program; selected research-doctoral categories further distinguish institutions offering human or veterinary medical education.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students receiving nonfederal loans sponsored by the institution or private lenders; excludes loans made directly to parents.

Headcount of women who applied for admission as first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students for the fall period, including early decision, early action, and students who began in the preceding summer. Reported only by institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

A categorical Carnegie classification of an institution’s graduate instructional programs, based on degrees awarded rather than program offerings, including the breadth and disciplinary concentration of master’s, professional-practice/other doctoral, and research doctoral degrees. Any single graduate-level degree qualifies an institution for inclusion; institutions are classified as postbaccalaureate or research-doctoral, with research-doctoral categories also distinguishing medical or veterinary schools where applicable.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received federal grants or federally sponsored educational assistance, including Pell Grants, SEOG, veterans' benefits, and training vouchers.
Average dollar amount of federal, state, local, and institutional grant or educational-assistance aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students.
Total Pell Grant dollars awarded to full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including students in academic, occupational, vocational, or technical programs.
