Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving student loans or grant/scholarship aid from the federal government, state or local government, or the institution; excludes federal work-study, parent loans, and private or other-source grants.

Total dollar amount of federal, state, local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, receiving Title IV aid, and whose income level is $110,001 or more. Populated only for public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students’ aid awarded during the full aid year.
Average tuition charged for the full academic year to full-time undergraduate students who meet the state or institution’s in-state residency requirements, measured in dollars.

Total dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local governments and institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the income category of $110,001 or more who received Title IV aid and paid in-state or in-district tuition. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students and aid awarded throughout the full aid year; the income category is based on the income used to determine the student’s Expected Family Contribution.

Headcount of women admitted for the fall period as first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including full- and part-time students, early decision/action applicants, and those who began in the preceding summer; applicable only to institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

Headcount of women who are U.S. nonresidents (temporary visa holders) and high school students enrolled for college credit during the 12-month reporting period. These students are counted among non-degree/non-certificate-seeking enrollment and should be less than or equal to the total non-degree/non-certificate-seeking headcount.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received nonfederal, institutionally or privately sponsored student loans; excludes loans made directly to parents.

Identifies the U.S. congressional district where the school is located, using the state FIPS code plus a two-digit district code. Code 00 denotes a state with one at-large representative, 98 denotes a U.S. area with a nonvoting delegate, and -2 denotes an entity with no congressional representation.

Categorical Carnegie Basic Classification of the institution, grouping U.S. colleges and universities by their degree offerings, research activity, institutional type, and special-focus or tribal status. It is a time-specific classification snapshot rather than a current-year measure; categories include associate’s, doctorate-granting, master’s, baccalaureate, special-focus, and tribal colleges.

Reports the full-academic-year dollar amount of typical tuition and required fees charged to full-time first-professional Theology students who meet the institution's or state's in-state residency requirements.
Average tuition charged for the full academic year to full-time undergraduate students who do not meet the institution's or state's residency requirements, reported in dollars.
Annual dollar charge for room and board for a typical full-time, first-time undergraduate student living off campus and not with family, based on a shared room and a specified meal plan.

Total dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, receiving Title IV aid, and in the specified income category based on income used to calculate Expected Family Contribution. Populated only for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report fall-enrolled students’ aid awarded throughout the full aid year.

Typical full academic-year tuition and required fees, in dollars, charged to full-time first-professional Veterinary Medicine (D.V.M.) students who meet the institution's in-state residency requirements.

Headcount of women who are nonresident aliens (in the U.S. temporarily on a visa or similar status) and enrolled for credit at the institution's official fall reporting date or October 15; permanent residents and other eligible noncitizens are counted in their appropriate racial/ethnic categories instead.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received nonfederal institutionally or privately sponsored student loans, excluding loans made directly to parents.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the fall cohort whose home state or residence cannot be determined from institutional records.
Typical full-year in-state tuition and required fees, in dollars, for a full-time student enrolled in an institution-defined first-professional program.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus with family who received any Title IV federal student aid during the full aid year. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting on fall enrollees, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour calendars reporting on students enrolled across the 12-month aid period.

Published dollar amount of required fees, excluding tuition, charged to full-time, first-time undergraduate students residing in the locality where they attend; it covers the full academic year and may be lower than the institution’s in-state rate.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, receiving Title IV aid, and whose aid-calculation income is $30,001–$48,000. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report on fall-enrolled students and aid awarded throughout the full aid year.

Annual required fees charged to full-time undergraduate students who do not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements; undergraduates are enrolled in associate, bachelor’s, or below-baccalaureate vocational/technical programs at a full-time course load.

Published in-state tuition charged for the full academic year to full-time, first-time undergraduate students who meet the applicable state or institutional residency requirements; reported as a dollar amount.

Headcount of part-time, first-time undergraduate students enrolled in credit-bearing degree or certificate programs, including associate, bachelor’s, vocational, and technical programs; applicable when the institution enrolls part-time students.

Typical dollar amount of tuition and required fees for a full-time optometry doctoral professional-practice student for the full academic year, charged to students who do not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements.

Headcount of students enrolled for credit exclusively in distance education courses as of the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15; occasional campus visits for orientation, testing, or academic support do not disqualify a course from being classified as distance education.

Percentage of the adjusted fall full-time cohort that re-enrolled at the institution in the following fall, either full- or part-time. The cohort consists of first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates: bachelor's-seeking students at 4-year institutions and degree/certificate-seeking students at 2-year and less-than-2-year institutions; students first enrolled in the preceding summer are included, and qualifying departures are excluded.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received any Title IV federal student aid and a grant or scholarship from the federal government, state or local government, or the institution; private-source grants, loans, and work-study are not counted as qualifying grant aid. Applicable to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions: standard-calendar institutions report fall-enrolled students awarded aid during the full aid year, while continuous or program-specific-calendar institutions report students enrolled during the 12-month reporting period and awarded aid during the full aid year.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received institution- or department-funded scholarships or fellowships, including awards targeted by residence, major, athletics, or other criteria.

Average net price in dollars per student for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received federal, state or local government, or institutional grant or scholarship aid during the full aid year; other grant sources are excluded. It is reported for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled over the 12-month aid period; the amount reflects a full academic year or, for the latter institutions, the length of the largest program.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV federal student aid during the full aid year, categorized by the income used to determine Expected Family Contribution as $110,001 or more. Populated for public institutions with standard academic calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students.

Average yearly net price in dollars (cost of attendance minus grant and scholarship aid) for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving Title IV aid whose family income is $0–$30,000. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars with fall-enrolled aid cohorts, and by public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars for students enrolled during the full aid year; for the latter, it reflects the cost and aid for the institution’s largest program over its program length.

Typical dollar amount of required fees charged for the full academic year to full-time, out-of-state students enrolled in an osteopathic medicine doctor’s professional practice program. Required fees are mandatory charges separate from tuition.
Total institutional-funded scholarships and fellowships, in dollars, awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students.
Average full academic-year tuition charged to full-time graduate students who reside in the institution's local district, where an in-district rate is offered; measured in dollars.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $48,001–$75,000 income range who received any Title IV federal aid during the full aid year, including grants, work-study, or loans. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

A dollar amount combining operating income or loss, net nonoperating revenues or expenses, and, when applicable, the FASB component unit’s change in unrestricted net assets; it includes specified appropriations, investment income, gifts, and plant-debt interest but excludes plant and endowment gifts, capital appropriations, and most investment gains or losses.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the fall cohort who pay out-of-state tuition rates.

Count of students in the cohort who did not receive a Pell Grant or Direct Subsidized Loan and left within 150% of normal time without graduating or transferring, but were excluded because of documented death or permanent disability, military or foreign-aid service, or an official church mission; students who returned before the 150% status date may still be included.

Total contracted work months for full-time women instructional staff as of November 1, measured across 9-, 10-, 11-, and 12-month contracts; covers non-medical instructional staff, including instruction-only or instruction combined with research or public service, and excludes staff in medical-school or standalone medical-school components.
Average dollar amount of non-Pell federal grant aid received per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate student, including grants such as SEOG and excluding Pell grants.
Headcount of full-time men in instructional roles on 9-, 10-, 11-, or 12-month contracts as of November 1, excluding medical-school and other medical staff.

Total dollars of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources awarded during the full aid year to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving Title IV aid whose reported income was 48,001–75,000. Applicable to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students, and to public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Reports the full-academic-year dollar amount of required fees charged to a full-time chiropractic (D.C. or D.C.M.) professional-practice student who does not meet the institution's or state's residency requirements.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received state or local government grants, scholarships, or waivers.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $0–$30,000 income group who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students’ aid over the full aid year.

A status code indicating whether an institution is active in the current year: 1 includes open, newly opened, restored, or currently closing institutions with prior-year data; 2 identifies potential additions or restores; and 3 covers other inactive institutions, including combined, deleted, out-of-scope, or unapproved potential institutions.

Headcount of men and women enrolled for credit on the institution’s official fall reporting date (or October 15) who are U.S. nonresidents—noncitizens or non-nationals present temporarily on a visa without indefinite-residence rights. Applicable to four-year institutions; permanent residents and other eligible noncitizens are included in the appropriate racial/ethnic categories instead.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $48,001–$75,000 income range who received Title IV federal grant aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report a fall cohort, and for applicable private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled over a 12-month aid period; it is not applicable to public institutions.

Indicates whether a master's program is offered for each 6-digit CIP code: 1 means offered and 0 means not offered, including programs with no awards during the 12-month reporting period. For 2-digit CIP categories and the institution grand total, it reports the count of master's programs offered rather than a binary indicator.

Indicates whether the institution offers for-credit continuing professional education programs or courses for individuals who have completed a professional degree, such as law, medicine, dentistry, or social work, and seek additional training in that field.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition at all income levels, among those awarded Title IV federal student aid. Populated for public institutions with standard calendar systems that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $30,001–$48,000 income range who paid in-state or in-district tuition, received any Title IV federal aid, and received grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or the institution. Applicable to public institutions with standard calendar systems that report aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year; excludes private institutions, nonstandard calendar systems, and aid from private or other sources.

The 75th-percentile ACT English score among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted ACT scores, including students who first attended in the prior summer. Reported for institutions without an open-admission policy when ACT scores are required for admission and at least 60% of these enrolled students submitted scores.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded during the full aid year to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received such aid; applies to public institutions with standard calendar systems reporting fall-enrolled students and aid for the full year, and excludes other grant-aid sources.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $48,001–$75,000 income group who paid the in-state or in-district tuition rate and received any Title IV federal aid plus grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or institution. Applicable only to public institutions with standard-term calendars that report fall-enrolled students' aid received during the full aid year.

The number of Direct Subsidized Loan recipients who did not receive Pell Grants and completed their bachelor's degree, other degree, or certificate within 150% of the program's normal completion time. The applicable cohort varies by institution and program type, including total, bachelor's, other-than-bachelor's, and two-year or less-than-two-year cohorts.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who lived in institution-controlled on-campus housing and received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan during the full aid year. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars for fall-enrolled cohorts, and by public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour calendars for students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Identifies which cohort the record represents: full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking entrants overall; the bachelor's-or-equivalent subcohort; the other degree/certificate-seeking subcohort at four-year institutions; or the overall degree/certificate-seeking cohort at two-year and less-than-two-year institutions. Students are undergraduates with no prior postsecondary experience, enrolled full time (typically at least 12 credits or 24 contact hours per week).
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the fall cohort who are legal residents of the state where they attend the institution.

Average base salary in dollars for full-time male instructional staff on 11-month contracts, measured as of November 1; excludes medical-school staff and supplements, overloads, bonuses, and stipends for other responsibilities.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded per full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate paying in-state or in-district tuition and receiving Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year.

The per-credit-hour tuition charge for part-time graduate students who reside in the institution’s locality, which may be lower than the in-state rate; part-time graduate enrollment is defined as 8 or fewer semester or quarter credits.

Indicates whether at least one certificate program lasting one year but less than two years within a six-digit CIP code can be completed entirely via distance education, based on programs reported for the institution’s 12-month completions period; for six-digit CIP records, 1 means offered and 0 means not offered. For two-digit CIP and institution-total records, the value is an aggregate count of programs offered rather than a binary flag.

Total dollar amount of federal, state, local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received Title IV aid and whose financial-aid income level is at least $110,001. It applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students with aid awarded during the full aid year, and to public or private institutions using clock-hour, continuous, or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Percentage of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted SAT scores, for institutions without an open-admission policy; covers the most recent admissions cohort, including students admitted the preceding summer.

Indicates whether all master’s programs within a 6-digit CIP code can be completed entirely through distance education, based on programs reported in the 12-month completions period; a program is counted as offered even if it awarded no degrees. At 6-digit CIP records, 1 means offered and 0 means not offered; 2-digit CIP and institution-total records aggregate the counts of programs offered rather than serving as simple yes/no indicators.

Total dollar amount of federal, state/local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at the in-state or in-district tuition rate, across all income levels, who received Title IV aid; populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting aid for fall enrollees over the full aid year.

Total base salary outlays, excluding supplements, overloads, bonuses, and additional administrative or other stipends, for full-time, non-medical instructional staff on 10-month contracts as of November 1. Instructional staff perform instruction only or instruction combined with research and/or public service; medical-school and standalone hospital staff are excluded, as are health or allied-health staff unless affiliated with the medical school.

Indicates whether a postbaccalaureate certificate program is offered, based on the institution reporting the program at the 6-digit CIP level, even if no awards were granted during the 12-month reporting period. Values are program offered or not offered for 6-digit CIP records, while 2-digit and grand-total records report the count of programs offered.

Unduplicated headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the full-year cohort who pay out-of-state tuition rates, meaning they are not legal residents of the state where they attend.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received Title IV federal grant aid and fall-enrolled students during the full aid year, within the specified income range. Populated for public institutions using standard term calendars (semester, quarter, trimester, or 4-1-4) that report fall-cohort financial aid data.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received any Title IV federal aid and were awarded grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or the institution; students receiving only private grants, loans, or work-study are excluded. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students with aid during the full aid year, and to public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Typical dollar amount of required fees charged for the full academic year to a full-time in-state dentistry doctor's professional practice student; required fees are mandatory charges separate from tuition.

Headcount of men enrolled for credit who are classified as Hispanic or Latino under the newer definition or Hispanic under the older definition, reported as of the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15.
Average full academic-year tuition charged to full-time undergraduate students who meet the applicable state or institutional residency requirements, reported in dollars.

Total dollar amount of federal, state, local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $30,001–$48,000 income range who pay in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report aid for students enrolled in the fall and awarded throughout the full aid year.

Number of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students of unknown gender who enrolled full or part time in the fall, including students who began in the preceding summer; includes early decision and early action students. Populated for institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

An unduplicated 12-month headcount of women enrolled for credit who are U.S. nonresidents—noncitizens or non-nationals present temporarily on a visa without indefinite-residency rights. These individuals are reported in the nonresident category rather than a racial/ethnic category; eligible permanent-resident noncitizens are included in the appropriate racial/ethnic categories.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $110,001-or-more income group who received Title IV aid. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students' aid over the full aid year, and to public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled over a 12-month aid period.

Average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying the in-state or in-district rate who received Title IV federal aid and whose reported family income was over $110,000. It reflects total cost of attendance minus average federal, state/local, and institutional grant or scholarship aid, and applies to public institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students' aid over the full aid year.

The 75th-percentile SAT I Math score among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students at institutions with non-open admission that require test scores and where at least 60% of enrolled students submitted SAT/ACT scores, including students admitted the preceding summer.
Typical required fees for a full-time doctor's professional practice student who does not meet the institution's or state's residency requirements, reported for the full academic year.

Counts full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at all income levels who received any Title IV federal aid, including grants, work-study, or loans, during the full aid year. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars and reporting on fall enrollment, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars and reporting enrollment over a 12-month period.
Identifies the contracted teaching period for faculty: less than 9/10 months, 9/10 months, or 11/12 months (full year).

Total dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $0–$30,000 income group who received Title IV federal student aid. Populated for private nonprofit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students with aid awarded during the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Headcount of students in the revised cohort who received neither a Pell grant nor a subsidized Stafford loan and were excluded from completion/transfer outcomes because they left within 150% of normal time due to death or permanent disability, military or federal foreign-aid service, or an official church mission; students who returned before the status date may still be included.

Total base-salary outlays in dollars for full-time male instructional staff on 12-month contracts, measured as of November 1; covers non-medical staff whose duties are instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service, excluding supplements, overloads, bonuses, and administrative stipends.

Total dollars of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $75,001–$110,000 income group who received Title IV aid. It applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report a fall cohort with aid over the full aid year, and to public or private institutions using clock-hour, primarily occupational, continuous, or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during the 12-month aid period; income is based on the financial aid office’s measure used to determine Expected Family Contribution.

Count of full-time, first-time degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduates who received any Title IV federal aid and whose income level was $110,001 or more. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students, and to public or private institutions with continuous or program-differing calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid year.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living in institution-owned or controlled on-campus housing who received federal, state or local government or institutional grant or scholarship aid during the full aid year; excludes students receiving only other grant sources. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report a fall cohort, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or primarily clock-hour calendars that report a 12-month enrollment period.

Indicates whether graduation-rate race/ethnicity data were reported using the new categories, the old categories, or a mixture of both; nonresident alien and race/ethnicity unknown are included in either method.

Average dollar net price (cost of attendance minus average federal, state, local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid) for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received such aid during the full aid year; grants from other sources are excluded. It is reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-cohort aid data, and by public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour/occupational calendars; the amount reflects a full academic year or the length of the institution’s largest program, as applicable.

Number of subsidized Stafford Loan recipients who did not receive Pell Grants and completed a bachelor's degree or equivalent within 150% of normal completion time at four-year institutions; the cohort may be total, bachelor's, or other-than-bachelor's as specified by PSGRTYPE.

Headcount of students enrolled for credit on the institution’s official fall reporting date (or October 15) who are non-U.S. citizens or nationals temporarily present on a visa; resident aliens and other permanent-status noncitizens are counted in the appropriate racial/ethnic categories instead.

Average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving federal, state or local government, or institutional grant or scholarship aid, based on the full cost of attendance less that aid. It applies to public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year and use the in-state or in-district tuition rate.
Annual dollar amount of mandatory fees, excluding tuition, charged to full-time veterinary medicine doctoral professional practice students who are not state or institutional residents.
Number of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received nonfederal, institutionally or privately sponsored loans; excludes loans made directly to parents.

Flags 2-year institutions where the first-time, full-time cohort’s OM six-year award completers are fewer than the corresponding GR200 completers within 150% of normal time, even though the longer OM period should produce at least as many completers.
Annual tuition and required fees charged in dollars to a full-time first-professional student classified as out of state, as defined by the institution.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition whose living arrangement is unknown and who received Title IV federal aid, across all income levels; populated for public institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students' aid received during the full aid year.

Indicates whether the institution enrolls students in doctor's degree–professional practice programs, such as medicine, dentistry, law, pharmacy, veterinary medicine, or other listed professional programs requiring at least six full-time-equivalent years of preparation.

Headcount of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who enrolled full time in the fall cohort and whose gender is unknown; includes students who began in the preceding summer and applies to institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

Total dollar amount of Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits awarded through the institution to undergraduate student recipients, including eligible spouses and dependents. It includes only benefits known to and awarded or certified by the institution, excludes benefits processed elsewhere and Yellow Ribbon institutional aid, and may cover tuition and fees, books and supplies, and housing.

Count of women classified as U.S. nonresidents (temporary visa holders without indefinite-residency rights) who are enrolled for credit at four-year institutions on the official fall reporting date or October 15. Permanent residents and other eligible noncitizens are reported in the applicable racial/ethnic categories instead.
Total dollar amount of federal, state, local-government, and institutional grant aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students.

Annual out-of-state required fees, in dollars, for a full-time first-professional veterinary medicine student. Required fees are mandatory charges beyond tuition; the amount applies to students who do not meet state or institutional residency requirements.

Average net price in dollars after grants and scholarships for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving Title IV federal aid, limited to students from families with income of $75,001–$110,000. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars using fall-enrolled students, and by public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour calendars using students enrolled during the full 12-month aid year; program-length institutions report the cost for their largest program.

Average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying the in-state or in-district rate, whose family income is $75,001–$110,000 and who received Title IV federal aid, calculated as total cost of attendance minus average grant and scholarship aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students' aid received during the full aid year.

Aggregate dollar amount of federal, state/local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition and receiving Title IV federal student aid. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.
Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students awarded federal Title IV subsidized or unsubsidized loans; excludes PLUS and other loans made directly to parents.

Dollar amount of other federal grant aid recorded as discounts and allowances against tuition and fees, excluding matching portions; private not-for-profit institutions generally report these amounts when the aid is applied to student accounts.

The typical dollar amount of required fees for a full-time law doctoral professional-practice student paying out-of-state rates for the full academic year. Required fees are mandatory fixed charges beyond tuition.

Indicates whether a bachelor's program is offered at the six-digit CIP level (1 = offered, 0 = not offered), based on the institution reporting the program in the 12-month completions data even if no degrees were awarded; two-digit CIP and grand-total records instead contain the count of programs offered.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received Pell grants.
Indicates whether the institution is a land-grant college or university designated by a state legislature or Congress under the Morrill Acts.

Total dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, in the $110,001-or-more income group, who received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort across the full aid year.

Total grant and scholarship aid, in dollars, from federal, state or local, and institutional sources for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, receiving Title IV aid, and whose aid-determined income is $110,000 or more. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort over the full aid year.

Count of full-time, first-time degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduates in the specified income band used to determine Expected Family Contribution who received any Title IV aid, including grants, work-study, or loans. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting a fall cohort, and to public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, clock-hour, or primarily occupational programs reporting a 12-month enrollment cohort; aid may have been awarded at any time during the full aid year.

Count of students excluded from the degree/certificate-seeking cohort because they left within 150% of normal time without graduating or transferring, for documented reasons such as death or permanent disability, military or federal foreign-aid service, or an official church mission. Students who returned before the 150% status date may still be included.

Headcount of full-time women in non-medical instructional roles—teaching alone or combined with research and/or public service—who are on 12-month contracts, measured as of November 1; medical-school and standalone hospital staff are excluded.

Number of Direct Subsidized Loan recipients who did not receive Pell Grants and completed an award requiring less than four academic years within 150% of the institution’s normal completion time; reported for the applicable total, bachelor’s, or other-than-bachelor’s cohorts at four-year institutions and for the cohort at two-year or less-than-two-year institutions.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded during the full aid year to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received such aid; applies to public institutions with standard term calendars reporting aid for fall-enrolled students.

Total dollar amount of nonfederal, institutionally or privately sponsored student loans awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates; excludes loans made directly to parents.
Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the fall cohort who pay in-district tuition rates.
Reports the total length of the institution’s sixth-largest program, expressed in either clock hours or credit hours.
Headcount of White, non-Hispanic men enrolled for credit at four-year institutions on the official fall reporting date or October 15.

Headcount of staff classified as nonresident aliens: non-U.S. citizens or nationals in the country temporarily on a visa and without permanent-residency status. It excludes resident aliens admitted as legal immigrants for permanent resident status.
Unduplicated headcount of full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the full-year cohort; each student is counted once during the reporting period.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition and receiving any Title IV aid, in the $110,001-or-more family-income group. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report a fall cohort and aid received throughout the full aid year.

Total dollar amount of grants and scholarships from federal, state or local, and institutional sources received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the specified income range who received Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates whose living arrangement is unknown, who pay in-state or in-district tuition and received federal, state/local, or institutional grant or scholarship aid (excluding students receiving only other grant aid). Populated for public institutions with standard calendar systems reporting aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year.

Headcount of nonresident aliens: people who are not U.S. citizens or nationals and are in the country temporarily on a visa without indefinite-residence rights. Resident aliens and other eligible noncitizens admitted for permanent-resident status are counted in the applicable racial/ethnic categories instead.

Indicates whether the institution enrolls full-time graduate students, excluding students in doctor's degree–professional practice programs; full-time generally means at least 9 semester or quarter credits or institution-defined full-time thesis/dissertation enrollment.

Identifies the cohort-status category being reported, such as normal time to completion, bachelor’s-degree cohort, completers within 150% of normal time, total transfer-out non-completers, excluded students, or non-completers still enrolled in long programs. Transfer-outs are students who left without completing and enrolled at another eligible institution; exclusions include deaths or permanent disability and qualifying military, foreign-aid, or church-mission service.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the graduation-rate cohort who are U.S. nonresidents—noncitizens or nonnationals in the country temporarily or on a visa; eligible noncitizens admitted for permanent residence are reported in their applicable racial/ethnic category instead.

A headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus and not with family who received grant or scholarship aid from federal, state, or local governments or the institution; students receiving only other grant aid are excluded. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars using a fall cohort and full aid-year reporting, and by public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars using a 12-month enrollment period and full aid-year reporting.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students awarded federal Title IV subsidized or unsubsidized student loans; excludes PLUS and other loans made directly to parents.

Identifies faculty personnel positions, excluding graduate, instructional, and research assistants, by tenure or contract status. Categories include tenure-track, not on tenure track, multi-year contract, annual contract, and less-than-annual contract positions.

Categorizes full-time new hires by their institution-assigned primary occupational activity, including faculty, executive/administrative/managerial, graduate assistants, other professional, technical/paraprofessional, and clerical/secretarial staff. It covers people hired into full-time permanent employment for the first time or after a break in service during the reporting period, excluding returns from sabbatical leave.

Average dollar cost of books and supplies for a typical full-time, first-time undergraduate student over the institution’s full academic period, including institutions with nontraditional calendar systems.

Published out-of-state tuition and required fees, in dollars, for full-time, first-time undergraduate students for the full academic year; out-of-state students do not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements. The measure applies to institutions using an academic-year calendar, including other nontraditional academic calendar systems.

Average dollar amount of federal Title IV subsidized and unsubsidized student loans awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates; excludes PLUS and other loans made directly to parents.

Average net price, in dollars, for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying the in-state or in-district rate, in the $48,001–$75,000 income range, who received Title IV federal aid. It covers public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort over the full aid year; net price is total cost of attendance minus federal, state/local, and institutional grants and scholarships.
The number of employees in archivist, curator, and museum technician; librarian; library technician; and academic affairs and other education services occupations.

Typical full-academic-year tuition and required fees, in dollars, charged to full-time students in a Dentistry (D.D.S. or D.M.D.) doctor's professional practice program who meet the institution's or state's in-state residency requirements.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the full-year cohort who pay in-state tuition rates, among the unduplicated cohort.

Headcount of male U.S. nonresidents in the cohort—people in the country temporarily on a visa without indefinite residence rights; eligible noncitizens admitted for permanent residence are reported in the applicable racial/ethnic categories instead.

An institution-level categorical code identifying the highest degree level offered, derived from the detailed level-of-offering fields; it also includes codes for other offerings and for institutions with no applicable reported offering.

Published out-of-state tuition and required fees for full-time, first-time undergraduate students for the full academic year; out-of-state means students who do not meet the institution's or state's residency requirements. Applies to institutions reporting an academic-year price of attendance, including degree-granting institutions with traditional or other academic calendar systems.
Average full-academic-year tuition charged to full-time undergraduate students who reside in the institution’s local district; measured in dollars per student.

Headcount of undergraduate students enrolled for credit who are not seeking a degree or recognized postsecondary credential, including high school students taking credit-bearing courses. For standard-term institutions, it covers students enrolled on the official fall reporting date; for nonstandard-term/program reporters, it is an unduplicated count of students enrolled throughout the full 12-month reporting period.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students paying the in-state or in-district tuition rate who received any Title IV federal student aid during the full aid year. Populated for public institutions with standard calendar systems that report aid for students enrolled in the fall.

The SAT Math score at or below which 75% of submitted scores fall, reported for first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students at institutions without an open-admission policy that require admission test scores; includes students entering in the preceding summer.
Typical dollar amount of required fees charged for the full academic year to a full-time, in-state theology first-professional student. Required fees are mandatory charges separate from tuition.

Identifies whether the student is undergraduate, first-professional, or graduate level. Undergraduates include students in bachelor’s, associate’s, or sub-baccalaureate degree or certificate programs, including those with a prior bachelor’s taking undergraduate courses for credit; first-professional covers specified professional degree programs, while graduate covers post-baccalaureate study.

Estimated annual dollar amount for full-time, first-time undergraduate students living off campus with family, covering expenses such as transportation, laundry, entertainment, and furnishings; tuition and fees, room and board, and books and supplies are excluded. It applies to the full academic year, including institutions using nontraditional academic calendar systems.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the full-year cohort who pay out-of-state tuition rates, meaning they are not legal residents of the state where they attend.

Headcount of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students of another gender who applied, were admitted, and enrolled part time in the most recent fall period, including eligible early decision, early action, and prior-summer entrants. Applies to institutions without an open-admission policy; the value is blank when the institution cannot report another-gender students and zero when it can report them but none enrolled.

Indicates how an institution uses standardized or special admissions test scores (such as SAT or ACT) when selecting entering first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students: required, recommended, neither, or unknown. Populated for institutions without an open-admission policy for this population.
A three-digit geographic code identifying the Combined Statistical Area associated with an institution’s address. It is not applicable for institutions that are not located in a CSA.
Reports student FTE for enrollment in doctor's degree–professional practice programs, including fields such as medicine, dentistry, law, pharmacy, and veterinary medicine.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV federal student aid during the full aid year, grouped in the $110,001-or-more income level used to determine Expected Family Contribution. Populated for public institutions with standard term-based calendar systems reporting fall-enrolled students and aid awarded throughout the full aid year.

Categorizes unduplicated enrollment headcount by undergraduate or graduate level, with undergraduate students further identified as degree/certificate-seeking or non-degree-seeking and degree-seeking students classified as first-time, transfer-in, or continuing; undergraduate counts also distinguish full-time from part-time status. Degree/certificate-seeking excludes high school students taking postsecondary courses for credit, and graduate students are those with a bachelor’s degree or higher taking postbaccalaureate courses.

Headcount of men in the cohort classified as Asian, Native Hawaiian, or Other Pacific Islander, using a derived combination of the newer Asian and Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander categories with the former Asian or Pacific Islander category.

Average dollar amount of Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits received per student recipient, including eligible spouses and dependents; reflects only benefits awarded or certified through the institution and known to it, and excludes Yellow Ribbon institutional aid and matching funds.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the full-year cohort who pay in-state tuition rates.
Measures the total length of the institution’s fifth-largest program, reported in either clock hours or credit hours.

Indicates whether TOEFL results are required, recommended, neither required nor recommended, or unknown in selecting entering first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at institutions without an open-admission policy.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received Pell grants.

Typical dollar amount of required fees charged for the full academic year to a full-time, in-state doctor's professional practice student in Pharmacy. In-state means the student meets the state's or institution's residency requirements; required fees are mandatory fixed charges generally assessed to students in addition to tuition.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living in institution-owned or controlled on-campus housing, charged the in-state or in-district tuition rate, and receiving federal, state, local, or institutional grant or scholarship aid (excluding students receiving only other grant sources). Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in this income bracket who received any Title IV aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or institution; excludes students receiving only private grants, loans, or work-study. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students' aid over the full aid year, and for eligible private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars reporting students enrolled over the 12-month aid period.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received any Title IV federal student aid and any grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state or local government, or the institution; aid from private or other sources, loans, and Federal Work-Study alone are excluded. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard calendars reporting fall-enrolled students’ aid over the full aid year, and to public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Headcount of awards/degrees conferred to men identifying as Asian, Native Hawaiian, or Other Pacific Islander, using the combined current categories or the comparable Asian/Pacific Islander category under the former definition.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus with family who received any Title IV aid during the full aid year. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report on fall enrollees, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour/occupational calendars that report on a 12-month enrollment period.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $48,001–$75,000 income range who paid in-state or in-district tuition, received any Title IV aid, and received grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or the institution. Applicable to public institutions with standard calendar systems that report aid for a fall cohort over the full aid year; private and for-profit institutions and continuous or program-length calendars are not covered.

Average dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state/local, or institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the specified income range who received Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or clock-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $48,001–$75,000 income range who received any Title IV aid and were awarded federal, state/local, or institutional grant or scholarship aid; private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions only, using fall enrollment with full-year aid reporting under standard calendars or 12-month enrollment and aid reporting under continuous or otherwise nonstandard private-institution calendars.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received Title IV aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or institution, for the income category based on the income used to determine Expected Family Contribution (0–30,000); excludes students receiving only private grants, loans, or Federal Work-Study. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report fall-enrolled students’ aid for the full aid year.

Counts full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates whose living arrangement is unknown and who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid during the full aid year. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report a fall cohort, and for public or private institutions using continuous or program-specific calendars that report a 12-month enrollment period.

Typical annual in-state required fees, in dollars, for a full-time podiatry doctor's professional practice student who meets the institution's or state's residency requirements. Required fees are mandatory fixed charges separate from tuition.

Average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying the in-state or in-district rate, in the $48,001–$75,000 income group, who received Title IV federal aid. This column applies to public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year.
Annual dollar amount of required fees, excluding tuition, charged to a full-time first-professional veterinary medicine student who meets the institution’s or state’s in-state residency requirements.

Number of all students reported by the institution as receiving Department of Defense Tuition Assistance Program benefits, including eligible servicemembers and potentially their spouses or dependents; excludes benefits not awarded or certified through the institution.

Average base salary in dollars for full-time male instructional staff on 12-month contracts, excluding medical-school staff; includes staff whose function is instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service, and excludes supplements, overloads, bonuses, and administrative stipends.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the fall cohort who pay in-district tuition rates.
Typical annual tuition and required fees charged in-state to a full-time first-professional dentistry student, reported in dollars for the institution's full academic year.

Annual dollar charge for on-campus room and board used by the financial aid office for a typical full-time, first-time undergraduate, including a shared room and a specified meal plan; it applies to full-academic-year attendance, including institutions with nontraditional academic calendars.
Average dollar amount of state and local government grants, scholarships, or waivers awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students.

Average dollar amount of Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits received by undergraduate student recipients, including eligible spouses and dependents; covers only benefits awarded or certified through the institution and known to it, and excludes matching institutional aid from the Yellow Ribbon Program.

Average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from families with income of $48,001–$75,000 who received Title IV federal aid (grants or loans); it is the cost of attendance minus average grant and scholarship aid. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars using fall enrollees, and by public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, clock-hour, or primarily occupational programs using students enrolled during the 12-month aid period; the cost basis is either the full academic year or the institution’s largest program length.

Headcount of Hispanic or Latino/Hispanic men and women enrolled for credit during the 12-month period, combining the current and former Hispanic ethnicity categories. Enrollment is reported as of the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15.

Typical full academic-year tuition and required fees charged to a full-time first-professional dentistry student (D.D.S. or D.M.D.) who does not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements; amounts may be assessed per term, course, or credit.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received per full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate at all income levels who received Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard-term calendars reporting a fall cohort over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid year.

Categorical Carnegie classification of an institution’s sector and academic/research profile, including doctoral, master’s, baccalaureate, associate’s, special-focus, and tribal-college categories. It is a time-specific snapshot based primarily on the institution’s degrees awarded, research activity, disciplinary focus, and student type; it is not a headcount or percentage.

Total men and women classified as Asian, Native Hawaiian, or Other Pacific Islander, combining the separate Asian and Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander categories with the older combined Asian/Pacific Islander classification.

Headcount of full-time male instructional staff, excluding medical staff, classified by contract length (9, 10, 11, or 12 months versus less than 9 months) as of November 1. Instructional staff perform instruction alone or combined with research and/or public service; medical-school staff and staff working strictly in associated hospitals are excluded.

Total dollar amount of federal, state/local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at all income levels who received any Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report a fall cohort with aid received throughout the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Headcount of full-time, non-medical instructional staff on 9-, 10-, 11-, or 12-month contracts, as of November 1. Instructional staff perform instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service; staff in medical-school components or freestanding medical schools are excluded, while hospital-only and affiliated health or allied-health staff are not included unless they fall under the medical school.

Average dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, whose household income used for Expected Family Contribution determination is $30,001–$48,000 and who received any Title IV federal student aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort over the full aid year.

Indicates whether each 6-digit CIP doctoral research/scholarship program can be completed entirely through distance education (1 = offered, 0 = not offered). For 2-digit CIP categories and the institutional grand total, it reports the count of such programs rather than a binary indicator, including programs with no awards during the 12-month reporting period.

Categorical Carnegie classification of an institution’s undergraduate instructional program, distinguishing associate’s-only and associate’s-dominant institutions from bachelor’s institutions by the share of bachelor’s majors in arts and sciences versus professional fields and by the extent of graduate-degree coexistence in corresponding fields (none, some, or high).

Operating expenses in dollars for maintaining campus grounds and facilities used for educational and general purposes. It is distinct from total student-services expenses, which cover admissions, registrar activities, student activities, counseling, financial aid administration, and related student support.

Fall headcount of men and women enrolled for credit who are American Indian or Alaska Native, combining the old and new race/ethnicity definitions; enrollment is measured at the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received Title IV federal aid during the full aid year and whose aid-calculation income was $110,001 or more. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars reporting aid for a fall cohort.

Indicates whether a 1-year but less than 2-year certificate program is offered entirely via distance education, recorded as 1 (offered) or 0 (not offered) for each 6-digit CIP code and award level; it can be 1 even when no awards were granted. The 2-digit CIP and institution grand-total records report the count of such programs rather than a binary indicator.

Average base salary in dollars for full-time, non-medical instructional staff whose contracts cover 11 months, including staff performing instruction alone or combined with research and/or public service. It excludes supplements, overloads, bonuses, and additional administrative or other stipends.

A derived coded selection flag identifying institutions currently in the IPEDS universe that are open to the public, participate in Title IV, and are primarily postsecondary; codes distinguish operating and degree-granting categories, while code 9 indicates an inactive institution. The four U.S. service academies are included under code 1 despite their deferment-only status.

Measures total undergraduate credit-hour activity attempted across all credit-bearing courses during the 12-month period, calculated from course credits multiplied by enrollment at the institution’s census date.

Indicates the number of 2-year but less than 4-year certificate programs offered, based on the institution’s 12-month completions reporting. At the 6-digit CIP level it is coded 1 for a program offered and 0 for not offered; 2-digit CIP and institution grand-total records contain the count of offered programs.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received during the full aid year by aid recipients among full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition. Applies only to public institutions with standard term calendars that report financial aid for fall-enrolled students.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at all income levels who received any Title IV federal aid during the full aid year. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report on fall enrollment, and for public or private institutions using continuous or program-differing calendars that report on enrollment across the full 12-month aid period.

Annual dollar amount of published in-state required fees charged to full-time, first-time undergraduate students for the full academic year; it covers students meeting the applicable state or institutional residency requirements and excludes tuition.

Indicates whether the institution offers recreational or avocational instructional programs for personal interest or leisure that do not lead to postsecondary credit, a formal award or degree, or occupationally specific skills.

Headcount of part-time employees on the institution’s payroll as of November 1, excluding casual employees and College Work-Study students. Covers staff employed by or working in the M.D. or D.O. medical school component, including affiliated health or allied health units, but excludes hospital-only staff and unaffiliated dentistry, veterinary medicine, nursing, or dental hygiene staff.

Total dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at all income levels who received Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard term calendars that report fall enrollment with aid awarded during the full aid year, and for public or private institutions using continuous or program-specific calendars that report enrollment over the 12-month aid period.

Headcount of male full-time, non-medical instructional staff whose contract covers 10 months, measured as of November 1. Instructional staff perform instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service; medical-school and standalone hospital staff are excluded.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates with income of $110,001 or more who received any Title IV federal student aid, including grants, work-study, or loans; income is the amount used to determine Expected Family Contribution. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report a fall cohort with aid received during the full aid year, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Total dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received Title IV aid; it is not an average or percentage. Applicable to private nonprofit and for-profit institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students over the full aid year, and to public or private institutions with continuous, contact-hour, or program-specific calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received student loans, including Title IV, institutional, and private loans but excluding PLUS and other loans made directly to parents.

Total dollar amount of Department of Defense Tuition Assistance benefits received by undergraduate students, including eligible spouses or dependents. It includes only benefits awarded or certified through the institution and known to the institution; payments not processed through the institution are excluded.

Categorical code classifying an institution's physical location on the urban-to-rural continuum, from large city through suburb and town to rural, based on Census geography. Institutions in American Samoa, the Northern Mariana Islands, Guam, and the Virgin Islands are not assigned a code.

Counts full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus with family who received grant or scholarship aid from federal, state, or local governments or the institution; students receiving only other types of grant aid are excluded. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars with fall-based aid reporting, and by public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, clock-hour, or primarily occupational calendars with 12-month aid reporting.

A five-digit code identifying the Core Based Statistical Area associated with the institution's address; it is not applicable when the institution is not associated with a CBSA. Use CBSATYPE to distinguish metropolitan from micropolitan statistical areas.

Indicates how a non-open-admission institution uses formal demonstrations of competency—such as portfolios, certificates of mastery, or assessment instruments—in selecting entering first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students: required for admission, considered if submitted but not required, or not considered.

The typical full-academic-year required fees, excluding tuition, charged to full-time veterinary medicine doctoral professional-practice students who meet the institution's or state's in-state residency requirements.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid and lived off campus without family. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students, and for public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled over the full 12-month aid year.
Percentage of all unduplicated undergraduate students enrolled for credit during the full-year reporting period who were full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking students.

A 5-digit code identifying the Core Based Statistical Area associated with the institution’s address; it is -2 when the institution is not associated with a CBSA. Use CBSATYPE to distinguish metropolitan from micropolitan areas.

Annual out-of-state required fees in dollars for a full-time first-professional chiropractic student; required fees are mandatory charges beyond tuition for students who do not meet state or institutional residency requirements.
Average dollar amount of state and local government grants, scholarships, and waivers received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students.

Identifies the method used to allocate combined graduation-rate data among separately reported parent and child institutions: student FTE, faculty/staff FTE, or a proportion submitted by the parent institution.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree- or certificate-seeking students in the fall cohort, including students first enrolled in the preceding summer or with unknown intent; at four-year institutions, this is limited to bachelor’s degree-seeking students. For standard-term institutions the cohort is defined at the official fall reporting date (or October 15), while institutions with continuous enrollment and a full-year cohort use students enrolled from August 1 through October 31.

Average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the specified income range who received Title IV aid, calculated as cost of attendance minus average grant and scholarship aid (excluding loans). Populated for private nonprofit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students for the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report a 12-month aid-year population; the amount reflects a full academic year or the length of the institution’s largest program, respectively.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $0–$30,000 income level who received Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students' aid over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-differing, or specified contact-hour/occupational calendars that report students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Total base-salary outlays, excluding supplements, overloads, bonuses, and additional administrative or other stipends, for full-time women instructional staff on 11-month contracts as of November 1.
