Covers non-medical staff whose duties are instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service; excludes staff employed in medical-school or standalone medical components, but not necessarily health or allied-health units unless affiliated with the medical school.

Classifies full-time new hires by IPEDS occupational category; instructional staff are additionally identified by faculty status and tenure status. New hires are individuals hired for full-time permanent employment for the first time or after a break in service between July 1 and September 30, excluding employees returning from sabbatical leave.
Name of the institution’s system, governing board, or corporate entity, where applicable.

Indicates whether a post-master’s certificate program is offered for each 6-digit CIP code, based on programs reported in the 12-month completions period; a program with no awards can still be reported as offered. At 2-digit CIP and institution-total levels, it is the count of post-master’s certificate programs offered.

Headcount of for-credit students enrolled exclusively in distance education courses who are located in the United States but in a different state or jurisdiction from the institution, measured as of the official fall reporting date or October 15.
Typical full-academic-year tuition and required fees, in dollars, charged to a full-time first-professional law student who does not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements.
Indicates that the institution reports none of the listed library resources or services as provided.

Headcount of for-credit students enrolled in at least one, but not all, distance education courses as of the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15. Distance education uses technology to deliver instruction to students separated from the instructor with regular and substantive interaction; occasional campus attendance for orientation, testing, or support does not disqualify a course.

The per-credit-hour tuition charge for in-state, part-time undergraduate students, meaning those enrolled below the full-time threshold (11 or fewer semester or quarter credits, or fewer than 24 clock hours per week).

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates whose living arrangement is unknown and who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid during the full aid year. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars based on fall enrollment, and for public or private institutions with continuous or program-length calendars based on enrollment over the 12-month aid year.

Published dollar amount of tuition and required fees charged for the full academic year to full-time, first-time undergraduate students residing in the institution's local district; this in-district rate may be lower than the in-state rate and applies to degree-granting institutions, including those with nontraditional academic calendars.

Headcount of women who are nonresident aliens—non-U.S. citizens or nationals temporarily in the country on a visa—enrolled for credit at the institution on its official fall reporting date or October 15.

Average dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state, local, or institutional sources received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $0–$30,000 income level who received any Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Categorizes faculty instructional staff by tenure status, contract type, and academic rank (professor, associate professor, assistant professor, instructor, lecturer, or no academic rank). Faculty are those whose principal activity includes instruction, research, or public service; graduate, instructional, and research assistants are excluded.

Total dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, whose aid-eligibility income was $75,001–$110,000 and who received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students' aid over the full aid year.
Measures total contact hours of coursework completed by undergraduates in occupational programs during the 12-month reporting period, calculated from the hours each student completed.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students awarded federal grant aid other than Pell Grants; the denominator is all students in this population.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV aid and federal, state/local, or institutional grant or scholarship aid, with family income used for Expected Family Contribution in the $75,001–$110,000 range; private-source grants, loans, and Federal Work-Study without qualifying grant aid are excluded. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort over the full aid year.

Count of subsidized Stafford Loan recipients who did not receive Pell Grants and were excluded from the 150%-of-normal-time cohort because they left for documented reasons such as death or permanent disability, military service, federal foreign-aid service, or an official church mission; students who returned before the status date may still be included.

Categorical Carnegie classification of an institution based on its degree production, research activity, disciplinary focus, and student characteristics, including doctoral, master’s, baccalaureate, associate’s, baccalaureate/associate’s, special-focus, and tribal-college categories. It is a time-specific institutional snapshot; the main degree-based categories generally exclude special-focus institutions and tribal colleges, which are classified separately.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received Title IV federal aid during the full aid year and whose financial-aid income used to calculate EFC was $0–$30,000. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall-enrolled cohort.

Total base-salary outlays, in dollars, for full-time male instructional staff on 10-month contracts, covering instruction or instruction combined with research and/or public service. Excludes supplements, overloads, bonuses, administrative stipends, and staff employed in medical-school components or standalone medical schools.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $0–$30,000 income group who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year.

The SAT I Verbal score at or below which 75% of submitting first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students scored; populated for institutions without open admission when SAT/ACT scores are required and at least 60% of this entering group submitted scores.

Total dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state/local, or institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received Title IV aid and whose financial-aid income level was $0–$30,000. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard-term calendars reporting fall enrollees for the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or clock-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Headcount of undergraduates enrolled for credit who are full-time and first-time at the undergraduate level, seeking a degree or certificate, measured at the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15.

Quality-control flag identifying institutions with aggregated unknown enrollment of at least 70 that reported zero transfer-out students across all four OM cohorts (first-time and non-first-time, full-time and part-time) despite reporting transfer-out data in the applicable GR 150 survey.

Indicates whether the institution offers the Yellow Ribbon Program, which provides participating veterans and eligible beneficiaries additional institutional aid toward tuition and fees beyond Post-9/11 GI Bill in-state tuition and fee coverage, with matching support from the Department of Veterans Affairs.

Categorical NCES-created comparison-group assignment for institutions participating in Title IV federal aid programs, used when an institution did not provide its own group. Groups are based on degree-granting status, institutional control, institution category, Carnegie classification, enrollment size, largest program for many nondegree institutions, and special categories such as tribal colleges, U.S. service institutions, and other jurisdictions; distance-learning-only institutions may be grouped separately or by Carnegie classification depending on the reporting cycle.

Fall headcount of men enrolled for credit who are nonresident aliens—temporary visa holders without indefinite U.S. residence rights; resident aliens and other permanent-status noncitizens are included in the appropriate racial/ethnic categories instead.

Total base-salary outlays, excluding supplements, overloads, bonuses, and extra-duty stipends, for full-time male instructional staff on 9-month contracts as of November 1. Instructional staff perform instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service; medical-school staff are excluded, but staff in affiliated health or allied-health units are included.

Headcount of Pell Grant recipients in the selected cohort—total, bachelor's, or other-than-bachelor's—who completed a bachelor's degree within 150% of the program's normal completion time; reported for four-year institutions.

Percentage of all undergraduates represented by the unduplicated full-year cohort of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students; the denominator includes all undergraduates regardless of enrollment status or credential-seeking status.
Indicates whether the institution requires all full-time, first-time undergraduate degree/certificate-seeking students to live on campus or in institutionally controlled housing.

Categorical indicator identifying the cohort or subcohort status being reported, such as normal-time completion, completion within 150% of normal time, bachelor’s-degree cohort, or transfer-out noncompleters. Transfer-out counts exclude students who left because of death or permanent disability, military or qualifying federal service, or official church missions.

For each bachelor's-level 6-digit CIP code, this indicates whether at least one program can be completed entirely via distance education: 1 means yes and 0 means no, based on programs reported in the 12-month completions collection (including programs with no awards). In 2-digit CIP and institution-total records, the field instead reports the total number of programs offered.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received any federal, state, local-government, or institutional grant aid.

Categorical classification of an institution’s undergraduate instructional program, based on the levels and fields of undergraduate degrees awarded and the extent to which graduate degrees overlap those fields; it distinguishes arts and sciences, professional, career and technical, and mixed undergraduate emphases and reflects a time-specific snapshot rather than an assessment of quality.

Indicates whether the institution has its own library or financially supports a shared library with another postsecondary institution; a library is an organized collection of print, microform, or audiovisual materials with accessible equipment and staff, including qualifying learning resource center units.

Binary indicator of whether at least one post-master's certificate program within a 6-digit CIP code can be completed entirely through distance education: 1 means offered and 0 means not offered. For 2-digit CIP and institution-total records, values are aggregate counts of programs offered rather than a 0/1 indicator; it covers programs reported in the 12-month completions period, including programs with no awards.

Estimated dollar amount for on-campus expenses such as laundry, transportation, entertainment, and furnishings, excluding tuition and fees, books and supplies, and room and board, for full-time, first-time undergraduate students over the full academic year.

Counts full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the specified family-income bracket who received any Title IV aid, including grants, work-study, or loans; income is the amount used to determine Expected Family Contribution. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard-term calendars that report fall-enrolled students receiving aid during the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

The per-credit-hour tuition charge, in dollars, for part-time undergraduate students who reside in the institution’s local service area; the institution may set this in-district rate below its in-state rate. Part-time undergraduates are enrolled in 11 or fewer semester or quarter credits, or fewer than 24 clock hours per week.
Average Pell Grant aid in dollars per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate student receiving Pell aid.

Annual tuition and required fees charged to full-time students in osteopathic medicine professional-practice programs who do not meet the institution's or state's residency requirements; reported in dollars for the full academic year.

Number of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate applicants who received an official offer of admission for the most recent fall period, including early decision, early action, and students who began in the preceding summer. Applies only to institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates; admitted students may enroll either full or part time.

Annual dollar amount of required fees charged to a full-time, first-professional law student who does not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements; required fees are mandatory fixed charges generally paid by nearly all students.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying the in-state or in-district tuition rate who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid, with income used to determine EFC between $30,001 and $48,000. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for the fall cohort across the full aid year.

Indicates whether the institution recognized an additional or decreased pension expense, pension liability or asset, or related deferral from implementing GASB Statement 68 for one or more defined-benefit pension plans. Primarily applies to public institutions; institutions without a defined-benefit plan or whose system, parent institution, branch, or other entity reports the pension impact instead should be reported as No.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received per student across all income levels, among full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV federal student aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall-enrolled cohort over the full aid year.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the fall cohort whose residence or tuition-rate status is unknown because the institution cannot determine their home state or residence.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition whose aid-eligibility income was in the 0–30,000 range and who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid. Populated for public institutions using standard term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort over the full aid year.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates awarded nonfederal institutionally or privately sponsored student loans, excluding loans made directly to parents.

Aggregate dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition and receiving Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.

Average dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $110,001-or-more income group who received Title IV aid. It applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall enrollment and full-year aid, and to public or private institutions with continuous, program-based, or clock-hour calendars reporting a 12-month enrollment period and full-year aid.

Headcount of students classified as nonresident aliens—non-U.S. citizens or nationals in the country temporarily on a visa without indefinite residence rights; resident aliens and other permanent or legally admitted noncitizens are reported in the applicable racial/ethnic categories instead.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the full-year cohort who pay in-district tuition rates, where in-district means legal residents of the locality served by the institution and eligible for reduced tuition.

Total dollars in federal, state, local, or institutional grants and scholarships awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received Title IV aid and whose financial-aid income falls between $30,001 and $48,000. Populated for private nonprofit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall enrollment and the full aid year, and for public or private institutions using continuous or program-specific calendars reporting a 12-month enrollment period.

Counts full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students paying in-state or in-district tuition, with income used for EFC of $110,001 or more, who received any Title IV aid and a grant or scholarship from the federal government, state/local government, or institution; students receiving only private grants, loans, or Federal Work-Study are excluded. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report fall-enrolled students' aid received during the full aid year.

Total dollar amount of federal, state, local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received across all income levels by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition and receiving Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year.

Aggregate dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition and receiving any Title IV aid, whose household income is $110,001 or more. Populated only for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort over the full aid year.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from families with income of $110,001 or more who received Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled over the full 12-month aid year.

Indicates whether a post-master’s certificate program is offered by 6-digit CIP code (1 = offered, including when no awards were granted; 0 = not offered); 2-digit CIP and grand-total records instead report the count of programs offered.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received student loans, including Title IV, institutional, and private loans where the student is the borrower, but excluding PLUS and other parent loans.

Average dollar amount of Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits awarded through the institution per student recipient, including eligible spouses and dependents. It covers only benefits known to and awarded or certified by the institution, excludes Yellow Ribbon institutional aid, and does not include benefits paid without institutional involvement.

Headcount of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students submitting ACT scores, including students who first enrolled in the prior summer and those with advanced standing; reported for institutions without an open-admission policy when admission requires test scores.

Average dollar amount of Department of Defense Tuition Assistance benefits received by graduate students, including eligible spouses or dependents; reflects only benefits awarded or certified through the institution and known to it, paid directly by the servicemember’s Armed Service.
Count of students in the adjusted cohort who received Direct Subsidized Loans but no Pell Grant and completed an award within 150% of the program’s normal completion time.
Average dollar cost of books and supplies for a full academic year or program for full-time, first-time undergraduate students.

Percentage of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students submitting SAT scores, reported for institutions without an open-admission policy when SAT scores are required and at least 60% of this student population submitted scores.

Identifies the method used to allocate combined student financial aid across parent and child institutions: student FTE proportions, faculty/staff FTE proportions, equal shares among institutions, or proportions submitted by the parent institution.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at all income levels who received any Title IV aid. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars for students enrolled in the fall and tracked through the full aid year, and by public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars for students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates whose living arrangement is unknown, who pay the in-state or in-district tuition rate and received federal, state, local, or institutional grant or scholarship aid (excluding students receiving only other grant aid). Populated only for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students who received aid during the full aid year.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV federal aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or the institution; private-source grants, loans, and work-study without qualifying grant aid are excluded. Populated for public institutions with standard calendar systems that report aid for a fall cohort over the full aid year.

Total credit-hour activity generated by graduate students over the institution’s 12-month reporting period, measured as attempted course credits multiplied by enrollment in each course and summed across credit-hour courses.

Published dollar amount of required fees for the full academic year, charged to full-time, first-time undergraduate students who do not meet the institution's or state's residency requirements; required fees are mandatory charges separate from tuition.
Fall headcount of men enrolled for credit who are classified as Asian, Native Hawaiian, or Other Pacific Islander, using the combined race/ethnicity definition.
Average Pell Grant dollars awarded per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate student.
Indicates whether the institution offers occupational programs designed to provide knowledge and skills for a specific occupation, potentially leading to a certificate, degree, or other formal award.

Average dollars of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate in the $0–$30,000 income group who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. This column applies only to public institutions with standard term calendars reporting aid for a fall cohort over the full aid year.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus and not with family who received grant or scholarship aid from federal, state, or local governments or the institution; students receiving only other grant sources are excluded. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars using fall-enrolled cohorts, and by public or private institutions with clock-hour, primarily occupational, continuous, or program-varying calendars using a 12-month enrollment period.

Total institutional-funded scholarship and fellowship dollars awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates, including awards targeted by factors such as residence, major, or athletics.

Typical annual in-state required fees, in dollars, charged beyond tuition to full-time students in doctor's professional practice programs who meet the state's or institution's residency requirements.

Headcount of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students enrolled part time, using the institution’s part-time threshold (11 or fewer semester/quarter credits or fewer than 24 clock hours per week).

Categorizes entering undergraduate students into four groups based on full-time versus part-time status and first-time versus non-first-time status. Full-time means at least 12 semester/quarter credits or 24 contact hours per week; first-time students have no prior postsecondary experience, while non-first-time students have prior postsecondary experience, and the entering period is fall-term or full-year depending on the institution’s reporting system.

Headcount of Hispanic or Latino/Hispanic women enrolled for credit on the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15; this derived measure combines the current Hispanic or Latino and former Hispanic race/ethnicity categories.

Total revenue in dollars received from private, non-governmental entities through grants and contracts for research, training, other programs, or general institutional operations, including amounts covering direct and indirect expenses.

Headcount of students in the revised cohort whose known gender is neither Men nor Women and who were therefore allocated to the binary gender categories. The cell is blank when the institution could not report another gender, and zero when it could report it but had no such students.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving grant or scholarship aid from federal, state, local, or institutional sources; students receiving only other grant sources are excluded. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard calendars reporting fall-enrolled students aided during the full aid year, and to public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Identifies the student enrollment level and status: undergraduate degree/certificate-seeking, undergraduate non-degree-seeking, or graduate. Undergraduate includes students in associate's, bachelor's, or sub-baccalaureate vocational/technical programs; graduate means postbaccalaureate-level students who hold at least a bachelor's degree.

Number of cohort students who did not receive a Pell grant or subsidized Stafford loan and completed a bachelor's, associate's, or certificate award within 150% of the program's normal completion time. The cohort may be total, bachelor's, or other-than-bachelor's for four-year institutions, or the applicable cohort for two-year and less-than-two-year institutions.
Total dollar amount of state and local government grants, scholarships, and waivers awarded to full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates whose living arrangement is unknown and who received grant or scholarship aid from federal, state, or local governments or the institution; students receiving only other grant sources are excluded. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students for the full aid year, and to public or private institutions using continuous, program-differing, or primarily contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Headcount of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate applicants who were admitted and enrolled full time in the most recent fall period, including eligible summer entrants and early decision/action students, and whose gender was reported as neither men nor women. The value is blank when the institution could not report another-gender data; it is zero when reporting was possible but no students identified as another gender.
Indicates whether the institution requires all full-time, first-time undergraduate degree/certificate-seeking students to live on campus or in institutionally controlled housing.

Indicator of whether the institution operates a hospital, inferred from reported hospital revenues or hospital-service expenses in finance data; student health services clinics are not treated as hospital activity.

Indicates whether a certificate program under 300 clock hours or 9 semester/trimester (13 quarter) credit hours is offered, based on the 12-month completions reporting period; at the 6-digit CIP level, 1 means offered and 0 means not offered, including programs with no awards. At the 2-digit CIP and institution-total levels, it is a count of the offered programs in that category or institution.

Measures the total dollar amount of federal, state/local, and institutional grants and scholarships received by full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduates in the specified income band who received Title IV aid. It applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students’ aid for the full aid year, and to public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Average net price, in dollars, for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying the in-state or in-district rate who received federal, state, local, or institutional grant or scholarship aid during the full aid year; it is total cost of attendance minus that average grant aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students and full-year financial aid.

Total dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition and receiving Title IV federal aid, aggregated across all income levels. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received Pell grants.

Count of male first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students officially admitted for the most recent fall period, including early decision, early action, and students who began in the preceding summer; populated only for institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living in institution-owned or controlled on-campus housing who received federal, state, local, or institutional grant or scholarship aid; students receiving only other grant aid are excluded. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students with aid received during the full aid year, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Headcount of male nonresident aliens enrolled for credit at four-year institutions, reported as of the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15; nonresident aliens are temporary visa holders, while permanent resident and other eligible noncitizens are included in the appropriate racial/ethnic categories.
Indicates whether the institution is part of a multi-institution system, a governing board, or a corporate structure with administrative oversight or control.

The net book value of an institution’s depreciable capital assets after accumulated depreciation, reported in dollars. It covers tangible and intangible operational assets with useful lives beyond one year, such as land improvements, buildings, equipment, infrastructure, capital-lease property, software, and similar assets, but excludes assets held in endowment funds or other capital-fund real-estate investments.

For each six-digit CIP program, indicates whether a doctor's-degree-other program is offered (1) or not offered (0), including programs with no awards; at two-digit CIP and institution grand-total records, reports the number of such programs offered.

Average dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid awarded per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate in the $0–$30,000 income group who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV federal student aid. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.
Headcount of students in the adjusted cohort who received subsidized Stafford Loans but no Pell Grant and completed an award within 150% of the institution's normal program completion time.

Categorizes enrollment records by student level (undergraduate or graduate), full- or part-time status, and, for undergraduates, degree/certificate-seeking versus non-degree-seeking status. Degree-seeking undergraduates are further classified as first-time, transfer-in, or continuing students; the categories use standard credit- or clock-hour definitions of full- and part-time enrollment.
Indicates whether the institution offers an academic library resource consisting of an organized collection of printed materials, with trained staff, scheduled services, and supporting facilities.
Count of full-time, first-time undergraduate degree/certificate-seeking students awarded state or local government grants, scholarships, or waivers.
Typical dollar amount of tuition and required fees charged for a full-time first-professional chiropractic student who qualifies for in-state residency, for the full academic year.

Headcount of employees on the institution’s payroll at the November 1 snapshot, reported by full- or part-time status, occupational function, and faculty and tenure status; casual workers and College Work-Study students are excluded, as are graduate, instructional, and research assistants from the faculty category.

Average base salary in dollars for full-time, non-medical instructional staff who are women and work under 10-month contracts, covering instruction or instruction combined with research and/or public service. It excludes supplements, overloads, bonuses, and additional administrative or other stipends.

Estimated dollar amount for miscellaneous on-campus expenses such as transportation, laundry, entertainment, and furnishings, excluding tuition and fees, books and supplies, and room and board. It applies to full-time, first-time undergraduate students for the full academic year, based on the amount used by the financial aid office for aid eligibility.

Headcount of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate men enrolled part time in the fall, including students who began in the preceding summer and those admitted through early decision or early action. Reported for institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus with family, paying in-state or in-district tuition, and receiving any Title IV federal student aid, across all income levels; populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year.

Indicates whether the institution's academic library offers staff trained to provide and interpret library materials. It is a yes/no library resource or service indicator, not a headcount or measure of staff size.
Count of students enrolled for credit during the 12-month period who took at least one distance education course but were not enrolled exclusively in distance education courses.

Total dollars in federal student loans awarded directly to degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including Title IV and specified health-profession loans but excluding PLUS loans and other federal loans not made directly to the student.
Unduplicated headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the full-year cohort whose home state or residence—and therefore tuition-rate status—is unknown.

Count of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students of another gender who were admitted for the most recent fall period, including early-decision, early-action, and prior-summer entrants, regardless of full- or part-time enrollment; applies only to institutions without an open-admission policy. The value is blank when the institution cannot report this gender category, and zero when it can report it but no such students were admitted.

Indicates whether the institution offered a two-year, but less than four-year, certificate program in a given six-digit CIP category during the 12-month completions period: 1 means offered and 0 means not offered. For two-digit CIP categories and the institution grand total, it reports the count of such programs offered rather than a binary indicator.

Headcount of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who applied, were admitted, and enrolled full time in the fall period, including early decision/action students and those who began in the preceding summer; applicable to institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

Average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates with income of $30,001–$48,000 who received Title IV federal aid, calculated as average cost of attendance minus average federal, state/local, or institutional grants and scholarships. It applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students, and to public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report a full 12-month aid period; the amount reflects a full academic year or the length of the institution’s largest program, respectively.

Binary indicator for a 6-digit CIP code showing whether at least one postbaccalaureate certificate program can be completed entirely through distance education; 1 means yes and 0 means no, including when the program is offered but awarded no certificates. On 2-digit CIP and institution-total records, the values are aggregate indicators of whether any programs are offered, rather than this program-level distance-education status.

Average dollar net price per full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate in the $0–30,000 income group who received Title IV federal aid, calculated as cost of attendance minus average federal, state/local, or institutional grants and scholarships. Reported for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars using fall enrollment and the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour/occupational calendars using a 12-month aid period; the latter report a program-length cost of attendance.

NCES-assigned category used to form automatic IPEDS Data Feedback Report comparison groups for institutions participating in Title IV federal aid programs. Groups are based on degree-granting status, control, Carnegie classification or highest degree offered, enrollment size, geographic region, locale, largest program, and special institutional types such as tribal, distance-learning, service, and other-jurisdiction institutions.

Indicates whether at least one associate’s program within a 6-digit CIP code can be completed entirely through distance education, based on the institution’s 12-month completions reporting; at the detailed CIP level, 1 means offered and 0 means not offered, even if no awards were granted. For 2-digit CIP and institution-total records, the value is the aggregated number of programs offered rather than a binary indicator.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received state or local government grants, scholarships, or waivers.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, in the $30,001–$48,000 income group, who received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students’ aid over the full aid year.

Headcount of undergraduate students receiving Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits, including eligible spouses and dependents, based only on benefits known to and awarded or certified through the institution. Yellow Ribbon institutional matching aid is excluded.

Total dollars in federal Title IV subsidized and unsubsidized student loans received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students; excludes PLUS and other loans made directly to parents.

Average dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local governments or institutional sources received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $75,001–$110,000 income group who received Title IV federal student aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid year.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received federal grant aid other than Pell Grants, including programs such as SEOG and eligible federal training grants.
Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received Pell Grants; this is a headcount, not a percentage or dollar amount.

Counts full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition whose income used for financial-aid eligibility was $0–$30,000 and who received Title IV federal aid (grants, work-study, or loans). Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant and scholarship aid for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, receiving Title IV aid, and whose aid-office-determined income is $75,001–$110,000; populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students’ aid over the full aid year.

Published dollar amount of tuition and required fees charged for the full academic year to full-time, first-time undergraduate students residing in the institution's local district; in-district tuition may be lower than the institution's in-state rate.
Annual dollar amount of required fees charged to full-time graduate students who reside in the locality where they attend the institution (in-district).

Indicates whether the institution offers undergraduate courses or programs through distance education, using technology to deliver instruction to students separated from the instructor with regular and substantive interaction; undergraduate includes associate's, bachelor's, and sub-baccalaureate vocational or technical programs.

Headcount of cohort students who received neither a Pell Grant nor a Direct Subsidized (formerly subsidized Stafford) Loan and completed an award within 150% of the program’s normal completion time. It covers total, bachelor’s, and other-than-bachelor’s cohorts at four-year institutions, and the cohort at two-year or less-than-two-year institutions.

Average dollar amount of Department of Defense Tuition Assistance benefits received by all student recipients, including eligible spouses or dependents; it covers only benefits known to and awarded or certified through the institution, not payments made outside the institution.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded during the full aid year to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received such aid; other grant sources are excluded. Populated for public institutions with standard calendar systems that report fall-enrolled students and aid awarded throughout the full aid year.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received Title IV federal aid and whose income used to determine EFC was $0–$30,000; reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars for fall-enrolled students receiving aid during the full aid year, and by public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars for students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded across all income levels to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students and aid awarded throughout the full aid year.

Average dollar amount of federal, state, local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, receiving any Title IV aid, and whose aid-office income is $48,001–$75,000. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.
Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received any federal, state, local, or institutional grant aid.

Percentage of the initial full-time cohort, excluding deaths, permanent disabilities, military or foreign-aid service, and official church missions, that re-enrolled at the institution as either full- or part-time students in the following fall. The cohort comprises first-time, full-time bachelor's or equivalent degree-seeking undergraduates at four-year institutions and first-time degree- or certificate-seeking students at two-year and less-than-two-year institutions; preceding-summer entrants are included, and prior program completers count among re-enrollees at two-year and less-than-two-year institutions.

Identifies the enrollment category for each institution’s students: undergraduate or graduate level, full- or part-time status, and—within undergraduate enrollment—degree/certificate-seeking versus non-degree-seeking status. Degree-seeking undergraduates are further classified as first-time, transfer-in, or continuing students; full-time and part-time thresholds differ for undergraduate and graduate students.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from families with income of $110,001 or more who received Title IV federal grant aid during the full aid year. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions: standard-calendar institutions use the fall cohort, while eligible private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars use students enrolled during the institution’s 12-month reporting period.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $110,001-or-more income category who received any Title IV aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or institution; students receiving only private/other grants, loans, or work-study are excluded. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard calendars reporting fall-enrolled students’ aid over the full aid year, and for eligible private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the financial aid cohort. For standard-term institutions it reflects enrollment as of the official fall reporting date; for nonstandard-term program reporters, it is an unduplicated cohort enrolled during the full 12-month aid year.
Average tuition charged for the full academic year to full-time graduate students who meet the institution's or state's in-state residency requirements, reported in dollars.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $75,001–$110,000 income range who paid in-state or in-district tuition, received any Title IV aid, and received grant or scholarship aid from federal, state/local, or institutional sources. Applicable to public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students' aid for the full aid year; excludes private institutions, nonstandard calendars, and aid from private or other sources.

Total dollars of federal, state/local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $75,001–$110,000 income group who received Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic terms that report fall-enrolled students for the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled over the full 12-month aid year.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus (not with family), paying in-state or in-district tuition, and receiving federal, state, local, or institutional grant or scholarship aid; excludes students receiving only other grant aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort awarded throughout the full aid year.

Headcount of women of Asian, Native Hawaiian, or Other Pacific Islander origin enrolled for credit on the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15; this derived measure combines the newer Asian and Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander categories with the older Asian or Pacific Islander category.

The typical full-academic-year tuition and required fees, in dollars, charged to a full-time first-professional podiatry student who meets the institution's or state's in-state residency requirements.

Average dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state, local, or institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $75,001–$110,000 income group who received Title IV federal student aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students’ aid over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-based, or contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period; income is the amount used to determine the student’s Expected Family Contribution.

Total dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the specified income range who received Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students, and for public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period; the income range is based on the income used to determine Expected Family Contribution.

A categorical classification of an institution’s undergraduate population based on fall part-time/full-time enrollment, first-year student academic preparation and selectivity, and the share of entering undergraduates who are transfers. Categories distinguish associate’s-degree-granting institutions from bachelor’s-degree-granting institutions and, for four-year institutions, inclusive versus selective or more selective profiles and lower versus higher transfer-in levels.

Counts full-time, first-time undergraduate students seeking a degree or certificate who received institution- or department-funded scholarships or fellowships, including awards targeted by residence, major, athletics, or other criteria.

Interest expense incurred on debt allocated to independent operations—activities unrelated to the institution’s primary missions, generally including major federally funded research and development centers and related IT, plant operations, and depreciation costs. It excludes interest associated with operations owned and managed as endowment investments.

SAT Writing score at the 75th percentile for first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students whose admission requires test scores. Applies to institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates; the score reflects the most recent available entering group, including students admitted in the preceding summer.

Counts full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates with an unknown living arrangement who received grant or scholarship aid from federal, state, local, or institutional sources; students receiving only other grant aid are excluded. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars using fall enrollment and full-year aid data, and by public or private institutions with clock-hour, primarily occupational, continuous, or program-specific calendars using 12-month enrollment and full-year aid data.

Average dollar amount of Department of Defense Tuition Assistance benefits awarded through the institution to graduate-student recipients, including eligible spouses or dependents; it excludes benefits not awarded or certified through the institution.

Average dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, receiving Title IV aid, and whose financial-aid income is $48,001–$75,000. Populated for public institutions with standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students’ aid over the full aid year.

A flag identifying 4-year institutions whose first-time, full-time cohort outcome data are inconsistent with their bachelor's degree-seeking cohort data, despite reporting only a bachelor's cohort and no associate degrees or certificates below the bachelor's level; cohort and 6- and 8-year completer counts should otherwise match across the surveys.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $0–$30,000 income range who received any Title IV aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or institution; private-source grants, loans, and work-study alone are excluded. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard calendars that report fall-enrolled students over the full aid year, and for eligible private institutions using continuous or program-specific calendars that report a 12-month enrollment period over the full aid year.

Indicates whether an Associate's degree program is offered, based on 12-month completions reporting: 1 means offered and 0 means not offered at the 6-digit CIP level. At 2-digit CIP and institution grand-total levels, it reports the total number of Associate's programs offered, or 0 if none.

SAT Critical Reading score at or below which 25% of score-submitting first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students fall; applies to institutions without open admission policies that require admission test scores.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the fall cohort who are not legal residents of the state where they attend the institution.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $0–$30,000 income range who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions using a standard term calendar that report aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year.

Headcount of men in the cohort who are nonresident aliens on a temporary visa or without indefinite U.S. residency; resident aliens and other eligible noncitizens with legal immigrant status are reported in the applicable racial/ethnic categories instead.

Identifies the institution’s predominant calendar system. Standard-term systems (semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, or other academic) imply fall-cohort graduation-rate data and full academic-year student-charge data, while program-based or continuous systems imply full-year-cohort graduation-rate data and student charges reported by program.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates with income of $0–$30,000 who received any Title IV federal aid, including grants, work-study, or loans. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report a fall cohort with aid awarded during the full aid year, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, clock-hour, or primarily occupational programs that report students enrolled during a 12-month period with aid awarded during the full aid year.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received federal student loans, including Title IV subsidized and unsubsidized loans but excluding parent loans such as PLUS.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $0–$30,000 income group who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received any Title IV aid; populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars reporting fall enrollment and aid received during the full aid year.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates whose living arrangement is unknown and who received federal, state, local, or institutional grant or scholarship aid; students receiving only other grant aid are excluded. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid year.

A headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the specified income bracket who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid during the full aid year. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard term calendars that report on fall enrollees, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report on students enrolled during the 12-month aid period; income is the amount used to determine Expected Family Contribution, including the applicable parent and/or student income.

Average dollar amount of nonfederal, institutionally or privately sponsored loan aid received per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate student receiving this aid; excludes loans made directly to parents.

Count of graduate students known to the institution who received Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits, including eligible spouses or dependents. It excludes Yellow Ribbon matching institutional aid and benefits not awarded or certified through the institution.

Aggregate number of contracted work months for full-time, non-medical instructional staff as of November 1, including staff whose duties are instruction alone or combined with research and/or public service; months reflect the contracted teaching period rather than the pay period.
Annual required fees, excluding tuition, charged to full-time out-of-state pharmacy students enrolled in a first-professional program; full-time status is defined by the institution.

Indicates whether the institution offered a Doctor's degree-professional practice program in each 6-digit CIP category: 1 means offered and 0 means not offered, including programs with no awards during the 12-month reporting period. For 2-digit CIP categories and the grand total, it reports the number of programs offered.
Typical dollar amount of required fees for a full-time, out-of-state first-professional student for the full academic year; required fees are mandatory charges beyond tuition.
Headcount of cohort women classified as Asian, Native Hawaiian, or Other Pacific Islander, using the combined current and former race/ethnicity definitions.

A headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates with income of $110,001 or more who received Title IV federal aid during the full aid year. It applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard-term calendars that report fall-enrolled students, and to public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.
Indicates that the institution does not offer distance education courses or programs.

Total dollars of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant or scholarship aid received during the full aid year by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received qualifying aid; other grant sources are excluded. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report financial aid for fall-enrolled students.

Unduplicated headcount of students enrolled for credit during the 12-month period who were identified as another gender, covering undergraduate and graduate students without breakdowns by full-time/part-time status or detailed degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate categories. The cell is blank when an institution cannot report another gender and zero when it can report it but has no such students.

Published dollar amount of required fees for full-time, first-time undergraduate students for the full academic year, charged to students residing in the institution's locality (in-district); this rate may be lower than the in-state rate.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus and not with family who received any Title IV federal aid, including grants, work-study, or loans. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting a fall cohort and full-aid-year awards, and for public or private institutions using clock-hour, primarily occupational, continuous, or program-specific calendars reporting a 12-month enrollment period and full-aid-year awards.

Total base salary outlays, excluding supplements, overloads, bonuses, and additional administrative or other stipends, for full-time, non-medical instructional staff on 12-month contracts. Instructional staff perform instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service; medical-school staff are excluded, but staff in affiliated health or allied-health schools may be included.

Indicates whether each 6-digit CIP program offers a Doctor's degree—research/scholarship program, including programs with zero awards during the 12-month reporting period; at the 2-digit CIP and institution-total levels, it reports the count of such programs. Values are 1 for offered and 0 for not offered at the program level, while aggregate records use the corresponding total program counts.

Total dollar amount of repayable student loans received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including Title IV, institutional, and private student loans but excluding PLUS and other loans made directly to parents.

Female high school students enrolled for college credit during the 12-month period whose race/ethnicity is unknown. This count is included in non-degree/non-certificate-seeking unduplicated 12-month enrollment and is generally less than the total non-degree/non-certificate-seeking enrollment.

Total dollars of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, whose income used to determine EFC was 30,001–48,000 and who received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year.

Average dollar amount of student loans awarded per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate student. Includes Title IV subsidized and unsubsidized loans and institutionally or privately sponsored student loans, but excludes PLUS and other loans made directly to parents.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV federal student aid during the full aid year. Applicable to public institutions with standard calendar systems that report aid for fall-enrolled students.

Total dollar amount of Department of Defense Tuition Assistance benefits received by all student recipients, including eligible spouses or dependents; includes only benefits awarded or certified through the institution and known to it, paid directly by the servicemember’s Armed Service.

Required fees in dollars for a full-time, in-state law student enrolled in a first-professional program, reported for the full academic year. In-state means the student meets the institution's or state's residency requirements.

A coded classification of the institution’s highest degree offering, distinguishing doctoral offerings (research/scholarship and/or professional practice, including other doctoral degrees), master’s, bachelor’s, associate, below-associate, and no reported offering levels.

Average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from households with income of $75,001–$110,000 who received Title IV federal aid, calculated as cost of attendance minus average grant and scholarship aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students for the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars reporting a 12-month aid period; the amount reflects the full academic year or the reported program length.

Headcount of women who are nonresident aliens in the reported cohort; these are temporary visa holders without permanent-resident status and are counted separately from U.S. citizens and resident aliens in the racial/ethnic categories.
Published out-of-state tuition and required fees for full-time, first-time undergraduate students for the full academic year; it excludes books, room and board, and other attendance expenses.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from families with income of $0–$30,000 who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars for the fall cohort, and by public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour calendars for students enrolled during the institution’s full 12-month aid-year reporting period.

Total dollars of federal, state/local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the specified income range who received Title IV aid and paid in-state or in-district tuition. This column applies only to public institutions with standard academic calendars that report aid for a fall cohort across the full aid year.

Average dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard academic calendars that report aid for a fall-enrolled cohort across the full aid year.

Count of full-time women in instructional roles on 11-month contracts, reported as of November 1. Instructional staff include employees whose function is instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service; medical-school staff are excluded.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates with income used to determine Expected Family Contribution below $30,000 who received Title IV aid (including grants, work-study, or loans). Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting a fall cohort, and for public or private institutions with clock-hour, primarily occupational, continuous, or program-variable calendars reporting a 12-month cohort.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus with family, paying in-state or in-district tuition, and receiving grant or scholarship aid from federal, state, local, or institutional sources. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year; students receiving only other grant aid are excluded.
Counts full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students receiving nonfederal loans sponsored by the institution or private sources; excludes loans made directly to parents.

Dollar value of net assets subject to donor or grantor restrictions, including both temporarily restricted assets and permanently restricted assets, such as term endowments and assets held under qualifying trusts.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the fall cohort who pay in-state tuition rates.

Headcount of male, full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students enrolled in the most recent fall period, including students who began in the preceding summer and those covered by early decision or early action; reported for institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

Indicates how an institution uses English proficiency tests for applicable entering first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates: required for admission, considered if submitted, or not considered even if submitted; applies to institutions without an open admission policy.

Total dollars in Department of Defense Tuition Assistance benefits received by graduate students, including eligible spouses or dependents, as reported to the institution. It excludes benefits awarded or certified outside the institution.

Identifies 4-year institutions with a remaining inconsistency between the full-time, first-time cohort and completer counts reported on the OM survey and the GR150 survey. Applies to institutions reporting an other-than-bachelor’s degree-seeking cohort, or only a bachelor’s cohort while also reporting below-bachelor’s completers; OM completers should be at least as numerous as GR150 completers because OM uses a longer completion period.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received during the full aid year by aided full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition. Applies only to public institutions with standard calendar systems that report financial aid for fall-enrolled students; excludes other grant-aid sources.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving any Title IV federal aid whose financial-aid income used for EFC determination was $110,001 or more. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars for fall-enrolled students receiving aid during the full aid year, and by public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars for students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Average dollar amount of institution-funded scholarships and fellowships received per full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate student, including awards targeted by residence, major, athletics, or other criteria.

Headcount of employees classified as archivists, curators, and museum technicians; librarians; library technicians; or other teachers and instructional support staff under the applicable SOC categories.
Average dollar amount of Pell Grant aid received by full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students.

ACT composite score at the 75th percentile among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted ACT scores. Reported only by institutions without an open-admission policy when admission tests are required and at least 60% of the enrolled students submitted scores.

Total dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant or scholarship aid received during the full aid year by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received such aid; excludes other grant sources. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students, and to public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Identifies whether the institution reported its 12-month unduplicated enrollment headcount using the new race/ethnicity categories, the old categories, or a mixture of both; nonresident alien and race/ethnicity unknown categories are shared by both methods.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from families with income of $110,001 or more who received Title IV aid; the denominator is these Title IV-aided students, including those whose Title IV aid was a loan. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars with fall enrollment cohorts, and to public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars reporting a 12-month aid-year cohort.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the fall cohort who pay in-district tuition rates.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $110,001-or-more income group who received any Title IV aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or institution; private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions report this for fall-enrolled students receiving aid during the full aid year, or for applicable continuous/program-length institutions for students enrolled during the 12-month reporting period.

Total dollar amount of student loans awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including Title IV and institutionally or privately sponsored loans but excluding parent loans such as PLUS.

Total dollar amount of federal, state/local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received Title IV aid and whose financial-aid income level was $110,001 or more. It applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students’ aid for the full aid year, and to public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received any financial aid, including grants, loans, scholarships, fellowships, waivers, benefits, and employer or other non-family aid.
Annual dollar amount of mandatory, fixed fees charged to nonresident students enrolled full time at the graduate level.

Categorical identifier for the undergraduate entering cohort in the Outcome Measures component: first-time or non-first-time, full-time or part-time, further split by Pell-recipient versus non-Pell-recipient.
