It applies to degree-granting institutions reporting full-year entering cohorts, including first-time entrants, undergraduate transfers entering for the first time, and non-degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates.

Count of students in the applicable cohort who received neither a Pell Grant nor a Direct Subsidized Loan and completed a bachelor's or equivalent degree within 150% of the program's normal completion time; reported for four-year institutions.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received any financial aid, including grants, scholarships, student loans, work-study, and other aid from government, the institution, or private sources; parent loans are excluded.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received federal grants or federally sponsored educational assistance, including Pell Grants, SEOG, veterans’ benefits, and similar aid.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from families with income of $0–$30,000 who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Headcount of male nonresident aliens enrolled for credit on the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15. Nonresident aliens are temporary visa holders without permanent-resident status; legal immigrants and resident aliens are reported in the applicable racial/ethnic categories.

Binary indicator of whether the institution’s general-purpose financial statements include postemployment benefits other than pension (OPEB) liabilities, expenses, and/or deferrals. It is reported as No when the institution has no OPEB plan, those amounts are retained by a higher-education system or not allocated to a branch campus, or the institution is part of a special funding situation; in jointly audited systems, the system office reports Yes and campuses report No when it absorbs the amounts.

Indicates whether a 1-year but less-than-2-year certificate program was offered, based on the institution’s 12-month completions reporting: at the 6-digit CIP level, 1 means offered and 0 means not offered, including programs offered with no awards; 2-digit CIP and institution-total records report the corresponding number of programs offered.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received federal grants or other federally sponsored educational assistance, including Pell and SEOG awards.

Identifies the fall reporting period for the most recent available cohort of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including students admitted the preceding summer; applicable to institutions without open admission that require test scores and had at least 60% of this cohort submit SAT or ACT scores.

Total dollar amount of federal, state/local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $75,001–$110,000 income range who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant or scholarship aid awarded during the full aid year to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received such aid; other grant sources are excluded. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting on fall enrollees, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-differing, or primarily clock-hour calendars reporting on students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Percentage of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students submitting ACT scores, using the entering cohort that includes students admitted in the preceding summer; reported for institutions without an open-admission policy.

Average dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state/local, or institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the income group of $110,001 or more who received Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or clock-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period; aid may have been awarded at any time during that full aid year.

Indicates whether a Doctor's degree–professional practice program is offered at the 6-digit CIP level (1 = offered, 0 = not offered), based on the institution's 12-month completions reporting; at 2-digit CIP and institution-total records, it is the count of programs offered.

Headcount of women in the cohort classified as Asian, Native Hawaiian, or Other Pacific Islander; this is a derived combined race/ethnicity category that aligns the newer Asian and Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander classifications with the former Asian/Pacific Islander category.

Reports the SAT Math score at or below which 25% of test-submitters fall, for first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students (including those entering the prior summer); populated for institutions without open admission when SAT/ACT scores are required and at least 60% of these students submit scores.

Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students receiving other loan aid, defined as nonfederal institutionally or privately sponsored student loans; loans made directly to parents are excluded.

Indicates whether the institution's academic library provides access to library collections shared with other institutions. It is a yes/no library resource or service indicator, with "None of the above" used when none of the listed resources or services apply.
Indicates whether the institution's academic library offers established hours when library staff services are available to users.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who live off campus without family and received federal, state, local, or institutional grant or scholarship aid; students receiving only other grant sources are excluded. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for a fall-enrolled cohort across the full aid year.

Average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from families with income of $75,001–$110,000 who received Title IV federal aid, calculated as cost of attendance minus average grant and scholarship aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students for the full aid year, and for public or private institutions using clock hours, primarily occupational programs, or continuous/program-specific calendars reporting a 12-month aid period; the amount reflects a full academic year or the length of the institution’s largest program.

The dollar amount of Title IV federal student loans awarded directly to non-degree/non-certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including eligible student loan programs but excluding PLUS loans and other federal loans not made directly to the student.

Dollar amount for a full academic year of room and board for a full-time, first-time undergraduate living off campus without family; room is based on a typical shared room and board on the institution’s specified meal plan.

ACT Writing score at the 75th percentile among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted ACT scores, including students admitted the prior summer; populated for institutions that require admission test scores and do not have an open-admission policy.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid and whose financial-aid-determination income falls in the stated range; income includes parents’ and student’s income for dependent students and the student’s income for independent students. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students’ aid over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month period and aid received during the full aid year.
Headcount of full-time men in instructional roles, excluding medical-school staff, who work under contracts covering fewer than 9 months, measured as of November 1.

Total dollar amount of federal, state, local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $48,001–$75,000 income band who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions using a standard calendar system that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.

Indicates whether the institution offers a doctor’s degree in professional practice, a degree requiring at least six full-time-equivalent academic years of study and leading to professional licensure or practice, such as medicine, law, dentistry, or pharmacy.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $75,001–$110,000 income group who received any Title IV federal aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or their institution; students receiving only private grants, loans, or work-study are excluded. Applicable to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard calendar systems reporting aid for fall enrollees over the full aid year, and to eligible private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars reporting students enrolled during a 12-month period.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $48,001–$75,000 income range who received Title IV aid. Populated for private nonprofit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.
Typical required fees in dollars for a full-time in-state law student in a doctor's professional practice program, covering the full academic year.

Total dollar amount of federal, state, local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving Title IV aid whose financial-aid income falls in the specified income range. It applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students’ aid for the full aid year, and to public or private institutions using continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who applied, were admitted, and enrolled for the fall period, including early decision/action students and those beginning in the preceding summer; applicable to institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.
Number of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received state or local government grants, scholarships, or waivers.

Reports the typical full-academic-year tuition and required fees, in dollars, charged to a full-time first-professional Osteopathic Medicine (D.O.) student who does not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements.

Total dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state/local, or institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the specified income bracket who received Title IV aid. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students with aid awarded during the full aid year, and to public or private institutions using continuous or program-specific/contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received state or local government grants, scholarships, or waivers.

A categorical classification of an institution’s undergraduate population based on the share enrolled part- versus full-time, the academic selectivity or inclusiveness of first-year students, and the share of entering undergraduates who are transfers. It covers associate’s degree-granting institutions and bachelor’s-or-higher degree-granting institutions, with categories differing by these thresholds; it describes institutional population characteristics rather than educational quality.

Total dollars in state and local government grants, scholarships, and waivers awarded to full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including students in bachelor's, associate, vocational, or technical programs.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV federal aid and any grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or the institution; private-source grants, loans, and work-study alone are excluded. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students' aid awarded over the full aid year.

Total dollar amount of federal grants and federally sponsored educational assistance awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates, including Pell Grants, SEOG, veterans' benefits, and other federal aid.

Average dollar amount of federal, state, local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the 30,001–48,000 income range who received Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students over the full aid period, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during a 12-month aid period.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid and whose financial-aid income used for EFC determination was $75,001–$110,000. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard term calendars for fall-enrolled students receiving aid during the full aid year, and by public or private institutions with continuous, contact-hour, or program-length calendars for students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Average dollar amount of student loans received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students; includes Title IV and institutionally or privately sponsored loans, but excludes parent loans such as PLUS.

Fall headcount of women who are U.S. nonresidents—noncitizens or non-nationals temporarily in the United States on a visa—enrolled for credit as of the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15; legally admitted permanent residents are counted in racial/ethnic categories instead.

The SAT Evidence-Based Reading and Writing score at the 50th percentile among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the reported admissions group, including students admitted the prior summer; populated for institutions without an open-admission policy that require test scores for admission.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $0–$30,000 income group who received Title IV aid and paid the in-state or in-district tuition rate. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the specified income band who received any Title IV aid and a grant or scholarship from the federal government, state/local government, or institution; private-source grants, loans, and work-study alone are excluded. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students with aid received during the full aid year, and for private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

The ACT Math score at or below which 75% of submitted scores fall, for first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students at institutions that require admission test scores and do not have an open-admission policy.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received state or local government grants, scholarships, or waivers.

SAT Verbal score at the 25th percentile among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including students who entered during the prior summer. Reported only by institutions without an open-admission policy when at least 60% of these enrolled students submitted SAT scores.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received Title IV aid during the full aid year and whose EFC income was $110,001 or more; applicable to public institutions with standard term calendars reporting aid for a fall cohort.

Binary indicator of whether at least one master's program within a 6-digit CIP code can be completed entirely through distance education, including programs with no awards during the reporting period. For 2-digit CIP and institution-total records, the value is an aggregate count of programs offered rather than a 0/1 indicator.

Identifies whether an institution reports on a standard academic-term calendar or on program-length or continuous calendars. Academic-year reporters use fall cohorts for Graduation Rates and report student charges for a full academic year, while program reporters use full-year cohorts and report charges by program.

Reports the ACT English score at the 25th percentile among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted ACT scores. Populated for institutions without open admission policies when ACT or other test scores are required and at least 60% of enrolled students submitted scores; the cohort includes students admitted in the preceding summer.

Headcount of full-time male instructional staff on 11-month contracts, as of November 1, excluding medical-school staff and staff working strictly in associated hospitals or unaffiliated health and allied-health programs.

Count of men classified as Asian, Native Hawaiian, or Other Pacific Islander, using a derived combined race/ethnicity category that harmonizes the newer Asian and Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander categories with the former Asian/Pacific Islander category.
Average dollar amount of federal, state, local, and institutional grant aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students.
Typical full-academic-year tuition and required fees, in dollars, for a full-time first-professional Medicine (M.D.) student who is not an in-state resident.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate recipient of any Title IV aid, across all income levels. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-based, or clock-hour calendars that report a 12-month aid-year population.

Aggregate dollar amount of federal, state/local, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received during the full aid year by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, whose aid-office income was $0–$30,000 and who received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting aid for fall-enrolled students.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received any federal, state, local, or institutional grant aid.

Average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from families with income of $48,001–$75,000 who received Title IV federal aid, calculated as cost of attendance minus average grant and scholarship aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the full aid year; it reflects the academic year or the length of the institution’s largest program, as applicable.

Fall headcount of women enrolled for credit who are American Indian or Alaska Native, combining the old and new race/ethnicity definitions; enrollment is measured on the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15.

Total dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $0–$30,000 income category who received Title IV aid and paid in-state or in-district tuition. Populated for public institutions using standard academic calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students awarded aid throughout the full aid year.

Binary indicator of whether at least one program in a 6-digit CIP code, consisting of certificates shorter than 12 weeks, can be completed entirely through distance education; 1 means offered and 0 means not offered, regardless of whether awards were granted during the reporting period. For 2-digit CIP and institution-total records, the values are aggregate counts of programs offered rather than binary indicators.
Count of female staff classified as nonresident aliens—non-U.S. citizens or nationals in the country temporarily on a visa without permanent-residency rights.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $75,001–$110,000 income range who paid in-state or in-district tuition, received any Title IV aid, and were awarded grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or the institution. Applicable only to public institutions with standard calendar systems reporting aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year.

Typical full-academic-year tuition and required fees, in dollars, charged to a full-time first-professional Pharmacy (Pharm.D.) student who does not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements.

Annual dollar amount of required, non-tuition fees charged to full-time undergraduate students enrolled at the institution in-district, meaning the locality where they attend school. Undergraduates include students in associate, bachelor's, and sub-baccalaureate vocational or technical programs; full-time means at least 12 semester or quarter credits, or 24 clock hours per week.

Annual in-state required fees charged to full-time undergraduate students, where in-state means meeting the institution's or state's residency requirements and required fees are mandatory fixed charges beyond tuition.

Headcount of men and women enrolled for credit at four-year institutions on the official fall reporting date or October 15 whose race/ethnicity was not selected and could not be determined through institutional procedures.

Annual dollar amount of required fees published for full-time, first-time undergraduate students who meet the institution’s or state’s in-state residency requirements, as used by the financial aid office for the full academic year.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition whose living arrangement is unknown and who received grant or scholarship aid from federal, state or local governments or the institution (excluding students receiving only other grant sources). Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students awarded aid during the full aid year.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving any Title IV federal aid whose income is $75,001–$110,000. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars for fall-enrolled students tracked through the full aid year, and by public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars for students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Categorical Carnegie classification of an institution's graduate instructional program, based on the graduate degrees it awarded, the breadth of fields, and the concentration of degrees across disciplinary domains. It applies to postbaccalaureate degree-granting institutions, including those with at least one research doctoral degree, and distinguishes categories such as single-program, comprehensive, dominant-field, and medical/veterinary-school research-doctoral institutions.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living in institution-owned or controlled housing who received grant or scholarship aid from federal, state, or local governments or the institution; students receiving only other grant sources are excluded. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students and full-aid-year awards, and for public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars reporting students enrolled during a 12-month period and full-aid-year awards.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates with family income of $30,001–$48,000 who received Title IV federal student aid during the full aid year. Applicable to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report on fall enrollees, and to public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report on students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Categorical code for the institution's degree of urbanization, ranging from large or mid-size cities and their urban fringes to large towns, small towns, and rural areas, based on Census Bureau population and metropolitan-area classifications.

Indicates whether a less-than-one-year certificate program is offered at each six-digit CIP level, and provides the total number of such programs for two-digit CIP categories and the institution. It measures programs offered rather than certificates awarded, including programs with no awards during the 12-month reporting period.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the fall cohort whose state of residence or tuition-rate status is unknown.

Dollar amount of published in-state required fees for full-time, first-time undergraduate students for the full academic year; required fees are mandatory charges separate from tuition and apply to students meeting the state or institution’s residency requirements. Covers institutions using standard or other academic calendar systems.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from households with income of $75,001–$110,000 who received Title IV federal grant aid during the full aid year. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting a fall cohort, and for applicable private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during a 12-month period.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who live off campus and not with family and received Title IV federal aid during the full aid year. Populated for public institutions with standard calendar systems reporting aid for students enrolled in the fall.

A binary indicator for each 6-digit CIP code showing whether all bachelor's programs in that CIP can be completed entirely through distance education; 1 means yes and 0 means no. For 2-digit CIP and institution-total records, it instead summarizes whether any programs are offered (1 = total programs offered, 0 = none).

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, with family income below $30,000, who received Title IV federal grant aid during the full aid year. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for students enrolled in the fall.
Total clock hours of coursework completed by undergraduate students in occupational programs during the 12-month reporting period, counting each student’s actual hours completed.

Total dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state/local, or institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates receiving Title IV aid whose income used for EFC determination was $48,001–$75,000. It applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students for the full aid year, and to public or private institutions with clock-hour, primarily occupational, continuous, or program-specific calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at all income levels who live in institution-controlled on-campus housing and received Title IV aid during the full aid year. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars for fall-enrolled cohorts, and by public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or primarily contact-hour/occupational calendars for students enrolled during the 12-month aid-year period.
Average dollar amount of state and local government grants, scholarships, or waivers awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students.
Count of full-time women in instructional roles, excluding medical staff, who are employed on 9-, 10-, 11-, or 12-month contracts, measured as of November 1.
Annual dollar amount of tuition and required fees charged to a full-time Osteopathic Medicine (D.O.) first-professional student who meets the institution’s in-state residency requirements.

Count of part-time, first-time undergraduate students enrolled in degree- or certificate-seeking academic, vocational, or occupational programs. Includes students entering college for the first time at the undergraduate level, including those with prior summer attendance or advanced standing.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $30,001–$48,000 income range who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid plus grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or the institution. Applicable only to public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students' aid received during the full aid year; excludes aid solely from private sources, loans, or work-study.

Total dollars in Title IV subsidized and unsubsidized federal student loans awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates; excludes PLUS and other loans made directly to parents.

Indicates whether the institution offers for-credit academic programs leading to a certificate, diploma, associate's, bachelor's, master's, doctoral, or first-professional degree, or providing credits applicable to such a degree.

Indicates whether standardized admission test scores such as the SAT or ACT are required, considered only if submitted, or not considered in selecting entering first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at institutions without an open-admission policy.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, with household income of $30,001–$48,000, who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid during the full aid year; populated for public institutions with standard term-based calendar systems reporting fall-enrolled students.

Headcount of full-time women in instructional staff roles, excluding medical-school staff and staff working strictly in associated hospitals or unaffiliated health and allied-health departments, grouped by a 9-, 10-, 11-, or 12-month contract.

Flags institutions reporting zero transfer-out students across all four Outcome Measures cohorts: first-time and non-first-time, full-time and part-time. It applies when enrollment unknown across those cohorts totals at least 70 and does not identify institutions that had reported transfer-out data on a previous GR150 survey; those are covered by OMFLG6GR.
Headcount of female full-time instructional faculty whose major assignment is instruction and who do not have faculty status; graduate, instruction, and research assistants are excluded.

Total dollars of federal, state, local, and institutional grant or scholarship aid received during the full aid year by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates from families with income of $0–$30,000 who received Title IV aid. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard-term calendars that report a fall cohort, and for public or private institutions using continuous or program-specific calendars that report a 12-month enrollment cohort.

Dollar average net price after grant and scholarship aid for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, receiving Title IV federal aid, and whose family income is $0–$30,000; applicable to public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year.

Average dollar amount of student loans awarded per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate student; includes Title IV, institutional, and private loans for which the student is the borrower, but excludes PLUS and other loans made directly to parents.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $0–$30,000 income level who paid in-state or in-district tuition, received Title IV federal aid, and received grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or the institution. Applicable only to public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students' aid over the full aid year; excludes private-source grants, loans, and work-study-only recipients.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, in the specified income range, who received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students’ aid received throughout the full aid year.

Headcount of cohort students who did not receive a Pell Grant or subsidized Stafford Loan and completed an award requiring less than four academic years within 150% of the program's normal completion time, reported for total, bachelor's, and other-than-bachelor's cohorts at four-year institutions and the applicable cohort at two-year or less-than-two-year institutions.

Headcount of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted SAT scores, including students entering in the preceding summer; reported for institutions without open admission when SAT scores are required and at least 60% of these students submitted scores.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus with family who received federal, state, local, or institutional grant or scholarship aid, excluding students receiving only other grant aid. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students over the full aid year, and to public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

A 2-digit categorical code describing the institution’s physical location on the urban-to-rural continuum, from large city through suburb and town to rural, based on Census geographic definitions. It is blank for institutions in American Samoa, the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, Guam, and the Virgin Islands, which are not assigned a code.

Total base-salary outlays in dollars for full-time, non-medical instructional staff on 9-month contracts, as of November 1; excludes supplements, overloads, bonuses, administrative stipends, and staff employed in medical-school or strictly hospital operations.

Published dollar amount of tuition and fees charged for the full academic year to full-time, first-time undergraduate students residing in the institution’s local district; this in-district rate may be lower than the in-state rate.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $0–$30,000 income level who received any Title IV aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or institution; students receiving only private grants, loans, or work-study are excluded. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard calendars that report fall-enrolled students with aid received during the full aid year, and to eligible private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars reporting students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Typical full-academic-year tuition and required fees charged to a full-time podiatry doctor's professional practice student who does not meet the institution's or state's residency requirements; the institution defines full-time status.

Classifies an instructional program as a STEM field under a policy-oriented definition focused on mathematics, natural sciences, engineering, and technologies; it is not the broader definition that may include social and behavioral sciences.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $48,001–$75,000 income range who received any Title IV federal student aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state or local government, or the institution; grants from private or other sources alone, loans, and Federal Work Study do not qualify. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard calendars for students enrolled in the fall and awarded aid during the full aid year, and by eligible private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars for students enrolled during the 12-month reporting period and awarded aid during the full aid year.
Count of men and women in the cohort classified as Asian, Native Hawaiian, or Other Pacific Islander, using the corresponding combined race/ethnicity categories.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received grant or scholarship aid from federal, state or local governments or the institution; students receiving only other grant aid are excluded. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars with fall enrollment and full-year aid reporting, and by public or private institutions using continuous, program-differing, or contact-hour calendars with enrollment and aid reporting over the full 12-month aid year.

Published dollar amount of tuition charged for the full academic year to full-time, first-time undergraduate students who do not meet the institution's or state's residency requirements; includes tuition only, not fees or other attendance costs.

A categorical Carnegie classification of an institution’s size and residential character, based on fall full-time-equivalent enrollment and, for four-year institutions, the share of degree-seeking undergraduates living in institutionally owned, operated, or affiliated housing. It covers associate’s-degree-granting institutions using five FTE size bands and bachelor’s-degree-granting institutions using four FTE size bands crossed with primarily nonresidential, primarily residential, or highly residential status; exclusively graduate/professional institutions are not classified.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received any Title IV federal student aid and whose income used to determine Expected Family Contribution was $0–$30,000. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard calendar systems reporting fall-enrolled students for the full aid year, and to public or private institutions with continuous, program-based, or contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the full 12-month aid year.

Reports total dollar expenses for operations and maintenance of educational and general-purpose campus grounds and facilities, including facilities, utilities, security, insurance, leasing, and related information technology costs when separately budgeted; amounts charged to auxiliary enterprises, hospitals, and independent operations are included.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the fall cohort whose state of residence or tuition-rate status is unknown.

Headcount of non-U.S. citizens or nationals temporarily in the United States on a visa who are enrolled for credit on the institution’s official fall reporting date (or October 15); permanent residents and other eligible immigrant noncitizens are included in the appropriate racial/ethnic categories instead.

For each six-digit CIP code, this indicates whether all doctoral research/scholarship programs can be completed entirely through distance education (1 = yes, 0 = no); a program reported with zero awards still counts as offered. On two-digit CIP and institution-total records, it is an aggregate count of programs in this category rather than a binary indicator.

Counts full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at all income levels who received any Title IV federal aid, including grants, work-study, or loans. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students for the full aid year, and for public or private institutions with continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the specified income range who received any Title IV federal student aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or their institution; private-source grants, loans, and work-study alone are excluded. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard calendars reporting fall-enrolled students’ aid over the full aid year, and for private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus with family who received federal, state, local, or institutional grant or scholarship aid; students receiving only other grant sources are excluded. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit standard-calendar institutions using fall enrollment with aid received during the full aid year, and by public or private institutions with continuous, program-variable, or primarily contact-hour calendars using enrollment during the full 12-month aid period.
Headcount of male American Indian or Alaska Native students enrolled for credit at the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15, combining the old and new race/ethnicity definitions.

Indicates whether the institution enrolls students in doctor's degree–professional practice programs, such as medicine, law, dentistry, pharmacy, or veterinary medicine; institutions answering yes may report these students as graduate-level enrollment.

Count of part-time employees on the institution’s payroll as of November 1, excluding medical school staff, casual employees, and students in the College Work-Study Program. Part-time status is based on the employee’s appointment at the snapshot date, not the contract length.

Total dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state or local, and institutional sources awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition, receiving Title IV aid, and whose income used for EFC determination was $48,001–$75,000. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.
Headcount of male full-time instructional faculty who do not have faculty status; excludes graduate, instructional, and research assistants.

Dollar amount of student aid funded by endowments and gifts that is applied as discounts or allowances against tuition and fee revenue; combined with net tuition and fee revenue, it represents gross tuition and fee revenue.

Identifies the fall reporting period used for counts of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate applicants, admits, and enrollees (full- or part-time), including early decision, early action, and students who began in the preceding summer; applicable only to institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

Annual dollar amount of in-state required fees charged to full-time, first-time undergraduate students for the full academic year; these are fixed charges required of most students and are reported separately from tuition.

Headcount of students enrolled for credit as of the institution’s official fall reporting date or October 15 who take exclusively distance-education courses in the U.S., but whose state or jurisdiction is unknown. Distance education requires instruction delivered exclusively through qualifying technologies with regular and substantive instructor interaction; occasional campus attendance for orientation, testing, or academic support does not disqualify a course.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition whose income used for Expected Family Contribution falls in the 30,001–48,000 range and who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid during the full aid year. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting aid for students enrolled in the fall.

Categorical classification of an institution’s graduate instructional program based on graduate degrees actually awarded, not programs offered; a single graduate-level degree qualifies the institution for inclusion. It distinguishes nondoctoral and doctoral institutions by the breadth and disciplinary concentration of graduate degrees, with medical/veterinary education identified in certain doctoral categories, and is blank for institutions that award no graduate-level degrees.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received Title IV aid and whose financial-aid income level was $75,001–$110,000. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students over the full aid year, and for public or private institutions using clock hours, primarily occupational credit hours, continuous calendars, or program-specific calendars reporting students enrolled over the 12-month aid period.

Combined base-salary outlays, excluding supplements, overloads, bonuses, and administrative stipends, for full-time women instructional staff on 9-month contracts as of November 1. Covers non-medical staff whose functions are instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service; excludes staff employed in medical-school components or free-standing medical schools, but not necessarily affiliated hospitals or other health programs.

Dollar amount of tuition and fee discounts and allowances funded by endowment income and gifts, including recognized contributed services; it is the portion of total student aid applied to tuition and fees and, when added to tuition and fee revenue, represents gross tuition and fee revenue.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received per full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate in the specified income band who paid in-state or in-district tuition and received any Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.

Categorical classification of an institution's undergraduate instructional program based on the types and levels of degrees awarded, the balance of arts-and-sciences versus professional fields, and the extent of graduate-program coexistence in related fields. It covers undergraduate education regardless of the institution's graduate offerings and is a time-specific snapshot of institutional attributes and behavior.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the fall cohort who are legal residents of the state where they attend the institution.

Headcount of students in the bachelor's degree-seeking cohort who left the institution within 150% of normal time without graduating or transferring, due to death or permanent disability, military service, qualifying federal foreign-aid service, or an official church mission.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates charged in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV federal grant aid during the full aid year. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students and their aid for the full aid year.

Count of awards or degrees conferred to men and women identified as Asian, Native Hawaiian, or Other Pacific Islander during the reporting period; the category combines the newer Asian and Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander definitions with the former Asian/Pacific Islander category.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV federal student aid and whose aid-eligibility income used for Expected Family Contribution falls within the specified range. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting fall-enrolled students who received aid during the full aid year.

Headcount of women who are first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students enrolled part time during the most recent fall period, including students who began in the preceding summer and those admitted through early decision or early action; reported only by institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.
Dollar amount of tuition and fee charges reduced through scholarships and fellowships funded by endowments and gifts.

Reports the typical full-academic-year tuition and required fees, in dollars, charged to a full-time student in the institution's veterinary medicine (D.V.M.) professional-practice program who meets the applicable in-state residency requirements.

Count of male full-time instructional faculty who do not have faculty status; includes staff whose primary assignment is instruction, including instruction combined with research or public service, and excludes graduate, instructional, and research assistants.

Annual out-of-state tuition and required fees charged to a full-time law (doctor's professional practice) student for the full academic year; the amount applies to students who do not meet the state or institution’s residency requirements.

Typical full-year tuition and required fees charged to a full-time M.D. (doctor's professional practice) student who meets the institution's in-state residency requirements, measured in dollars. It uses the institution's own definition of full-time and its academic-year schedule.

Categorical code describing the institution’s physical-location position on the urban-to-rural continuum, from large city through suburb, town, and rural, using city size and distance from urbanized areas or clusters. Institutions in American Samoa, the Northern Mariana Islands, Guam, and the Virgin Islands have no assigned code.

Categorizes undergraduate full-year entering cohorts at degree-granting institutions by first-time versus non-first-time status, full-time versus part-time enrollment, and Pell-recipient versus non-Pell-recipient status. The entering population includes first-time undergraduates, undergraduate transfers entering the institution for the first time, and non-degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates.

Counts full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus with family who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid; it is a headcount, not an aid amount. Populated for private nonprofit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting a fall cohort and full aid-year awards, and for public or private institutions using clock-hour, occupational, continuous, or program-specific calendars reporting a 12-month cohort and full aid-year awards.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates who received any Title IV federal grant aid (including Pell, FSEOG, ACG, National SMART, or TEACH Grants). Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report a fall cohort, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-differentiated, or primarily contact-hour calendars that report an enrollment population over the full 12-month aid year.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received any Title IV federal student aid and grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or institution; private-source grants, loans, and Federal Work-Study alone are excluded. Reported for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard calendars for fall-enrolled students receiving aid during the full aid year, and for applicable private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars for students enrolled during the 12-month reporting period.

Headcount of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who enrolled part time and whose gender is unknown in the reported fall admissions cohort, including eligible summer entrants and early-decision/action students; applies to institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

Identifies whether the institution reported 12-month unduplicated enrollment headcount using the new race/ethnicity categories, the old categories, or a mixture of both; nonresident alien and race/ethnicity unknown categories are common to all methods.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received institutional scholarships or fellowships, including awards targeted by residence, major, athletics, or other criteria.

Headcount of full-time, first-time undergraduate students enrolled in credit-bearing programs leading to a degree or certificate, including students in associate, bachelor's, vocational, or technical programs below the baccalaureate. Includes students entering college for the first time, including those with prior summer enrollment or advanced standing.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying the in-state or in-district tuition rate who received federal, state or local government, or institutional grant or scholarship aid; students receiving only other grant aid are excluded. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.

Typical in-state tuition and required fees charged for the full academic year to a full-time student enrolled in an Optometry (O.D.) doctor's professional practice program; the amount applies to students meeting the state or institution's residency requirements.

Categorizes institution-reported staff by their primary occupational activity, based on the activity taking most of their time, and distinguishes full-time and part-time status. Casual employees and College Work-Study students are excluded; graduate assistants are classified separately from faculty and other staff.

Headcount of full-time, non-medical instructional staff whose teaching contracts cover fewer than 9 months, measured as of November 1; includes staff in instruction or instruction combined with research and/or public service, but excludes medical-school and strictly hospital staff.

Indicates the fall reporting period used for SAT/ACT results for first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates, including students who first enrolled in the preceding summer. Applicable to institutions without an open-admission policy when test scores are required for admission.

Headcount of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students enrolled part time, using the institution’s part-time enrollment threshold (11 or fewer semester/quarter credits or fewer than 24 contact hours per week).

Total dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded during the full aid year to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $48,001–$75,000 income group who received Title IV aid. Applies to private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard academic calendars reporting fall-enrolled students, and to public or private institutions using clock-hour, primarily occupational credit-hour, continuous, or program-specific calendars reporting students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.
Total Pell Grant dollars awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including students in academic, occupational, vocational, or technical programs.
Percentage of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who received institutional grants, scholarships, or fellowships funded by the institution or its departments.

Indicates whether the institution offers for-credit occupational programs designed to prepare students for a specific occupation and potentially leading to a certificate, degree, or other formal award; it excludes avocational and adult basic education.

Average dollars of grant and scholarship aid awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $0–30,000 income group who received any Title IV aid; Title IV eligibility includes grants, work-study, and loans, while this measure covers grant and scholarship aid only. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard-term calendars that report fall enrollment with aid awarded throughout the full aid year, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour/primarily occupational calendars reporting a 12-month enrollment period.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition whose income used to determine Expected Family Contribution was $48,001–$75,000 and who received Title IV federal aid (grants, work-study, or loans). Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students awarded aid during the full aid year.

Average dollar amount of nonfederal, institutionally or privately sponsored student loans awarded to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students; excludes loans made directly to parents.

Average dollar cost of attendance remaining after federal, state, local, or institutional grants and scholarships for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying the in-state or in-district rate. It covers public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for students enrolled in the fall, with aid awarded throughout the full aid year.

Count of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received Title IV federal grant aid during the full aid year, grouped by the stated family-income level. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting aid for fall-enrolled students.

Average dollar amount of federal, state, local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $110,001-or-more income level who pay in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars reporting aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year.

Published full-academic-year tuition in dollars for full-time, first-time undergraduate students who reside in the institution’s local district; an in-district rate may be lower than the institution’s in-state tuition.

Book value in dollars of the institution’s total plant, property, and equipment at the end of the fiscal year, including land and improvements, infrastructure, buildings, equipment and capitalized art or library collections, capital-lease property, and construction in progress; revenue-producing buildings are excluded.

Reports dollar expenses for operation and maintenance of campus grounds and facilities used for educational and general purposes, when charged to independent operations unrelated to the institution’s primary missions; may include related information technology, depreciation, and (for FASB institutions) interest, but excludes endowment-investment operations.

The number of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate applicants for the most recent fall period, including full- and part-time enrollees, early decision and early action applicants, and students who began in the preceding summer. This is reported only by institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.

The ACT English score below which 75% of submitted scores for first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students fall; reported by institutions without an open-admission policy when admission test scores are required.

Categorizes institutions by degree-granting status and highest or predominant level of awards, distinguishing graduate-only, primarily baccalaureate, other baccalaureate, associate's/certificate, and nondegree-granting institutions. It is not applicable for inactive institutions or administrative units, and is not reported when required Institutional Characteristics or Completions data are unavailable.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the highest income level who paid the in-state or in-district tuition rate, received any Title IV federal aid, and also received grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or the institution; students receiving only private/other grants, loans, or work-study are excluded. Applicable to public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students' aid for the full aid year.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition who received any Title IV federal grant, work-study, or loan aid, grouped by the income used to determine Expected Family Contribution. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report fall-enrolled students receiving aid at any time during the full aid year.

SAT Critical Reading score at the 75th percentile among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted SAT/ACT scores; reported only by institutions without an open-admission policy when admission test scores are required.
Headcount of full-time men in non-medical instructional roles, including instruction alone or combined with research and/or public service, employed on 9-month contracts as of November 1.

Average net price in dollars for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying the in-state or in-district rate, in households with income of $0–$30,000, who received Title IV federal aid; it is total cost of attendance minus average federal, state/local, and institutional grant or scholarship aid. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students awarded aid during the full aid year.

Indicates whether the institution accepts postsecondary credit earned through dual enrollment, in which high school students or students seeking a recognized equivalent take college courses and receive transcripted credit for passing grades. This excludes credit-by-exam programs such as Advanced Placement and International Baccalaureate.

Dollar amount of required fees for full-time, first-time undergraduate students residing in the institution’s locality (in-district) for the full academic year; this rate may be lower than the in-state rate.

Average dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state, local, or institutional sources received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $110,001-or-more income group who received Title IV aid. Reported for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars with fall-cohort/full-aid-year reporting, and for public or private institutions using continuous or program-specific calendars with 12-month/full-aid-year reporting.

Average dollar amount of federal student loans awarded to degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students, including Title IV loans made directly to the student but excluding PLUS and other loans not made directly to the student.

Numeric FIPS-based code identifying the congressional district where the school is located; the state code is combined with a two-digit district code, with 00 for at-large districts, 98 for territories with a nonvoting delegate, and -2 for areas without congressional representation.
The typical dollar amount of required fees charged for a full-time, out-of-state podiatry student for the full academic year; these are mandatory fixed charges separate from tuition.

Headcount of students in the adjusted cohort who earned a bachelor's degree by the eight-year status point; students earning multiple awards are counted by their highest award, including four- or five-year cooperative and accelerated bachelor's programs.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $110,001-or-more income group who received any Title IV federal aid and were awarded grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or their institution; private-source grants, loans, and work-study alone do not qualify. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard calendars that report fall-enrolled students with aid received during the full aid year, and for applicable private institutions using continuous or program-different calendars that report students enrolled during the 12-month aid period.
The headcount of full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students awarded state or local government grants, scholarships, or waivers.

Indicates whether completions race and ethnicity were reported using the new categories, the old categories, or a mixture of both. The new method reports Hispanic/Latino regardless of race and race categories for non-Hispanic/Latino individuals; nonresident alien and race/ethnicity unknown are common to both methods.

Annual dollar amount of required fees charged to full-time, first-time undergraduate students residing in the institution’s locality; this in-district rate may be lower than the in-state rate and is reported for the full academic year.

ACT English score at or below which 75% of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the reported admissions group scored; populated for institutions that require admission test scores and do not have an open-admission policy.

Categorical Carnegie classification of institutions by degree levels, research activity, program mix, institutional control, size, setting, and special-focus or tribal-college status; codes identify categories such as associate’s, doctoral, master’s, baccalaureate, special-focus, and tribal colleges.

A categorical Carnegie classification of an institution’s undergraduate profile, based on fall undergraduate part-time/full-time enrollment, first-year student achievement or admissions selectivity, and the share of entering undergraduates who are transfers. Values distinguish associate’s-degree-granting two-year institutions from bachelor’s-degree-granting four-year institutions and indicate part-time intensity, inclusive versus selective or more selective admissions, and lower versus higher transfer-in rates; it applies to degree-granting institutions with an undergraduate population.

The per-credit-hour charge in dollars for part-time undergraduate students who do not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements; undergraduates include students in associate, bachelor’s, or sub-baccalaureate vocational or technical programs, and part-time means 11 or fewer semester or quarter credits or fewer than 24 clock hours per week.
Headcount of students in the adjusted cohort who earned a bachelor's degree within six years of entry; for students earning multiple awards, only their highest award by the status point is counted.

Identifies whether the institution reports student charges for the full academic year or by program length, and whether graduation, retention, and student financial aid data use a fall or full-year cohort. Standard-term institutions use a fall cohort, while other, continuous, or program-length calendar institutions use a full-year cohort; program-based institutions report charges for the entire program length.

Indicates whether the institution offers distance education courses or programs at the graduate level. Graduate students are those studying at the post-baccalaureate level, whether or not enrolled in a formal graduate program.

Average dollar amount of non-Pell federal grant aid awarded per full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate student; includes programs such as SEOG and other federal student aid grants.

Total dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $75,001–$110,000 income range who pay in-state or in-district tuition and received Title IV aid. Populated for public institutions using standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students across the full aid year.

Published dollar amount of required fees for the full academic year charged to full-time, first-time undergraduate students who do not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements; required fees are mandatory charges separate from tuition.

Aggregate dollar amount of federal, state, local, and institutional grants and scholarships received by full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the specified income range who received any Title IV aid; it is not a per-student amount and excludes work-study and loans. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report fall-enrolled students, and for public or private institutions using continuous, program-specific, or contact-hour calendars that report students enrolled during the full 12-month aid period.

Categorizes full-time faculty by institution-assigned academic rank and tenure status. Faculty are employees whose principal activity is instruction, research, or public service; graduate, instructional, and research assistants are excluded.

The ACT English score at or below which 25% of submitted scores fall, for first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students (including those entering in the prior summer); populated for institutions that require admission test scores and do not have an open-admission policy.

Percentage of degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduate students enrolled for credit who were awarded federal loans made directly to the student, including Title IV student loans and specified health-profession loans but excluding PLUS and other loans not borrowed by the student.
Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students awarded nonfederal institutionally or privately sponsored student loans, excluding loans made directly to parents.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates paying in-state or in-district tuition at the specified income level, among those who received any Title IV federal aid. Populated for public institutions with standard-term calendars that report aid for a fall cohort across the full aid year.

Headcount of graduate students receiving Department of Defense Tuition Assistance benefits, including eligible spouses or dependents; covers only recipients and benefits known to or awarded/certified through the institution.
Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the fall cohort who pay out-of-state tuition rates.

Count of students in the cohort who did not receive a Pell Grant or subsidized Stafford Loan and were excluded from the 150%-of-normal-time completion cohort because they left for documented reasons such as death or permanent disability, military or foreign-aid service, or an official church mission.

Reports the typical full-academic-year dollar amount of tuition and required fees charged to a full-time chiropractic doctor's professional practice student who meets the institution's or state's in-state residency requirements.

Average dollar amount of federal, state/local, or institutional grant and scholarship aid per full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate in the $48,001–$75,000 income group who received Title IV aid and paid in-state or in-district tuition. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students received throughout the full aid year.

Counts full-time women who are first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students enrolled in the most recent fall period, including students who began in the preceding summer and those admitted through early decision or early action; reported only by institutions without an open-admission policy for entering first-time undergraduates.
Typical dollar amount of required fees for a full-time, first-professional theology student who does not meet the institution’s or state’s residency requirements, for the full academic year.

Aggregate dollar amount of grant and scholarship aid from federal, state/local, or institutional sources received by full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in the $48,001–$75,000 income range who received Title IV aid and paid in-state or in-district tuition. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars reporting aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year.

Count of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students in the $0–$30,000 income category who received any Title IV federal student aid and were awarded grant or scholarship aid from the federal government, state/local government, or institution; private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions report this for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year, or for applicable nonstandard-calendar institutions over their 12-month reporting period.

Average dollar amount of federal, state or local government, and institutional grant and scholarship aid awarded per full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate paying the in-state or in-district rate and receiving any Title IV aid, across all income levels. Populated for public institutions with standard term calendars that report aid for fall-enrolled students over the full aid year.

Number of students in the specified cohort who completed a bachelor's or other award within 150% of the program's normal completion time; for four-year institutions, cohorts may be total, bachelor's, or other-than-bachelor's, while two-year and less-than-two-year institutions report students completing any award.

Average base salary in dollars for full-time, non-medical instructional staff who are women and work under 12-month contracts, as of November 1. Covers staff whose duties are instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service; excludes supplements, overloads, bonuses, and additional administrative or other stipends.

Headcount of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates living off campus and not with family who received any Title IV aid (grants, work-study, or loans), across all income levels. Reported by private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions with standard term calendars for fall-enrolled students receiving aid during the full aid year, and by public or private institutions with continuous or program-specific calendars or primarily contact-hour/occupational programs for students enrolled during the institution’s 12-month reporting period.

The 75th-percentile ACT Math score among first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students who submitted ACT scores. Reported for institutions without open admission policies where ACT scores are required and at least 60% of these enrolled students submitted scores; includes students entering in the prior summer.

Headcount of full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at all income levels who received any Title IV federal student aid (grants, work-study, or loans) during the full aid year. Populated for private not-for-profit and for-profit institutions using standard academic calendars that report a fall cohort, and for public or private institutions with clock-hour, primarily occupational, continuous, or program-specific calendars that report students enrolled over a 12-month period.

Headcount of women among full-time, non-medical instructional staff, including staff whose duties are instruction alone or instruction combined with research and/or public service, across all listed contract lengths. Medical-school staff are excluded, but staff in associated hospitals or separate health and allied-health schools are excluded only when they are not part of the medical school.
